As an early-stage product it currently exposes no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched with published company identity and link properties.

providers.name: KakaoPay
providers.description: KakaoPay is a Korean mobile payment platform and fintech service by Kakao Corp providing REST APIs for payment processing, QR code payments, online checkout, subscription billing, money transfers, and financial product management. The platform enables merchants and developers to integrate KakaoPay's payment infrastructure via secure REST APIs authenticated with admin keys or bearer tokens.

providers.name: Plooto
providers.description: Plooto is a Toronto-based payments automation company (founded 2015 by Hamed Abbasi and Serguei Kloubkov) that helps small and medium businesses and accounting firms automate domestic and international accounts payable and accounts receivable. Its cloud platform unifies bill pay, approval workflows, supplier and customer payments, reconciliation, and reporting across Canadian EFT, US ACH, credit card, and cross-border rails, syncing two-way with QuickBooks Online, Xero, and NetSuite. Plooto is a licensed money services business in its home market of Canada, working with Tier 1 banks and processing partners. Its posture is integration-led rather than API-platform-led: money movement runs on a first-party backend gateway (api.plooto.com) that powers the app and its accounting connectors, but Plooto does not publish a public, self-serve developer portal, downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or public API reference. Partner and embedded access is arranged through a gated partner onboarding process, not open developer sign-up.

providers.name: Vareto
providers.description: Vareto is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform that helps finance teams build financial models, budgets, and forecasts — including headcount and capacity planning, sales revenue forecasting, and P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow modeling — with real-time multiplayer collaboration, executive and board reporting, and data integrations spanning ERPs (NetSuite, SAP, QuickBooks, Sage Intacct), HRIS platforms (Workday, ADP, Rippling, and 25+ more), CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift), and spreadsheets. Vareto is SOC 2 Type 2 attested with a public Drata trust center, but does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: FloQast
providers.description: FloQast is an accounting transformation platform that automates the financial close, reconciliations, and record-to-report workflows while preserving audit compliance and human sign-off. Built by accountants for accountants, it offers month-end close management, AI-driven transaction matching and reconciliation, journal entry management, variance analysis, consolidation, and Connected Compliance for evidence collection, risk management, and controls testing. Its Transform line adds no-code AI agents for accounting workflows where every output is explainable and every decision logged. FloQast connects to ERPs including Workday, Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Sage Intacct, Xero, and QuickBooks, and serves 3,500+ companies. It is an early ISO 42001 adopter with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ISO 27701 certifications. FloQast does not publish a public developer API; this profile catalogs its identity, integration, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Monarch
providers.description: Monarch (Monarch Money) is a modern personal finance and money-management app that brings a household's accounts, budgets, investments, and goals into one shared view. It aggregates connected bank, card, loan, and investment accounts, automatically categorizes transactions, and lets couples, families, and financial professionals collaborate on budgeting and net-worth tracking at no extra cost. Monarch is a direct-to-consumer subscription product ($99/year) and does not publish an official public developer API — account connectivity is handled by third-party aggregators and the app is driven by a private internal GraphQL backend (api.monarch.com/graphql, authenticated). A community-maintained, unofficial Python library reverse-engineers that backend. Monarch is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company; this profile was enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Adaptive
providers.description: Adaptive is an AI-native project accounting platform for the construction industry, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The product automates the money side of running construction jobs: accounts payable and bill capture, owner and subcontractor billing, change orders, lien waivers and compliance, draws, work-in-progress (WIP) reporting, and cash-flow forecasting. Adaptive packages this as a set of purpose-built AI "clerk" and analyst agents (AP Clerk, Billing Clerk, Change Order Clerk, Compliance, Field Coordinator, Forecasting Analyst, WIP Analyst) that work alongside a project accountant, and it integrates with construction and accounting systems such as Procore and QuickBooks. Adaptive is a SaaS application rather than a public API provider; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs, but it does maintain a public product changelog, a help center, and a Vanta trust center. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources.

providers.name: Omnea
providers.description: Omnea is an AI-native procurement platform that automates the full source-to-pay (S2P) process, unifying intake management, strategic sourcing, third-party risk management, and supplier management behind autonomous agents. Buyers raise requests conversationally through Slack, Microsoft Teams, or an OAuth-protected remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, and Omnea routes intelligent workflows, price-intelligence benchmarking, continuous supplier monitoring, and automated approvals. The company is backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and exposes a documented public REST API plus a hosted MCP endpoint for agent integrations. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched from live probes of its public surfaces.

providers.name: Billtrust
providers.description: Billtrust is an AI-powered accounts receivable and B2B payments technology company that helps businesses accelerate cash flow by automating the order-to-cash cycle. Its platform spans automated invoicing and invoice delivery, B2B payment acceptance across multiple modalities, AI-driven cash application that matches payments to invoices, intelligent collections, credit decisioning, and a B2B eCommerce storefront. Billtrust connects to more than 40 ERP systems and 260+ accounts-payable portals, serving manufacturing, distribution, equipment, medical, retail, transportation, and business-services companies. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from the Bain Capital Ventures portfolio; Billtrust does not currently publish an open public developer portal or OpenAPI, so enrichment captures its identity, compliance program, and domain security posture from public surfaces.

providers.name: Archlet
providers.description: Archlet is an AI-native eSourcing, sourcing-optimization and eAuction platform, founded in 2018 in Zurich, Switzerland, that helps procurement teams run RFIs, RFPs, RFQs and reverse auctions faster and with more transparency. Its Spark AI engine automates RFx setup, auction configuration, scenario generation and bid summarization, while advanced bid analytics and scenario optimization unlock savings across strategic, tactical and tail-spend sourcing. Archlet exposes open, well-documented APIs for intake, CLM, reporting, supplier management and data-lake integrations that sync bi-directionally with ERP and P2P systems such as SAP, SAP Ariba, Coupa and Oracle. Trusted by enterprises including PepsiCo, TotalEnergies, Bosch, Walmart and FedEx, and backed by HV Capital.

providers.name: Asaas
providers.description: Asaas is a Brazilian financial-services and payments platform headquartered in Joinville, SC. It operates as a Banco Central-authorized payment institution and simplified credit company (SCD), offering small and medium businesses a digital account ("Conta Asaas") combined with collection, billing, and receivables tooling. The Asaas API (v3) at api.asaas.com is a REST/JSON surface covering Customers, Charges (Cobranças), Subscriptions, Installments, Pix (including Pix Automático recurring), Boleto, Credit Card, Checkout sessions, Payment Links, Split Payments, Transfers, Bill Payments, Anticipation of Receivables, Subaccounts / White-label, Invoices (Nota Fiscal), Escrow, Chargeback handling, Webhooks, and supporting services like Serasa default reporting, cell-phone recharges, and SMS / WhatsApp / email notifications. A full sandbox at sandbox.asaas.com, an Atlassian-hosted status page, a Discord developer community, and an llms.txt-indexed documentation site round out the developer experience. Asaas does not publish a first-party SDK on a GitHub org; the ecosystem is served by third-party community SDKs in Node.js, PHP, Python, Go, and Ruby plus e-commerce plugins for WooCommerce, Magento, and Nuvemshop.

providers.name: Finli
providers.description: Finli is a financial technology platform serving two markets. For small and medium-sized businesses it provides a full digital back office — professional invoicing and quoting, payment processing (ACH, credit card, and Apple Pay), customer relationship management, inventory tracking, and autopay. For banks and credit unions it delivers those same tools as a white-labeled offering so financial institutions can attract and deepen small-business relationships, keep deposits, and own their customer data without taking on operational risk. Finli is SOC 2 Type II certified and PCI DSS compliant, and was founded by CEO Lori Shao. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; Finli publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: AvidXchange
providers.description: AvidXchange is a fintech provider of AI-powered accounts payable (AP) and payment automation software for middle-market businesses. Its platform digitizes invoice capture, approval workflows, purchase orders, and supplier payments, integrating with more than 220 accounting and ERP systems and connecting buyers to a large supplier network for paperless, straight-through AP processing. AvidXchange publishes a partner and integration developer portal (ReadMe-hosted) for connecting ERP systems and building against its payment and invoice automation platform; the API reference is gated behind partner login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, QED Investors, and Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Miter
providers.description: Miter is a Human Capital Management (HCM) platform purpose-built for construction contractors, consolidating payroll, HR, benefits, field operations, and expense management into a single connected system. Its construction payroll automates prevailing-wage, certified-payroll, and union compliance, multi-state tax handling, and fully-burdened job-cost tracking in real time, while its HRIS covers recruiting, benefits, performance, and learning. Field Operations adds time tracking, scheduling, daily reports, production tracking, and safety, and Expense Management handles reimbursements, per diems, and corporate cards. Miter connects to construction ERPs and accounting systems (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, Procore, Viewpoint, and more) through off-the-shelf integrations or a custom REST API. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: SetSail
providers.description: SetSail is a revenue-operations and sales-AI platform (now part of ZoomInfo) that automatically captures sales activity data from email, calendar, and contacts and syncs it to Salesforce, then layers AI-powered revenue intelligence on top of it, including MEDDIC deal analysis, meeting preparation, deal alerts, and performance coaching. Insights are delivered to sales reps and leaders through Slack, email, the browser, and Salesforce, and activity data can be routed to Snowflake, Databricks, Tableau, and Looker for analytics. SetSail does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Substly
providers.description: Substly is a SaaS management platform designed for small and medium-sized businesses to track software subscriptions, optimize spend, manage user access, and detect shadow IT across cloud applications. It provides centralized oversight, automated renewal tracking, and integrations with Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID.

providers.name: Touchmark
providers.description: Touchmark is solving AI pricing - instead of AI being priced per token regardless of quality, Touchmark prices it by the quality, efficiency, and value of the output, so spend is fair, predictable, and tied to what you actually get. Applications emit the events they already produce (model outputs, tool calls, code diffs) with a base price, and Touchmark's out-of-band judge returns a quality-adjusted fair price for each event on a separate valuation stream. A Y Combinator Summer 2026 company founded by Ilia Bolgov and Roman Yanushevskyi in San Francisco; the TypeScript SDK (@touchmark/sdk) is in private beta.

providers.name: Monograph
providers.description: Monograph is firm-management software purpose-built for architecture and engineering (A&E) practices, unifying project management, resourcing and staffing, time tracking, budgeting, invoicing and client payments in one connected system. Used by thousands of US-based A&E firms, it integrates with QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, but publishes no public developer API, webhooks, or SDKs. Backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

providers.name: Coast
providers.description: Coast is a fintech company providing a unified payments platform for fleet-based and field-service businesses, combining a smart Visa fuel card, corporate card, field card, and bill pay into a single program with granular spending controls, GPS- and tank-capacity-based fraud prevention, fuel rebates, and a fraud guarantee. Coast operates a stable v2 REST API (the Coast API) behind a developer portal that lets businesses programmatically access cards, drivers, vehicles, transactions, receipts, and controls, alongside native integrations with telematics (Samsara, Geotab, Verizon Connect), accounting (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct), and fleet management (Fleetio, Whip Around) platforms. Coast is backed by Accel and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Debitura
providers.description: Debitura is an API-first international debt collection platform covering cross-border B2B and B2C receivables. It publishes three separate public REST APIs, one per role in the network rather than one API with role-gated endpoints: the Customer API for creditors uploading invoices to collection and tracking cases, the Referral Partner API for platforms embedding collection as a referral and tracking revenue share, and the Collection Partner API for collection agencies operating cases on the platform. All three are OpenAPI 3.0.4, each on its own host, and each authenticates with an API key in the XApiKey header; the Customer API additionally accepts a bearer token, and the Referral Partner API exposes OAuth operations for minting them. Webhooks appear in all three, each with a paired test surface for exercising events before going live. Debitura publishes its own APIs.json at docs.debitura.com, which is how this profile was built.

providers.name: LiqPay
providers.description: LiqPay is a Ukrainian payment platform operated by PrivatBank that provides REST APIs for accepting card payments, creating hosted payment pages, processing subscriptions, managing refunds, sending invoices, and conducting card-to-card transfers. It supports Mastercard, Visa, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Privat24 wallets across 120+ countries, with full fiscalization (RRO) support for Ukrainian merchants.

providers.name: Accordance Ai
providers.description: Accordance (operated by Agnetic Labs Inc.) is a San Francisco frontier AI platform built for tax, audit, and accounting professionals. Founded by researchers from the Stanford AI Lab, it provides a firmwide agentic AI platform that performs tax research with authoritative code, context, and citations, complex accounting analysis, and audit insight — with visible reasoning and verifiable source citations. Accordance is SOC 2 Type II certified, never trains on customer data, and is backed by Menlo Ventures, Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and New Enterprise Associates. The product surface is the Accordance application (app.accordance.ai); no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Aleph
providers.description: Aleph is an AI-native financial planning & analysis (FP&A) platform for finance teams that want live data, spreadsheet-native workflows, automated reporting, and AI-assisted analysis in one system. It consolidates data from ERP, HRIS, CRM, billing, and databases through 200+ no-code connectors, offers bi-directional Excel and Google Sheets add-ins, web dashboards, and an AI layer (Aleph Intelligence, Aleph Agent, AI Variance Analysis, AI Mappings). Aleph also ships an Aleph Agent MCP integration that brings governed financial data to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible tools. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures; SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified.

providers.name: Ctrl
providers.description: Ctrl (Ctrl, Inc., a Delaware corporation) is an AI-powered workspace for revenue and sales teams that consolidates the tools and data a rep needs — CRM, email, calendar, and messaging — into a single actionable view. Founded in 2021 by Omri Sagzan and Aviv Nahum and based in Tel Aviv and London, Ctrl automates the manual work of updating records across apps such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Slack, and helps teams codify and replicate their winning sales playbooks. The company raised a $9M seed round led by LocalGlobe and Earlybird in 2023 and was acquired by Sana Labs in October 2024. Ctrl is a UI/workspace product surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Getaleph
providers.description: Aleph (Getaleph) is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform that automates finance busywork so teams can focus on strategic work. It consolidates data from 150+ ERP, CRM, and HRIS integrations using no-code tools, syncs live data into Excel and Google Sheets, and builds interactive dashboards for stakeholders. The Aleph Agent delivers instant, auditable answers in Slack, Teams, or Aleph, and the hosted Aleph Agent MCP server plugs governed financial data directly into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible AI tools without CSV exports. Aleph is SOC 1 & 2 Type II certified and is backed by Khosla Ventures.

providers.name: Trope
providers.description: Trope is an AI-native platform that helps ERP implementation partners deliver successful implementations faster, deploying AI agents across discovery, requirements, fit-gap analysis, data migration, approval workflows, UAT scripts, training guides, documentation, and go-live readiness — built for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central consultancies and other implementation teams. Trope also maintains Trope CUA, an open-source MCP-native computer-use agent for background desktop automation on Windows and macOS. Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Tide
providers.description: Tide is a UK business finance and administration platform ("built by business owners for business owners") serving over two million small businesses, sole traders, freelancers, and limited companies. It combines a business current account (an e-money account powered by ClearBank), expense cards, invoicing and payment tools (Tap to Pay, card readers, QR codes, payment links), MTD-ready accounting and admin, business credit and finance (loans, asset finance, invoice finance), company formation, and business insurance. Tide is authorised and regulated in relation to its regulated activities by the UK Financial Conduct Authority. Tide was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis, Creandum, and Speedinvest. It does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; "Open Banking" is offered as a consumer product feature.

providers.name: Neo.Tax
providers.description: Neo.Tax is an AI-powered tax automation platform that helps enterprises and their accounting teams generate audit-ready R&D tax credit studies, software capitalization (ASC 350-40), and R&D capitalization (IRC Section 174) documentation. The platform ingests engineering and financial data from tools like Jira, GitHub, payroll systems, and Workday and uses large language models and agentic AI to qualify projects under IRC Section 41, eliminating the manual surveys and interviews that traditionally drive R&D tax credit work. Neo.Tax is backed by GV and Uncork Capital and delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS product; it operates a customer application, a help center, a public status page, and a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR) but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: EarnUp
providers.description: EarnUp is a San Francisco-based financial-wellness fintech that automates consumer debt paydown and savings. Using patented technology and predictive analytics, its platform lets people schedule and automatically make payments toward mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and other personal debt, and save for life events. EarnUp sells engagement and AI-advisor tooling to lenders, mortgage servicers, credit unions, employers, unions, and financial professionals, and reports that more than three million people have used the platform. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; EarnUp publishes no public developer API, so enrichment is limited to identity and security posture.

providers.name: EIS Group
providers.description: EIS Group (EIS Ltd) is a United States core-systems vendor for insurance, founded in 2008 out of Exigen Insurance Solutions and headquartered in San Francisco, California. EIS sells the EIS Platform and EIS OneSuite — a cloud-native, microservices core suite covering customer management, policy administration, billing, and claims — across group benefits, property and casualty / general, protection, life and annuities, and pet insurance. EIS markets itself as API-first and claims thousands of open REST APIs (1,100 digital APIs announced in 2019, 9,000+ claimed for OneSuite) fronted by the EIS DXP API middleware, but none of that surface is public. There is no self-serve developer portal on eisgroup.com; the documentation host docs.eisgroup.com answers HTTP 401 behind an HTTP Basic realm named "EIS Group Users", so the entire API reference is a customer/partner login wall. No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or public Postman collection could be retrieved. The only public code EIS ships is two open-source GitHub repositories (kraken-rules, ui-render), which are libraries rather than APIs. ACORD is attested only indirectly — an analyst evaluation hosted on eisgroup.com states the system integrates using "web services, APIs, RESTful APIs, ACORD and certified ACORD" — with no ACORD artifacts, AL3 mappings, or IVANS/agency-download detail published. What EIS does publish is a substantial certification posture — a certified MACH Alliance membership (Microservices, API-first, Cloud-native SaaS, Headless) and a full ISO stack covering 27001, 27701, 22301, 27017, 27018, 27035-1, 12207, 15288, 25000 and ISO/IEC 42001, which EIS announced in June 2025 as the first cloud-native insurance core platform provider to obtain. One first-party package is public, eis-ui-render on npm. This is the canonical United States core-systems posture — the APIs exist and are sold, but they are reachable only through a licensed implementation.

providers.name: PeopleSoft Financials
providers.description: API collection for Oracle PeopleSoft Financials suite covering General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Asset Management, and other financial modules.

providers.name: FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification)
providers.description: FOCUS, the FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification, is an open standard maintained under the FinOps Foundation that normalizes cost and usage data across cloud, SaaS, data center, and other technology vendors. FOCUS defines a common data schema, a controlled vocabulary of column names, allowed values, and pricing attributes so that practitioners can apply a consistent set of FinOps practices regardless of which provider generated the underlying billing dataset. FOCUS is purely a data specification rather than a REST API; conforming providers expose exports of their billing data in the FOCUS format, and tooling consumes those exports against the published column library, data model, and validator.

providers.name: Huice
providers.description: Huice (慧策) is a Chinese enterprise software company whose flagship product, Wangdiantong (旺店通) ERP, is a tailor-made e-commerce management system for merchants operating across multiple online channels. It provides order management, warehouse and inventory management (WMS), goods and product-archive management, procurement, after-sales/returns processing, and financial operations (慧经营). Huice runs a public Open Platform (open.wangdian.cn) exposing an HTTP API (openapi2) for third-party integrators to synchronize shops, goods, orders, stock, purchasing, and logistics. The API uses a sid + appkey + timestamp + MD5 signature (sign) authentication scheme, page_no/page_size pagination, and a code/message response envelope, with separate sandbox and production hosts.

providers.name: Invoice2go
providers.description: Invoice2go (part of BILL) is a mobile-first invoicing and small-business management platform for freelancers, contractors, and self-employed professionals. It lets users create and send professional invoices and estimates, accept online payments via bank transfer, credit and debit card, and PayPal, track expenses and billable time, capture customer reviews, and view business reports across web, iOS, and Android. Serving roughly 225,000 small-business users, Invoice2go focuses on getting paid faster and simplifying back-office admin. It was acquired by BILL in 2021. There is no live public developer API; third-party integrations are delivered through an Apideck-powered integrations marketplace (QuickBooks, Xero, MYOB, HubSpot, Shopify, Zapier, and more).

providers.name: LiveFlow
providers.description: LiveFlow is an agentic accounting and FP&A platform that connects accounting systems such as QuickBooks and Xero to real-time financial reporting, consolidation, and forecasting. Its Flow product automates month-end close, reconciliation, accounts-receivable management, and journal entries across multiple entities, while LiveFlow FP&A automates consolidation, reporting, and forecasting on a company's existing systems. The platform targets complex, multi-location businesses in construction, healthcare, food & beverage, and retail. LiveFlow is backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Jeeves
providers.description: Jeeves is a global financial platform for cross-border businesses, combining corporate cards (physical and virtual with spend controls and cashback), automated expense management with approval flows and policy enforcement, cross-border payments and transfers to 150+ countries in 40+ currencies, instant and stablecoin-based settlement, non-dilutive corporate credit, and AI-driven spend insights. Jeeves operates across Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Canada, the USA, the UK, and the European Union, serving globally operating companies. Backed by a16z and CRV, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Marlo Technologies
providers.description: Marlo is a maritime ERP platform for dry bulk, tanker, and commercial shipping companies, unifying chartering, voyage management, finance, banking, and compliance in a single system. Operators use Marlo to plan charters, track voyage operations and cargo, model voyage P&L and cashflow, run valuations and credit scoring, manage loans and covenants, hold multi-currency accounts with FX transfers and corporate cards, and handle sanctions screening, emissions tracking, and CII rating management. Marlo is a Techstars-backed company and holds SOC 2 (AICPA) certification. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass the company exposes a customer web application (app.marlo.co) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Simplifi by Quicken
providers.description: Simplifi by Quicken is a personal finance management application that aggregates financial accounts from over 14,000 institutions, enabling users to track spending, manage budgets, monitor investments, set savings goals, and access projected cash flow analytics. The platform uses OAuth-based API connections to banks and purpose-built APIs to billers to pull data into a unified financial dashboard available on web and mobile.

providers.name: Vertice
providers.description: Vertice is an intelligent procurement platform built for the modern enterprise with agentic workflows, AI insights, and expert buyers that empower finance and procurement teams across 30+ countries to buy smarter and scale faster. The platform covers SaaS purchasing and contract management, cloud spend optimization (AWS, GCP, Azure), and integrates with ERPs, CLMs, ticketing platforms, communication tools, TPRM systems, and SSOs to centralize procurement workflows. Vertice processes over $30B in spend with proven 20%+ savings for customers including ARM, Blackberry, Factorial, and Santander.

providers.name: Juni
providers.description: Juni is a Swedish fintech (headquartered in Göteborg, founded 2020) that provides a financial platform for ecommerce and digital businesses: business banking with multi-currency accounts, corporate and virtual cards, local and global payments, spend management, working-capital financing, and AI-driven accounting with integrations such as Fortnox. Juni is a licensed payment institution under the oversight of the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (SFSA) and is backed by EQT Ventures. It exposes a regulatory PSD2 / Open Banking (ASPSP) API surface for third-party providers, but publishes no public product API, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Hearth
providers.description: Hearth is a business-management platform for residential home-improvement contractors and trades professionals. It bundles customer financing (a marketplace of 18+ lenders with $0 dealer fees), quotes and estimates, digital contracts and e-signature, invoicing and payments, client management, and scheduling, together with Harper, a 24/7 AI receptionist that answers calls, handles follow-ups, and creates social content. Hearth serves 16+ residential contracting verticals including roofing, HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, fencing, and flooring, and is backed by 8vc.

providers.name: Inscope
providers.description: Inscope is an AI-powered financial reporting and automation platform for accounting firms and enterprise finance teams. It drafts accurate, GAAP-compliant financial statements, cash flow statements, and audit workpapers in minutes, keeping a human reviewer in the loop to review and sign off. The platform targets the financial close, reporting, and audit workflow, and states SOC 2 Type I and Type II certification with GDPR/CCPA compliance. Inscope is a private SaaS backed by Norwest Venture Partners; it publishes no public product API or developer portal today. Customer sign-in runs on a PropelAuth-hosted OpenID Connect tenant at auth.inscopehq.com.

providers.name: Von
providers.description: Von (vonlabs.ai) is an AI RevOps agent from Rattle Software, the Insight Partners and Sequoia backed team behind gorattle.com, positioned as an AI data scientist for revenue teams. Von connects to CRMs, data warehouses, call recorders, and sales engagement tools - Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Gong, Outreach, Salesloft, and more, plus 100+ integrations consumed via MCP - to automate pipeline forecasting, win/loss analysis, churn detection, sales coaching, and Salesforce administration. Von publishes no public API or developer program; its security posture is documented at trust.vonlabs.ai (SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, CASA Tier 2).

providers.name: Waterlily
providers.description: Waterlily is an AI-native, end-to-end long-term care (LTC) planning platform for financial advisors, insurance professionals, and the families they serve. Trained on more than 500 million data points, its models predict an individual's personalized likelihood of needing long-term care, project the cost and duration of that care, and estimate the caregiving hours each family member is likely to contribute. A roughly three-minute intake produces a personalized care timeline and plan with localized cost estimates, and its Quote-and-Apply engine computes mathematically optimal LTC insurance policy configurations across hundreds of thousands of options. Founded by Lily Vittayarukskul and backed by Insight Partners. Waterlily is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company; it exposes no public developer API today (integrations are one-click CRM imports for Salesforce, Wealthbox, and Redtail).

providers.name: Finrep
providers.description: Finrep is an AI-powered financial reporting intelligence platform for the office of the CFO. It helps SEC reporting, technical accounting, legal counsel, investor relations, disclosure committee, internal audit, tax, and ESG teams research, benchmark, validate, and draft SEC disclosures grounded in EDGAR filings, authoritative accounting guidance (ASC/IFRS), and IR materials — with every answer traceable to inspectable source documents. Finrep ships 40+ purpose-built CFO-office workflows spanning comment-letter analysis, disclosure drafting, Section 16 filing, and peer benchmarking, and can deploy on-premises or in a private cloud. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: AppFolio
providers.description: AppFolio is a Santa Barbara, California cloud-based real estate technology company providing property management software to residential, commercial, community association (HOA), student housing, single-family, and affordable housing operators, plus investment management tooling for sponsors and funds. Its flagship AppFolio Performance Platform unifies workflow automation, accounting and reporting, marketing and leasing, maintenance, resident communication, and resident services on a single multi-tenant SaaS. AppFolio embeds Realm-X, an in-house agentic AI layer (Realm-X Assistant, Performers, Flows) directly into the platform rather than as an add-on. Integrations are delivered through the AppFolio Stack marketplace, where certified partners (ButterflyMX, Conservice, HappyCo, Knock, Lowe's, Property Meld, and many more) connect via the AppFolio Stack API. The Stack API is gated behind a partner application, security-compliance questionnaire, and terms-of-service signing; OAuth 2.0, a sandbox environment, webhooks, and an OpenAPI/Swagger reference are made available only to approved partners through the developer.appfolio.com portal, so no public specification is reachable for catalog inclusion. AppFolio's revenue model is per-unit SaaS subscription plus value-added services (payments, screening, insurance, marketing). The AppFolio GitHub organization publishes internal Ruby on Rails, React, and tooling libraries (react-gears, ae_page_objects, store_base_sti_class) but no public API SDK, CLI, or OpenAPI artifact.

providers.name: Back Office
providers.description: Back Office, Inc. operates Finally (finally.com), a Miami-based fintech that provides a unified, AI-powered bookkeeping, accounting, and finance suite for growing small and medium-sized businesses. The platform combines automated bookkeeping and ledger management, accounts payable and bill pay, expense management, corporate cards with built-in controls, invoicing, payment processing, payroll across 150+ countries, and credit monitoring, with AI agents that classify transactions, reconcile accounts, close the books, and prepare audits. Founded in 2018 and trusted by over 3,500 companies, Finally publishes a SOC 2 trust center but does not currently expose a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity, web properties, and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Brex
providers.description: Brex is the first fully unified spend platform with global corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, travel, and bill pay. Brex makes it easy for finance teams to control all of their spend, all in one place. Using the Brex API, you can power your internal tools and create custom workflows.

providers.name: Concourse
providers.description: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Its platform lets finance, accounting, and data teams query financial data in natural language, generate board and investor reporting with commentary, and run forecasts and scenarios against real-time data. Concourse connects natively to financial and operational systems including QuickBooks, NetSuite, Ramp, Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Brex, Rippling, Gusto, BigQuery, and Databricks, and says it cuts manual finance work by over 75%. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by CRV, raising a $12M Series A alongside general availability. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Orolabs
providers.description: ORO Labs provides an agentic procurement orchestration platform for enterprise spend management. It coordinates people, processes, systems, and data so employees can get what they need without friction, unifying intake management, supplier onboarding and lifecycle, risk and compliance orchestration, and AI-driven workflow automation. The platform offers a no-code workflow builder, a purpose-built agent builder for custom procurement AI agents, and bring-your-own-LLM flexibility, with secure, semantically rich integrations across the procuretech landscape. ORO Labs is backed by Felicis and Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Papaya Pay
providers.description: Papaya Payments is a Los Angeles based fintech that operates a mobile-first digital billing and bill-pay platform. Businesses in healthcare, government and municipalities, utilities, insurance, field services, and debt collection use Papaya to let their customers pay bills by photographing a paper statement or scanning a QR code and paying over SMS, email, or the Papaya iOS and Android apps, with no account or login required. Papaya advertises a Quickpay embeddable payment widget for paper-statement and portal integrations, and states that more than 2.5 million Americans have used the service. The company markets PCI, HIPAA, and SOC2 compliance. As of this profile Papaya publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API specification; it is a consumer-facing payments product rather than a developer platform. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Buildium
providers.description: Buildium, part of RealPage, is a cloud property-management platform aimed at small and mid-sized residential, association, and community-association property managers. The platform covers accounting, leasing, applicant and tenant management, rent collection, maintenance, communications, owner and resident portals, and association management. Buildium publishes a Public API used by certified partners and customers for property, lease, tenant, owner, vendor, rental application, financial, and webhook integration with the Buildium platform.

providers.name: Fullseam
providers.description: FullSeam builds AI agents for corporate accounting and finance operations teams, automating the manual work that happens outside traditional accounting software. Its agents handle accounts receivable (following up on payments, generating requested documentation, and entering invoices into customer AP portals), accounts payable (extracting invoices from multiple sources, matching them against purchase orders and contracts, chasing vendors for missing information, and categorizing expenses before posting to the general ledger), cash application, and reconciliation. FullSeam integrates with existing systems including QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage, Bill, Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, and PandaDoc rather than requiring a platform migration, flagging exceptions with full context for human review and maintaining audit logs for compliance. Founded by the team behind TaxProper (acquired by Opendoor), FullSeam is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company.

providers.name: Origin Financial
providers.description: Origin (Blend Financial Inc. DBA Origin Financial) is a personal finance platform built around an SEC-regulated AI financial advisor, combining spending tracking, budgeting, investing, tax filing, estate planning, and couples money management in one app, and offering employers a financial wellness benefit. Account connections run through partners including Plaid, MX, and Mastercard. Origin is a consumer and employer product with no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: TigerBeetle
providers.description: TigerBeetle is an open-source (Apache 2.0) distributed financial accounting and transactions database, purpose-built for high-throughput, mission-critical double-entry bookkeeping and online transaction processing (OLTP). It is NOT an HTTP/REST API and ships no OpenAPI - the database is accessed over a custom binary wire protocol on TCP (default port 3000) via official client libraries for .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Rust. The "API" is the set of client operations - create_accounts, create_transfers, lookup_accounts, lookup_transfers, get_account_transfers, get_account_balances, query_accounts, and query_transfers - that use fixed-size, cache-line-aligned structs for zero-deserialization performance. TigerBeetle is self-hostable; a fully managed service is also offered to select enterprise partners via sales@tigerbeetle.com.

providers.name: Zone & Company
providers.description: Zone & Co (Zone & Company) is a NetSuite-native financial operations software vendor whose SuiteApp suite automates the back office across five product families - Quote to Cash (ZoneBilling billing and revenue recognition, ZonePayments Stripe integration), Procure to Pay (ZoneProcure, ZoneCapture, ZoneApprovals), Treasury (ZoneLiquidity cash forecasting, ZoneReconcile), Payroll Management (ZonePayroll, Employee Portal), and Record to Report (ZoneReporting on Power BI, Data Warehouse, ZoneExtract, Solution 7). The products are delivered as native Oracle NetSuite SuiteApps distributed through the SuiteApp Marketplace rather than as a standalone public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Maxima
providers.description: Maxima is an AI-native accounting and financial-close automation platform for enterprise finance teams. Its AI agents automate the core work of the accounting close — journal entries, cash coding, payroll entries, bank and balance-sheet reconciliations, flux (variance) analysis, and fixed-asset depreciation — while connecting natively to the systems finance teams already use (the company advertises 150+ integrations across ERPs, banks, and payroll providers). Maxima is an early-stage, enterprise-focused company backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this pass the company runs a corporate marketing site and a gated web application (app.maximahq.com) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Metric
providers.description: Metric is an AI-powered financial intelligence and accounting platform built for business owners, founders, and CEOs. It replaces spreadsheets and expensive CFO teams with a real-time financial dashboard and Max, an AI co-pilot (CF-AI) that answers financial questions such as runway, hiring capacity, and spending in plain language, drawn from live financial data. Metric handles accounting and bookkeeping, payables and receivables, invoicing, eight report types, and UAE VAT compliance, and connects to QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Xero, and Shopify. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi with offices in Rawalpindi, Singapore, and Riyadh, it is backed by 500 Global and serves businesses across 190+ countries. Metric is a SaaS web application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Pointone
providers.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: InvestCloud
providers.description: InvestCloud is a wealth-management technology company that provides an AI-driven digital wealth platform connecting advisors, financial institutions, asset managers, TAMPs, RIAs and investors across the full investment lifecycle. Its product surface spans front-office advisor and client solutions, a wealth data platform ("Digital Warehouse") that aggregates custodial, market and portfolio data, managed account solutions including the Advisor Programs List (APL) and Private Markets Account, post-trade processing and settlement, revenue management, and the NaviPlan and RetireUp financial planning products acquired with Advicent. InvestCloud markets a developer platform — branded "Wealthsqope Digital Developer" — offering web-service APIs, embeddable widgets, code recipes, client libraries and application API keys, but that platform and its reference documentation sit entirely behind a portal login, and no machine-readable API contract is published publicly.

providers.name: Ava
providers.description: Ava is a consumer financial-technology company that helps people build credit and reduce the cost of debt. Its products include the Ava Credit Builder Mastercard (a no-interest card usable at approved subscription merchants), a Save & Build secured savings loan, and rent and utility payment reporting to the three major U.S. credit bureaus (TransUnion, Equifax, Experian). Ava operates as a mobile app on a subscription model and partners with regulated banks and lenders (including Patriot Bank, N.A. and Pier Lending) to deliver its products. This profile was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Ava is a consumer app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Fifteenth
providers.description: Fifteenth is a San Francisco-based fintech company operating an AI-powered personal tax platform for ambitious earners — founders, investors, executives, and technology professionals with complex financial situations such as equity compensation (ISOs, RSOs, RSUs, NSOs), liquidity events (IPOs and acquisitions), partnership income (K-1s), and active stock and crypto trading. The service pairs dedicated human CPAs with AI-driven automation: users link their banking, payroll, and investment accounts via one-click integrations (Workday, Rippling, Robinhood, Wealthfront, Carta, Charles Schwab, AngelList, Coinbase and more), and the platform automatically detects tax-relevant transactions, organizes documents, models scenarios, and delivers proactive quarterly planning plus unlimited year-round advice at flat-fee pricing starting around $1,000 per year. Fifteenth raised $8.25M in seed funding (February 2025) led by A* and General Catalyst. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: GetGoing
providers.description: GetGoing is a cloud-based corporate travel and expense (T&E) management platform for small and midsize businesses, built and operated by BCD Travel. It combines self-service booking of flights, hotels, rental cars and rail with automated travel and expense policy enforcement, pre-trip approval flows, streamlined payments and invoicing, traveler safety and duty-of-care, and analytics dashboards in a single product that can be implemented in under two hours. GetGoing pairs the digital self-service experience with BCD Travel's global travel-management expertise and support, and is offered across the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium. GetGoing does not publish a first-party public developer API; programmatic travel integration is provided by the separate, authorization-gated BCD Travel Developer Hub.

providers.name: OEN
providers.description: Oen (應援科技) is a Taiwan-based fintech company operating an integrated payments and CRM cloud platform. It provides multi-channel payment processing (credit cards, convenience-store payments, bank transfers, and subscriptions), electronic invoicing, and a supporter-relationship CRM covering event and ticketing management, member and volunteer management, merchandise/reward redemption, and email/SMS communications. The platform serves nonprofits, political organizations, educational institutions, entertainment events, and commercial merchants, with more than 600 organizations and individuals using Oen. The company runs an API Gateway and mobile-payment surface, a public responsible-disclosure and bug-bounty program, and displays PCI DSS Level 1, ISO 27001, and ISO 27701 trust badges.

providers.name: Rho
providers.description: Rho is an all-in-one finance platform for businesses that combines business banking, treasury, corporate cards, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, and automated month-end close. Customers get a business checking account with high FDIC sweep insurance, a yield-bearing treasury product, corporate cards with cash back, and zero-fee bill pay, all reconciled against connected accounting systems. Rho serves startups, small businesses, enterprises, accountants, banks, and consumer brands, with no per-seat fees. The platform exposes APIs for use cases such as vendor onboarding and virtual card issuance so partners can embed Rho capabilities into their own portals. Native integrations exist for QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

providers.name: Satago
providers.description: Satago is a UK financial-technology platform offering a three-in-one cash flow management solution for small and medium-sized businesses: Risk Insights (real-time credit checks, risk bands, and suggested credit limits), Credit Control (automated invoice chasing with customizable email and SMS reminder sequences, statements, and late-fee handling), and Invoice Finance (fast, flexible funding with advance rates up to 90% on single or multiple invoices, offered as both selective and full facilities). The platform synchronizes with 300+ accounting packages including Sage, Xero, QuickBooks, KashFlow, and FreeAgent to keep debtor data current. Satago sells to businesses directly and through partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API, consuming the accounting platforms' APIs rather than exposing its own.

providers.name: Settle
providers.description: Settle is a financial operations platform built for consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and ecommerce companies, unifying procurement, accounts payable automation, and working capital financing in one back office. Teams create and manage purchase orders, track goods received and true landed costs, collect and approve bills, pay vendors with real-time visibility, and access flexible inventory and growth financing ($20K-$15M) underwritten from payables and purchasing data. Founded in 2019 and backed by Ribbit Capital, Kleiner Perkins, and Founders Fund, Settle has funded more than $3 billion to brands. A developer API covering bill pay, payments, and landed-cost data is in early access via a public waitlist.

providers.name: Bippit
providers.description: Bippit is a UK-based financial wellbeing platform that gives every employee access to personal, qualified financial coaching alongside AI-powered guidance available 24/7, planning and budgeting tools, payroll savings, and educational content and webinars. Sold to employers as a workplace benefit, it also provides organisations with aggregate financial-wellbeing insights and analytics. Bippit is FCA-regulated (No. 845814), ICO-registered (No. ZA533579), ISO 27001:2022 certified, and GDPR / UK DPA 2018 compliant, with data stored in the EEA. Backed by Techstars. Bippit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and compliance surface.

providers.name: Briefcase
providers.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: HubSync
providers.description: HubSync is an AI-powered, end-to-end tax and accounting workflow platform built for CPA firms, founded in 2019 by John McGowan and headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee. The SaaS platform unifies the engagement lifecycle in one interface: engagement letter generation and tracking, tax organizers and prepared-by-client data collection, document management, e-signature (including IRS Form 8879), batch federal and state extensions, tax return breakup and delivery, e-file status tracking, web-based tax workpapers, firm analytics dashboards, and integrated bill-and-pay. Its HubSync Halo layer adds agentic AI orchestration across those stages. HubSync publishes an llms.txt and states that it ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and bi-directional API integrations with CCH Axcess/ProSystem fx, Thomson Reuters GoSystem/UltraTax and SurePrep, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI description or endpoint documentation — the entire integration surface is provisioned per customer firm.

providers.name: Leapfin
providers.description: Leapfin is an AI-powered financial data platform for record-to-report and automated revenue recognition. It ingests transactional data from billing systems, payment processors, and data warehouses, standardizes it into a unified Financial Records schema, applies templated GAAP, SOX, IFRS, and ASC 606 revenue rules, and produces audit-ready journal entries and revenue reports that post to ERPs such as NetSuite. Programmatic data ingestion is available through the Leap Connect API (released March 2024); the platform also offers Luca, a native AI agent for exploring and reporting on revenue data. Leapfin is enterprise SaaS - the developer reference is on a partner/login-gated documentation portal, so the API surface below is modeled from Leapfin's public product and help-center material rather than fully reproduced endpoint-by-endpoint.

providers.name: BossTax
providers.description: BossTax is a mobile bookkeeping and tax-filing app for 1099 workers, freelancers, and independent contractors. Founded in 2022 and based in Stamford, Connecticut, BossTax lets self-employed users track expenses by photographing receipts, automatically categorize deductions, log expenses hands-free by voice, manage separate business banking, and file federal, state, and local taxes with a licensed tax professional for a single flat fee with no subscriptions. BossTax is an IRS-authorized Electronic Return Originator (ERO) and is backed by Bloomberg Beta and Boyd Street Ventures. The company ships iOS and Android consumer apps; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time, so this profile tracks the company identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Collective
providers.description: Collective is an all-in-one financial back-office platform built for self-employed entrepreneurs, solopreneurs, and businesses-of-one. It bundles S Corp formation and election, bookkeeping, payroll (as a Gusto partner), business and personal tax preparation and filing, quarterly tax planning, and a dedicated accounting team into a single membership. Roughly 12,000 members use Collective to optimize self-employment taxes, with members reporting average annual business-tax savings around $10,000. Collective is a private fintech company backed by General Catalyst, Kindred Ventures, and QED Investors. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web, security, and compliance footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cryptio
providers.description: Cryptio is an enterprise-grade crypto accounting, reporting, and audit platform that provides an institutional system of record for digital assets. It ingests and normalizes transaction data across 150+ blockchains, exchanges, custodians, and DeFi protocols, then automates sub-ledger accounting, cost-basis and gain/loss calculation, reconciliation, tokenization compliance, and loan management. Cryptio syncs into traditional ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Dynamics 365, Oracle Fusion, SAP, Sage) and is used by 400+ institutions including exchanges, banks, asset managers, and DeFi enterprises to produce audit-ready financial reporting for digital assets.

providers.name: Oze
providers.description: Oze is an African fintech platform on a mission to help small businesses grow, with a stated vision of building 100 million profitable businesses. Operating across Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, and Madagascar, Oze offers a Business App for bookkeeping, invoicing, inventory management, and online sales; no-collateral SME loans; and lending-management software that banks and microfinance institutions use to issue loans to small businesses. The company reports serving over 300,000 businesses. Oze is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. At the time of this enrichment pass Oze publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: PayPro Global
providers.description: PayPro Global is an all-in-one Merchant of Record platform that lets SaaS, software, video game, and AI tool companies sell globally. The platform handles international payments, subscription billing, tax compliance, fraud prevention, and revenue recovery, and exposes APIs and webhooks for managing subscriptions, payments, and customer data.

providers.name: Pilot
providers.description: Pilot provides bookkeeping, tax, and CFO services for startups and small businesses, pairing purpose-built financial software with a team of finance experts and former operators. Its offerings include monthly bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation and filing, R&D tax credit studies, fractional CFO and COO support, and stock administration. Pilot serves venture-backed startups and growing SMBs, integrating with accounting and payroll tools to deliver accurate books and financial reporting. Pilot is backed by CRV, Foundry Group, Index Ventures, SV Angel, Techstars, and Union Square Ventures. As of this profile Pilot does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its product is delivered as a managed service through its web application.

providers.name: Whatifi
providers.description: Whatifi is a visual financial modeling and scenario planning platform for small and medium businesses, letting founders, fractional CFOs, VFX and gaming studios, and startups model, forecast, and share runway, staffing, capacity, and profit scenarios without spreadsheets or formulas. The product uses an event-based canvas of 30+ pre-built business logic "Events" to build and compare "what if" forecasts in real time, and connects to accounting and banking data through integrations with Excel, Google Sheets, Xero, QuickBooks, Plaid, Railz, and OpenAI. Whatifi is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass Whatifi publishes a marketing site, a Notion-hosted help center, and a web application, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Romit
providers.description: Romit was a bank-agnostic digital wallet and payment-gateway platform for the card-not-present merchant-acquiring industry, built by a team of ex-Robocoin (bitcoin ATM) founders and backed by the 500 Global (500 Startups) accelerator. The Romit Merchant Suite let merchants stop chargebacks, reduce fraud and resolve disputes, while its consumer wallet let customers securely store payment methods, view transactions and communicate with merchants. Its OAuth2 REST API (api.romit.io/v1) exposed Banking (cards + linked bank accounts), Identity/KYC, Transfer (authorize/capture/refund/void money movement), Subscription, Plan and Invoice resources. Romit (romit.io) has since ceased operations; this profile captures the API surface derived from the surviving public evidence.

providers.name: Ameriprise Financial
providers.description: Get financial planning advice and retirement investment advice from Ameriprise financial advisors at ameriprise.com. Ameriprise Financial is a diversified financial services company offering comprehensive financial planning, wealth management, retirement planning, investment management, insurance, and annuities through a nationwide network of financial advisors.

providers.name: Xelix
providers.description: Xelix is a London-based company (with a US office in Wilmington, DE) providing an AI-powered Accounts Payable control platform that bolts onto existing ERP, P2P, and email systems. Its five modules — Transactions (duplicate/incorrect payment and fraud prevention), Statements (supplier statement reconciliation), Helpdesk (generative-AI vendor query resolution), Vendors (master vendor data cleansing), and Reports — process 115M+ invoices annually for 200+ global customers. Backed by Insight Partners ($160M raised July 2025 to advance agentic AI in AP). Xelix is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certified, GDPR compliant, hosted on AWS (EU/US/UK data residency), and publishes a Vanta trust center and an UptimeRobot status page. Integration is file-based (daily SFTP transfer of invoice, workflow, and master vendor data) plus optional SSO and email integrations; the company publishes no public developer portal or documented API surface, though its platform runs on api.xelix.com and its engineering team maintains open-source Python/Rust packages on GitHub (xelixdev).

providers.name: Credit Sesame
providers.description: Credit Sesame is a consumer financial health platform that provides free daily credit-score monitoring, credit reports, and personalized recommendations for credit cards, loans, and insurance based on a member's approval likelihood. Members can build credit through everyday debit purchases and upgrade to the Sesame+ premium tier for three-bureau credit reports, advanced credit tools, and identity-theft protection. Credit Sesame operates consumer web and mobile applications and, as of this profile, does not publish a public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile backed by Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Finaloop
providers.description: Finaloop is a real-time, ecommerce-native bookkeeping and accounting platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC) and multichannel brands. It replaces QuickBooks/Xero, human bookkeepers, and integration tooling with automation plus a team of ecommerce accounting experts, delivering always-current financials. Finaloop continuously syncs sales, returns, fees, reimbursements, inventory movements, COGS, and banking across 60+ ecommerce, marketplace, payment, banking, lending, and 3PL integrations (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, PayPal, Stripe, Chase, ShipBob, and more) to produce real-time P&L, balance sheet, and cash-flow statements, inventory analytics, and tax services. Finaloop exposes no public developer API; its APIs are internal connectors to source platforms, so this profile is identity- and posture-focused rather than spec-bearing.

providers.name: Graneet
providers.description: Graneet is a French vertical-SaaS ERP for the construction and public-works (BTP) sector, built for small and mid-sized contractors (roughly EUR 2M to 100M in revenue) to protect project profitability from the office to the job site. It unifies cost estimating and quotations, progress (situation) invoicing, purchase and supplier-invoice management, project planning and labor tracking, cash and bank reconciliation, and real-time margin dashboards, with a companion mobile app and prebuilt integrations to accounting tools such as Sage 100 and Pennylane. The product is delivered as a cloud application (app.graneet.com) backed by internal Main, BFF, and Quotation APIs; there is no public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Hanover Park
providers.description: Hanover Park is an AI-native ERP and fund administration platform for private market investors, unifying fund accounting, portfolio intelligence, and the LP experience in a single system of record. It pairs a proprietary general ledger, waterfall engine, investor portal, and portfolio management layer with AI agents that read email, propose journal entries, and extract portfolio updates, all reviewed by expert fund accountants. The platform automates capital calls, cash reconciliation, general-ledger posting, KPI collection, and reporting for venture capital, private equity, and other private-market firms. Founded in 2024 and headquartered around a modern back-office thesis, Hanover Park raised a $27M Series A led by Emergence Capital (with Lux Capital and Susa Ventures) and has grown from $1B to $15B in assets under administration. The company is SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified with a zero-trust, client-isolated AI architecture. No public API or developer program is published at this time; the product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application.

providers.name: Xpedeon
providers.description: Xpedeon is a construction-specific ERP platform from Algorithms Software Pvt Ltd (30+ years in construction software), serving general contractors, specialist contractors, housebuilders and developers, engineer-to-order manufacturers, and off-site manufacturers across the UK, India, the GCC, and the US. The cloud platform covers construction finance and accounting, job costing and CVR, contract and subcontractor management, procurement, inventory and supply chain, plant and equipment, warehouse management, HR and payroll, CRM, and a mobile app for site teams, and is ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and SOC 2 certified. Xpedeon publishes no public API, developer portal, or integration documentation, but does publish an llms.txt. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: ProfitWell
providers.description: ProfitWell (now ProfitWell Metrics by Paddle, following Paddle's 2022 acquisition of ProfitWell) is a free subscription analytics product that delivers accurate, real-time SaaS metrics such as MRR, churn, ARPU, LTV, retention, and cohort analysis by connecting directly to billing systems like Stripe, Braintree, Chargebee, Recurly, and Paddle. The ProfitWell API at https://api.profitwell.com/v2 provides programmatic access to subscription lifecycle events, customer data, financial metrics, and engagement data, authenticated via a bare API key passed in the Authorization header (no Bearer prefix).

providers.name: Blockskye
providers.description: Blockskye is an enterprise travel management and payments platform for large corporate travel programs, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York. It combines a consumer-grade online booking tool sourced through direct supplier and NDC connectivity, BMAX direct settlement that wires a customer's ERP straight to travel suppliers so booked travel bypasses corporate cards and expense reports, B360 for capturing personal co-brand card loyalty on business trips while holding policy compliance, and real-time reporting across every booking channel, with transactions recorded to a tamper-resistant distributed ledger. Blockskye delivers an end-to-end corporate travel solution in partnership with KAYAK for Business. The platform is sold and operated as an enterprise service: the booking, servicing and settlement application runs at horizon.blockskye.com behind a customer login and the knowledge base sits behind a Freshworks OAuth login. Blockskye operates a live production API host at api.blockskye.com but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Getbasis
providers.description: Basis (getbasis.ai) is an AI-powered accounting platform that builds autonomous agents purpose-built for accountants. Its agents execute accounting workflows end-to-end across tax, audit, advisory, and client accounting services (CAS), shifting accounting professionals from doing the work to reviewing it. The company emphasizes enterprise-grade security and compliance for accounting firms — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001 certifications, AES-256 encryption, strict tenant isolation, and US-only hosting. Basis is backed by Khosla Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. It is a product company with no public developer API, SDK, or API reference at this time.

providers.name: Meisterwerk
providers.description: Meisterwerk is a modular all-in-one SaaS platform for German-speaking (DACH) trades and craft businesses (Handwerk), built by MEISTERWERK APP GmbH in Berlin. It gives small and medium craft firms (1-50 employees) a single operating system for job and resource scheduling (Einsatzplanung), a native mobile app for iOS, Android and Windows, chronological job documentation with photos and chat, quoting and invoicing with e-invoice support, EU-compliant mobile time tracking with GPS, digital forms and signatures, absence/holiday planning, and configurable workflows. AI features (planning assistant, speech-to-text documentation and time entry, and the standalone "Frag Maxi" phone assistant) are built in. It integrates with lexoffice, sevdesk, bexio and orgaMAX accounting software; a public open interface (Offene Schnittstelle) is announced but not yet publicly documented. Over 8,000 active users; data is hosted on servers in Germany and the platform is GDPR (DSGVO) compliant.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: Jify
providers.description: Jify is an India-based financial wellness platform (part of the Moneyview group) that partners with employers to give employees earned wage access: its On-Demand Salary lets workers draw already-earned pay before payday. Beyond earned wage access it offers salary advances, a rewards and discount marketplace, micro-savings, digital gold investing, credit-score tracking, smart tax tools, and a money manager for budgeting and expense tracking, delivered through Android and iOS apps. Jify is a consumer / B2B2C fintech app and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance claims (ISO 27001, CISA-certified, independently tested by Appknox).

providers.name: SAP America
providers.description: SAP America, Inc. is the US subsidiary of SAP SE, headquartered in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and serving as the Americas headquarters for the parent company's enterprise software portfolio (ERP, SCM, CRM, HCM, analytics, and cloud platform). SAP America itself does not publish a US-specific developer portal or APIs distinct from the parent SAP SE surface — all API documentation, SDKs, and OpenAPI artifacts are catalogued under the sibling `sap` repository (api.sap.com, SAP Business Accelerator Hub, SAP BTP). This repo is a subsidiary placeholder that exists to (1) record SAP America as a distinct US legal entity for partnership, public-sector, procurement, and FedRAMP / GovCloud contexts, and (2) cross-link to related US-only sibling subsidiaries — most importantly SAP NS2 (SAP National Security Services), the independent US subsidiary that operates SAP workloads in the Cloud Intelligence Enterprise (CIE), the DoD cloud environment, and the Commercially Regulated Environment (CRE) for federal, defense, and intelligence community customers. No tier-1 API artifacts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, capabilities, plans, rate limits, FinOps) are generated in this repo per the api-evangelist no-empty-artifact rule — they are maintained under the parent `sap` repo and the per-product child repos (`sap-business-technology-platform`, `sap-successfactors`, `sap-ariba`, `sap-concur`, `sap-fieldglass`, `sap-api-management`, `sap-integration-suite`).

providers.name: Vertical Bar Inc.
providers.description: Vertical Bar Inc. builds CrossCheck, a DevOps and operations-visibility platform for NetSuite environments. CrossCheck gives NetSuite teams configuration tracking, change management and deployment safety: environment snapshots, comparisons and restore, automated record-and-replay regression testing that catches issues before production, AI-assisted error analysis with fix suggestions, and process mining to surface workflow delays and inefficiencies. Vertical Bar also offers managed services and industry-specific solutions for medical device, food and beverage, chemical, and aerospace and defense manufacturers, plus the FieldTrail browser extension for NetSuite field customization. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Agency
providers.description: Agency (agency.inc) builds Kai, an autonomous AI co-worker for customer success — an AI agent that works a company's entire book of B2B SaaS accounts, monitoring product usage, surfacing churn and expansion signals early, and running personalized onboarding, adoption, and renewal outreach so revenue and customer-success teams have command over their book. Agency raised a $20M Series A led by Menlo Ventures with participation from Sequoia Capital, Felicis, Snowflake Ventures, and Databricks Ventures. It is a demo-led enterprise product and does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Credit Genie
providers.description: Credit Genie is a consumer fintech operated by Creditly Corp. (Wilmington, Delaware, founded 2019) that runs a mobile-first money app for people living between paychecks. Its Cash Boost product advances $10-$150 with no interest and no hard credit check, funded against a linked bank account rather than a credit score, while Money Manager layers spending tracking, cash-flow prediction and subscription detection on top of that same bank connection. A Line of Credit product and AskGenie, an AI financial assistant, are in early access. Creditly Corp. is registered with the California DFPI under the CCFPL (registration 04-CCFPL-1956127-3514680) and has raised roughly $21M from Fortress Investment Group, Khosla Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures, Tippet Venture Partners and Gabriel Investments. Credit Genie is a direct-to-consumer app company: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: PiggyVest
providers.description: PiggyVest is a Lagos-based Nigerian fintech (operated by Piggytech Global Limited, RC 1405222) running the country's largest online savings and investment platform, with 6M+ registered users as of 2026.
