Founded in January 2016 by Somto Ifezue, Odunayo Eweniyi, and Joshua Chibueze as Piggybank.ng and rebranded to PiggyVest in April 2019, the company digitizes the traditional Nigerian "kolo" piggy-bank, layering automated savings, fixed-term safe-locks, naira and dollar wallets, and curated investments on top of licensed banking partners (originally United Bank for Africa) and a PCI-DSS-compliant payment stack. The consumer product family includes Piggybank (automated daily/weekly/monthly savings), SafeLock (fixed-tenor savings with up-front interest), Target Savings (goal-based saving, solo or group), Flex Naira (flexible wallet with free transfers), Flex Dollar / SafeLock Dollar (USD savings), HouseMoney (rent wallet), Investify (curated investment opportunities), GetIT (lifestyle purchase plans), Piggy Points (rewards), and an Accountability Partner feature, all delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps published by Piggytech Global. On the developer side, PiggyVest operates a separate B2B brand — PiggyVest Business — at piggyvest.business and exposes the PiggyVest Business API at api.piggyvest.business, documented at www.piggyvestbusiness.com/docs. The Business API is a Bearer-token authenticated REST API (secret key in Authorization header) covering customer creation and retrieval, customer wallets (create / retrieve / list, accrued-interest tracking, reserved account numbers, funding accounts), wallet-to-wallet and bank transfers (with name inquiry and bank lookup), transactions (status, history, T+1 settlement), scheduled payments (create / cancel / reactivate), webhooks for real-time event notifications, and a "Pay with Pocket" SDK / hosted-checkout integration that lets merchants accept payments funded from a Piggyvest user's Pocket balance. Default rate limits are approximately 100 requests per minute. No public OpenAPI specification, official SDK packages, or open-source client libraries are currently published; access is gated by signing up for a PiggyVest Business dashboard account. Alongside the API, PiggyVest Business offers Invoicing, Customizable Accounts, Business Safelock, Investify for Business, and business savings earning up to 18% per annum. Public engineering presence is limited — the Piggytech Global GitHub org (github.com/PiggyTech) hosts a small set of community wrappers (react-paystack, Smile Identity Node.js and React Native wrappers) and the consumer brand maintains a static piggyvest.github.io site, but there is no developer org publishing official Piggyvest Business SDKs.

providers.name: Apron
providers.description: Apron is a London, UK-based financial technology company that helps small business owners, accountants, and bookkeepers automate supplier payments, payroll, expenses, and payment collection. The platform captures invoices, batches and pays bills directly from a business bank account, and reconciles transactions in real time with accounting software such as Xero and QuickBooks Online. Founded by Bogdan Uzbekov (an early Revolut operator), Apron serves more than 10,000 businesses and is an FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (firm reference 1004915), ISO 27001 certified, and regulated under the UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 and Electronic Money Regulations 2011. Apron does not currently publish a public developer API; it integrates as a consumer of the Xero and QuickBooks accounting APIs.

providers.name: Indinero
providers.description: Indinero is a Finance-as-a-Service (FaaS) provider that combines professional accountants, tax experts, and fractional CFOs with AI-accelerated workflows to deliver outsourced accounting, bookkeeping, business tax preparation, payroll, 409A valuations, and on-demand financial support. Founded in 2009 and backed by 500 Global, the company serves startups through $500M+ revenue businesses across technology, SaaS, ecommerce, healthcare, construction, crypto, professional services, and non-profits, integrating primarily with QuickBooks Online and NetSuite. Indinero is SOC 2 compliant and delivers its services through a client portal (the indinero Exchange) rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Abacum
providers.description: Abacum is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform built for CFOs and finance teams to connect financial data, automate planning and reporting, and align cross-functional teams. It unifies budgeting and forecasting, headcount and revenue planning, scenario modeling, investor and board reporting, and P&L / balance-sheet / cash-flow roll-ups, with 700+ prebuilt integrations across ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Xero, Dynamics 365), HRIS and payroll (Workday, Rippling, BambooHR, Gusto, Deel), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), billing (Stripe, Chargebee, Maxio), and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). An Excel connector and embedded workflows keep planning models and actuals in sync. Abacum surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum and Scale Venture Partners.

providers.name: Sumary
providers.description: Sumary is a Denmark-based fintech building an AI-native workflow engine for finance and accounting teams. Its platform layers autonomous accounting agents, anomaly detection, and on-demand reporting over a company's existing accounting systems — automating reconciliations and variance explanations, validating transactions to catch errors and potential fraud, and generating management reports, margin analyses, and cost breakdowns for bookkeepers, controllers, CFOs, and finance leaders. The company raised a $4.2M (27M DKK) pre-seed round led by byFounders with participation from Partech and Tenity. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's web, trust, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Wiselayer
providers.description: WiseLayer is an AI-powered accounting automation platform that provides named "digital workers" (AI agents) for finance and accounting teams, automating tasks such as accruals, vendor communications, payroll accounting, bank reconciliations, depreciation and amortization, lease accounting, and prepaid expenses. The platform emphasizes transparent, explainable AI ("AI that shows its work") with natural-language interaction, automated email digests, and 300+ integrations into ERPs, billing, procure-to-pay, and HRIS systems. WiseLayer was acquired by BlackLine (NASDAQ: BL) and its product is now offered as Verity Accruals by BlackLine. WiseLayer was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. The company operates a SaaS application at app.wiselayer.com and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: AtoB
providers.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Brigit
providers.description: Brigit is a consumer financial technology company whose mobile app helps people manage everyday money with instant cash advances of up to $500 with no credit check, interest, or late fees, a Credit Builder account, and a Finance Helper for budgeting, spending analysis, bill tracking, and overdraft prediction. The app also bundles identity-theft protection and a deals-and-offers marketplace, and is offered on paid monthly subscription tiers. Brigit reports more than 12 million users. This API Evangelist profile is a company lead surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (Canaan Partners, DCM Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners); Brigit is a direct-to-consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record is enriched at the identity and web-property level.

providers.name: NetSuite Accounting
providers.description: NetSuite Accounting is the cloud financial management module of Oracle NetSuite that delivers general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, cash management, tax management, fixed assets, and real-time financial reporting and consolidation for growing businesses. NetSuite exposes its accounting records (invoices, bills, journal entries, payments, accounts, customers, vendors, and ledgers) through SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL queries, and RESTlets, secured with OAuth 2.0 and token-based authentication for ERP and finance integrations.

providers.name: Wishup
providers.description: Wishup is a remote-work outsourcing platform that matches businesses with pre-vetted virtual assistants, bookkeepers, and automation specialists, typically onboarding a trained professional within 60 minutes. Its managed talent handles inbox and calendar management, CRM and social-media work, bookkeeping, project management, and AI-driven workflow automation across industries such as healthcare, e-commerce, real estate, startups, nonprofits, and legal services. Wishup runs a client-facing Employee Management App for task tracking and real-time feedback, but publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Paro
providers.description: Paro is an AI-powered professional services marketplace that connects businesses and accounting firms with vetted, on-demand finance and accounting experts. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Chicago, Paro uses proprietary AI matching to pair clients with the top 2% of finance professionals across 60+ industries and 250+ skill sets — spanning bookkeeping, fractional CFO and controller services, financial planning and analysis, tax and compliance, and full-time recruiting. For accounting firms it provides staff augmentation, busy-season support, and service-expansion consulting. Paro operates a talent platform (app.paro.io) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, content, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Headnote
providers.description: Headnote is a legal payments and accounts-receivable platform built specifically for law firms. Founded in 2016 by attorney Sarah Schaaf, it lets firms accept trust-compliant credit card and eCheck (ACH) payments via shareable payment links and a hosted client payment portal, then automates collections, AR tracking, and client NPS/satisfaction reporting. Headnote is designed to be 100% compliant with IOLTA rules, the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct, and lawyer trust/operating account requirements across all 50 states, and integrates with existing billing and practice-management software by attaching a Headnote payment link to invoices. Card and bank data are tokenized with Stripe and Plaid and the platform runs on AWS with PCI-compliant, encrypted-at-rest-and-in-transit infrastructure. Headnote was acquired by ASG LegalTech (an Alpine Investors platform, alongside PracticePanther, Bill4Time, and MerusCase) in 2020. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. Headnote does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile is an identity record.

providers.name: plancraft
providers.description: plancraft is a German cloud-based business management software for craftspeople and trades businesses (Handwerk). It digitizes administrative workflows end to end — quote and estimate creation, project planning, time tracking, on-site documentation, material and labor costing, and invoicing — inside one integrated platform aimed at small and mid-sized construction and trade companies. plancraft supports DATEV export for tax/accounting workflows and DATANORM and GAEB catalog imports for material data and tender processing. It is a venture-backed SaaS company (portfolio company of Creandum). As of this enrichment pass plancraft publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — integrations are delivered as prebuilt connectors and standardized file-format import/export.

providers.name: Zervant
providers.description: Zervant is an online invoicing and billing platform for freelancers, sole traders, and small businesses. It lets users create, send, and manage estimates and invoices online, automate recurring invoices and payment reminders, track time and expenses, and get paid online across free and paid subscription tiers. Founded in Espoo, Finland and now part of the Ageras group, Zervant is a Northzone portfolio company. No public developer API is currently documented — this profile captures the company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Accrual
providers.description: Accrual is an augmented accounting intelligence platform for accounting firms and growing service businesses, offering what it calls the complete accounting workspace spanning engagement management, document intake, data processing, tax return generation, assurance workflows, and client collaboration. Backed by General Catalyst, the company emphasizes secure, US-hosted infrastructure with AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, data isolation, and SOC 2 Type II attestation, and states that customer data is not used to train AI models. Accrual does not publish a public API or developer program at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its published security posture.

providers.name: Contractor Foreman
providers.description: Contractor Foreman is all-in-one construction management software for contractors - estimates, invoicing, scheduling, time cards, daily logs, change orders, and job costing - used by contractors in more than 75 countries. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference; the company's dedicated API subdomain (api.contractorforeman.net) displays only a "Coming soon" placeholder as of this review. The one confirmed API capability is a private, account-scoped API key (generated under Settings > Integration > Zapier) that powers Contractor Foreman's official Zapier app, exposing Customer and Lead create/archive/delete triggers and actions plus a File Uploaded trigger. That key and its underlying endpoints are not documented or published for direct third-party use outside the Zapier integration; broader third-party connectivity otherwise runs through native integrations (QuickBooks, Gusto, Google Calendar/Outlook, Stripe, Angi Leads, CompanyCam, MS Project, SweetPay) and Zapier/webhook automation rather than an open API.

providers.name: Liveboard
providers.description: LiveBoard is a tutor-management platform that helps tutoring businesses, academies, and independent tutors run their operations end to end. It combines branded virtual classrooms (video calls, screen sharing, an interactive whiteboard, recording, and file sharing) with session scheduling and attendance tracking, tutor/student/parent management, calendar-based billing with online payments, auto-invoicing, payroll, and progress reporting. Liveboard says it serves 200,000+ tutors and companies across 200+ countries, scaling from solo tutors to organizations with thousands of tutors. It is a consumer/SaaS product with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time; integrations are teaching-focused (Wacom pen tablets, a LaTeX formula editor, and the Desmos graphing calculator). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pemo
providers.description: Pemo is a UAE-based fintech offering smart corporate cards and an all-in-one spend management platform for businesses across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The product combines physical and virtual corporate cards with expense management, automated receipt capture, invoice management, and accounting automation, giving finance teams real-time control and visibility over company spending. Pemo serves more than 10,000 companies and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. Pemo does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SiFi
providers.description: SiFi (الحلول المبسطة المالية) is a Saudi Arabian fintech company offering a comprehensive corporate spend-management platform for businesses in the Kingdom. Licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and serving more than 5,000 clients, SiFi provides physical and virtual corporate cards with spending controls, real-time expense tracking, employee reimbursements, accounting automation, local vendor payments and international transfers (coming soon), and a cashback rewards program, delivered through web and iOS/Android mobile apps. SiFi is backed by QED Investors. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Dave
providers.description: Dave is a U.S. consumer financial-technology company (Nasdaq: DAVE), founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that operates a mobile banking app serving roughly 14 million members. Its products include ExtraCash short-term cash advances of up to $500 (underwritten with its CashAI cash-flow model rather than credit scores), an FDIC-insured Dave Checking account with early direct deposit and Round-Up savings, and a Goals savings account. Banking services are provided through partner banks such as Coastal Community Bank. Dave is a consumer app and does not publish a first-party public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal: there is no developer.dave.com / docs.dave.com, and api.dave.com is the app's private, undocumented mobile backend. Programmatic access to Dave-held consumer data is aggregator-mediated — Dave both consumes Plaid (to let members link external accounts) and is reachable as a supported institution through open-finance aggregators. This profile captures its public identity, aggregator-only open-finance posture, commercial link surface, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Every
providers.description: Every is an AI-native, all-in-one back-office and finance platform built for startups, unifying incorporation, business banking and cards, treasury and cash management, global payroll, HR and benefits, AI-assisted bookkeeping, and startup tax preparation (including R&D tax credits) into a single system. It offers free Delaware C-corp formation, business checking with cashback debit cards, treasury-bill and money-market investing, and bundled per-stage plans for new founders through established startups. Backed by Redpoint Ventures. Every does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, commercial, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Harness Wealth
providers.description: Harness — the company that launched as Harness Wealth, and today a wholly owned business of Multiplier, Inc. — is a New York City firm that runs an advisory platform for tax and wealth practices. It operates three connected surfaces: a marketplace that matches individuals with complex financial situations (equity compensation, liquidity events, business owners, real estate, high net worth) to vetted tax advisors; a client portal and workflow platform that tax firms run their engagements, documents, questionnaires and e-file on; and Harness Wealth Advisers, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser that recommends third-party advisers. Harness publishes no public developer program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook documentation on any Harness host, and the product is delivered entirely as an end-user web application at app.harness.co.

providers.name: Approve.com
providers.description: Approve.com is a cloud-based procurement platform founded in 2019 in Israel that lets businesses stand up a proper purchase-order process quickly, streamlining purchase requisitions, multi-step approvals, real-time budgets, and vendor onboarding with real-time spend controls and insights. Tipalti acquired Approve.com in April 2021 and now operates it as Tipalti Procurement (Tipalti Approve). Its Procurement REST API is still served from the approve.com domain (production https://triggers.approve.com, sandbox https://triggers.sandbox.approve.com), authenticating with an x-api-key header and exchanging JSON with ISO 8601 dates; the purchase-orders API exposes GET and Update purchase-order operations so an external system can stay in sync with Tipalti.

providers.name: Lavante
providers.description: Lavante was a SaaS supplier information management (SIM) and profit-recovery company built on its patented Lavante Connect platform. Its products — Lavante SIM, Lavante Recovery and Vendor File Cleanse — cleansed vendor master files, verified addresses and TINs, ran OFAC screening, onboarded suppliers onto the Lavante Supplier Network, and drove dispute resolution and recovery audit across the procure-to-pay (P2P) ecosystem for Fortune 1000 clients in hospitality, retail, entertainment, manufacturing and medical. Lavante was acquired by PRGX Global and its standalone site was retired; www.lavante.com now 302-redirects to www.prgx.com, where the supplier-facing capability lives on as PRGX Supplier Connect. Lavante never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs or API documentation — the Internet Archive holds no api/developer/docs/swagger paths for the domain.

providers.name: wacai
providers.description: Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fintech and personal-finance company founded in 2009, best known for its "挖财记账" personal accounting and bookkeeping app and its internet wealth-management platform. Beyond its consumer apps, Wacai operates a partner-facing open API gateway (挖财开放平台) at open.wacai.com that exposes services through a single JSON-over-HTTPS entry point using appKey/appSecret signed requests, with official client SDKs published for Java (Maven Central), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Airbase
providers.description: Airbase is a modern spend management platform for finance teams that combines accounts-payable (AP) automation and bill pay, guided procurement and purchase orders, corporate cards, and expense reimbursements on a single system with real-time general-ledger sync. Airbase Inc. was acquired by Paylocity in a ~$325M deal announced September 4, 2024 and completed October 1, 2024, and now operates as "Airbase by Paylocity," extending Paylocity's HCM suite into the office of the CFO. Airbase exposes a developer platform at developer.airbase.io (REST API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman and Insomnia collections, a webhooks management API, an OAuth playground, and a sandbox) used to build custom connections for systems not covered by the pre-built integrations. API access is account-gated - credentials are generated inside the customer's Airbase/Paylocity tenant rather than through open self-serve signup - so the logical APIs below are honestly modeled from the documented product surface and developer portal, and the exact endpoint paths and base URL are not publicly reproduced here (endpointsModeled).

providers.name: nsKnox
providers.description: nsKnox is an Israeli fintech-security company that protects business-to-business payments against fraud and misdirection for corporations and banks. Founded and led by Alon Cohen, the founder and former CEO of CyberArk, nsKnox built its platform on a patented Cooperative Cyber Security (CCS) architecture in which payment and bank-account data is shredded and distributed across multiple independent "Knoxer" systems so that no single breach reveals anything. Its PaymentKnox product line covers outgoing payments (accounts payable), incoming payments (accounts receivable), Bank Account Certificates, Master Data Guard, Payment Check, and an Adaptive Payment Security service that validates payee bank accounts worldwide using Quick Check in-network lookups and Knox Verify out-of-network mini-transactions against the banking system. Customers connect through a hosted portal, scheduled file transfer, or a direct ERP API integration with systems such as SAP and Oracle. nsKnox publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the API surface is documented to onboarded customers only.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Brightside
providers.description: Brightside (Brightside Benefit, Inc.) is an employer-sponsored financial care benefit that helps working families reduce everyday money stress. Delivered as an employee benefit through employers, Brightside pairs each employee with a human Financial Assistant and a mobile/web app offering emergency cash and loans, debt management and credit-score improvement, savings and early wage access, bill negotiation, crisis support (eviction, utilities, food), and guidance through major life events. The company is backed by a16z, Obvious Ventures, and Trinity Ventures. Brightside is a consumer-facing benefits platform and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Pillar
providers.description: Pillar is an Italian construction-technology company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Milan, building what it calls the operating system for the construction industry (il sistema operativo per l'edilizia). Its cloud platform unifies the back office of building firms (imprese edili) — invoicing (fatturazione), cash-flow management (flussi di cassa), bank reconciliation, quotes and estimates (preventivi), procurement, job and project cost control (gestione commessa), and delivery notes and site work reports (DDT e rapportini) — alongside on-site safety (Pillar Sicurezza) and an AI layer (Pillar AI) that automates data entry in real time, including inputs captured from the job site over WhatsApp. Pillar is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital and today reaches customers through a book-a-demo model rather than a public self-serve signup or a developer-facing API; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sidekick
providers.description: Sidekick is a UK-based online wealth management and investing platform that offers expert-led investments and savings products once reserved for the ultra-wealthy, delivered through a mobile app and web platform. Its product range spans managed investment portfolios, savings accounts, private equity access, and cryptocurrency exposure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp, Sidekick is a consumer (B2C) fintech and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: caimitech
providers.description: caimitech.com is the domain of Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co.), a Chinese personal-finance and wealth-management company founded in 2009 that offers accounting/bookkeeping apps, personal financial management (PFM) tools, wealth-management services, and credit solutions. Its developer surface is the Wacai Open Platform (挖财开放平台) — an HMAC-signed API gateway addressed by (api_name, api_version) pairs rather than REST paths, with first-party client SDKs in Java (published to Maven Central under com.wacai), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#, plus a separate topic-based message gateway (pull/ack). Access uses an app_key/app_secret credential with MAC or RSA request signing and an optional token service. No OpenAPI document is published; this profile was enriched from the provider's public GitHub SDKs and package registries.

providers.name: Office Luv
providers.description: OfficeLuv is office management and purchasing software that centralizes all of a workplace's ordering into a single platform. It aggregates dozens of vendors and thousands of products (supplies, snacks, cleaning supplies, groceries, and more) into one unified marketplace with consolidated invoicing, spend analytics and reporting, multi-user approval workflows, employee stipends for remote and in-office staff, and optional on-site service for program design, pricing negotiation, and restocking. Customers include Wayfair, Braze, Glassdoor, Hulu, and Upwork. Office Luv was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The product is delivered as a private SaaS web application (app.officeluv.com); no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published at this time.

providers.name: Aiwyn
providers.description: Aiwyn is a practice-automation platform built for modern accounting and CPA firms, unifying payments, practice management, client experience, and tax into a single relationship-centered system. Aiwyn Payments automates invoicing, card and ACH collection, and reconciliation; Aiwyn Practice covers time, billing, project management and resource planning; Aiwyn Experience delivers a unified client portal for engagement letters and secure document exchange; and Aiwyn Tax adds AI-assisted tax preparation. The company serves 800+ firms and raised $113M from KKR and Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company; Aiwyn publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, its published llms.txt, and probed domain security.

providers.name: Marand
providers.description: Marand Software (Marand d.o.o., Ljubljana, Slovenia) builds cloud-native Business Support System components for communications service providers, positioned as a vendor of TM Forum Open Digital Architecture (ODA) components. Its product line covers a Unified Product Catalog, 360 Customer / Inventory, CPQ, CRM, Multiservice Enterprise Billing, AI/ML solutions and custom software services. Marand's components implement the TM Forum Information Framework (SID) and expose TM Forum Open APIs; the company is a TM Forum Open API Gold certified member, holds Open API conformance certifications for TMF633 (Service Catalog Management, 2022) and TMF673 (Geographic Address Management, 2023), achieved "Ready for ODA" status in March 2024, and co-authored the TMF760 Product Configuration API with Orange and Amdocs as one of the first fifth-generation TM Forum Open APIs. Marand publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification of its own — its APIs ship inside licensed components deployed at operator customers, and the contracts they implement are the TM Forum specifications.

providers.name: Oatfi
providers.description: OatFi is a fintech infrastructure company that describes itself as "The Modern Credit Network for B2B Payments." It provides embedded credit, lending, and working-capital products that platforms and marketplaces can offer inside their own payment workflows. Its product surface spans Accounts Payable (flexible payment terms for buyers), Accounts Receivable (guaranteed or early supplier payouts), and Commercial Charge Cards (scaled credit and capital for commercial card programs), backed by modular components for KYB and fraud verification, underwriting, origination, loan management, capital-markets access, and collections. OatFi exposes these capabilities through APIs for approvals, settlements, and reconciliation. The developer documentation (docs.oatfi.com, a ReadMe hub) and dashboard are access-gated, so no public OpenAPI or API reference is available for cataloging at this time. Backed by QED Investors.

providers.name: Savvy
providers.description: Savvy (Savvy Advisors, Inc.) is a technology-driven, SEC-registered investment advisory firm founded in 2021 and headquartered in New York, NY. It combines licensed fiduciary financial advisors with proprietary technology — including Savvy Intelligence, an AI workspace for advisors — to deliver personalized wealth management for high-net-worth individuals and independent financial advisors. Savvy manages $5B+ in assets across 100+ advisors in 30+ U.S. locations, custodying at Fidelity and Charles Schwab. The firm serves two audiences: clients seeking wealth management (financial planning, investment management, direct indexing, tax optimization, retirement, trust and estate planning) and advisors looking to join or build a practice on its platform. Savvy publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain security posture, and the verbatim /llms.txt it exposes for agents.

providers.name: ChangEd
providers.description: ChangEd (Changed) is a consumer financial-technology company whose mobile app helps people pay off debt faster by automatically rounding up everyday purchases to the nearest dollar and directing those micro-savings toward student loans, credit cards, mortgages, personal loans, and auto loans. Founded by brothers Dan Stelmach and Nick Sky, the app launched in 2017, appeared on Shark Tank and took investment from Mark Cuban, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It links to a user's bank account, tracks spending, automates extra debt payments, supports savings goals, and visualizes payoff progress for a $4/month subscription, with banking services provided by nbkc bank (Member FDIC). ChangEd is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clerkie
providers.description: Clerkie, operated by Henry Labs Inc. and founded in San Francisco in 2016, is an AI-powered debt management and loan-recovery platform serving both consumers and institutional lenders. The consumer side offers a conversational financial assistant for budgeting, debt negotiation, and personalized repayment planning, while the B2B side — marketed as Fiber, launched in 2021 and now sold on its own domain getfiber.ai — gives lenders, banks, credit unions, and collection agencies an AI-driven recovery suite spanning CRM, an inventory management system (IMS), an AI agent, omnichannel communications, borrower scoring, a self-service payment portal, and workflow automation. Clerkie markets a RESTful API and multi-currency payment processing for lenders to integrate loan portfolios, real-time reporting, and automated repayment arrangements, but publishes no public developer documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer portal — integration is arranged through a sales conversation. The company has raised over $41M from Left Lane Capital, Flourish Ventures, Vestigo Ventures, and Citibank.

providers.name: Riff
providers.description: Riff is an Oslo, Norway based enterprise software company building AI agents for supply chain, procurement, planning, and logistics operations. Its agents automate repetitive back-office work such as chasing supplier order confirmations, updating order and delivery status, matching invoices, and monitoring deliveries, while keeping actions deterministic, auditable, and team-controlled rather than purely generative. Riff integrates non-disruptively with existing ERP systems including SAP, Oracle, Infor, and Microsoft, is EU-based with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 aligned and GDPR compliant data handling, and was founded by veterans of Cognite. The company raised a $16M Series A backed by Northzone and other investors. Riff has no public developer or API program at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Zibo
providers.description: Zibo (operating as Azibo) is a financial services and property-management platform for independent landlords and rental property owners. The company offers a free-to-use platform that bundles rent collection, tenant screening, online rental applications, lease agreements and eSignatures, document storage, maintenance and messaging, banking, and rental-property accounting. Azibo monetizes through interest on cash balances, card-transaction fees, paid lease/eSignature and screening products, and renter subscriptions such as credit-boost programs. The product is delivered as a SaaS web application (app.azibo.com) that integrates third-party providers including Stripe, Plaid, TransUnion, Latchel, and signNow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. Zibo was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Farther
providers.description: Farther is a technology-driven wealth management and registered investment advisory (RIA) firm that pairs human financial advisors with a proprietary "Intelligent Wealth Platform." The firm has recruited more than $23 billion in client assets and positions itself among the fastest-growing US financial services firms (Inc. Magazine, Deloitte Technology Fast 500). Services span financial and retirement planning, investment and portfolio management, tax-intelligent optimization, trust and estate planning, generational wealth, small-business services, Farther Asset Management, and institutional offerings. The client experience runs through a single-page web/mobile application at app.farther.com and integrates account aggregation via Plaid. Farther does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures the firm's public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Kyrok
providers.description: Kyrok GmbH is a Berlin-based software company building an AI operating system for mid-sized pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturers in Europe. The platform layers over a company's existing ERP (SAP S/4HANA, SAP R/3, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Infor, Applus) and connects the systems supply chain teams currently hold together by hand into intelligent operations across customer service, production planning, material planning and procurement. Kyrok positions itself on an "AI assists, people decide" model, running on European infrastructure in Frankfurt am Main, GDPR-compliant, with ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certifications in progress. The company announced a EUR 3.1M round in June 2026 and names AnalytiChem and Konapharma as customers. Kyrok connects to ERP systems via API but publishes no public developer API, API reference, or SDKs as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Swypex
providers.description: Swypex is an Egyptian fintech, founded in 2022 and headquartered at Smart Village in Cairo, that provides an all-in-one financial management platform for businesses. The platform bundles corporate cards, payments, invoice management, and working capital financing into one system, giving finance teams real-time visibility and control over company spend. Swypex launched Egypt's first approval-based corporate card, where each transaction's limit unlocks only after real-time review and approval by the company's finance team, and offers e-invoicing (with an Odoo integration) and Swypextend working-capital financing. Swypex is licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt and operates its card program in partnership with Visa and Mashreq Bank. It raised a $4M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first fintech investment in MENA), with Foundation Ventures and Raba Partnership. Swypex does not publish a public developer API; its products are delivered through web and mobile apps plus a small set of native integrations (Odoo, e-invoicing, Just2Pay).

providers.name: Yardi Propware
providers.description: Yardi Propware was the original flagship property management software by Yardi Systems, first released in 1984. It was an early desktop-based real estate management platform for residential and commercial property accounting, leasing, and management. Yardi has since evolved its platform into cloud-based offerings including Yardi Voyager and Yardi Breeze. No publicly accessible developer portal or documented REST API has been confirmed for Yardi Propware specifically; Yardi's modern integrations are managed through the Yardi Interface Partnership Program.

providers.name: Bhub
providers.description: BHub (bhub.com) is a Brazilian accounting and financial back-office company serving small and medium-sized businesses across Brazil. It combines bookkeeping and tax accounting (contabilidade), financial business-process outsourcing (BPO financeiro) covering accounts payable/receivable and reconciliation, tax consulting (consultoria tributaria), and corporate/legal structuring (societario), delivered through its online client hub at app.bhub.ai. Specialized divisions Agrocontar (agribusiness) and Quality Associados (nonprofit/third sector) extend its sector coverage. Backed by QED Investors, BHub reports processing tens of millions of invoices and reconciling billions of reais annually. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio lead; BHub currently exposes an internal application backend (api.bhub.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Blend Financial
providers.description: Blend Financial Inc., doing business as Origin Financial (useorigin.com), is a consumer wealth management and personal finance platform that unifies income, net worth, spending, investments, assets, and liabilities into a single application. Origin pairs AI-powered budgeting and spend tracking with investment tools, estate and tax planning, and access to CFP professional advice; investment advisory services are provided through Origin Investment Advisory LLC, a subsidiary of Blend Financial Inc. The company is a consumer (B2C) product backed by 500 Global, Felicis Ventures, Founders Fund, and other investors, and also offers employer-sponsored financial wellness. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network it is a company profile; Origin publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Brightmoney
providers.description: Bright Money (Bright) is a San Francisco-based financial technology company that describes itself as the world's first AI Loan Assistant. Its consumer mobile app helps people pay off credit-card debt faster, build credit history, and access affordable credit through products including Bright Builder (a secured 0% APR credit line reported to the major bureaus), Bright Plan debt-payoff and budgeting, Smart Round-Ups automated savings, rent reporting, personal loans up to $10,000 through network partners, and cash advances up to $750 for all credit scores. Bright is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: BrightPlan
providers.description: BrightPlan is a San Jose, California based financial wellness company that sells a Total Financial Wellness platform to enterprise HR and benefits teams, combining a self-service digital financial planning application, an AI-powered financial wellness coach, and access to human CFP fiduciary advisors. BrightPlan LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and the product is delivered to employees as an employer-sponsored benefit rather than as a self-serve consumer subscription. The employee experience runs at my.brightplan.com and web.brightplan.com with iOS and Android apps; employer value is framed around benefits engagement, retention, and measurable financial wellbeing. BrightPlan markets HRIS and benefits-system integration to employers but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Heard
providers.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.

providers.name: Plum
providers.description: Plum is a UK-based personal finance "money app" that helps consumers save and invest automatically. Its mobile app pairs automated savings algorithms (eight saving automations) with a range of regulated products including Easy Access Savings, a Cash ISA, a 95-day Notice Account, a money-market Interest pocket, a Stocks & Shares ISA, a Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP), and access to thousands of stocks and funds. Plum operates under FCA oversight through multiple entities covering payment services, e-money, investment broking, and account information services, and monetizes via subscription tiers (Basic, Plus, Boost, Max). It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Taxfix
providers.description: Taxfix is a Berlin-based fintech that lets individuals and self-employed people in Germany prepare and file their annual income tax return from a mobile app or web browser. Users either answer a guided set of roughly 70 questions to self-file (Taxfix Basic) or hand the return to an independent tax expert via the Expert Service, with data transmitted to the tax authority over the official ELSTER interface. The company reports more than 10 million tax returns filed and over 5 billion euros in refunds. Taxfix is a consumer (B2C) product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture. Backed by Creandum, Index Ventures and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Ajax
providers.description: Ajax is an AI-powered timekeeping platform built specifically for law firms. It automatically captures attorney work across applications, documents, emails, phone calls, and video meetings, then generates OCG-compliant, voice-matched time-entry narratives and syncs them with one click to practice-management and billing systems. Ajax integrates with SurePoint, Clio, MyCase, Filevine, PracticePanther, Centerbase, Actionstep, and Soluno, and positions itself around recovering otherwise-lost billable hours. The company is SOC 2 aligned, encrypts data in transit and at rest, does not train models on customer data, and enforces rolling data deletion. Ajax is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a product/SaaS company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Quanta
providers.description: Quanta is a San Francisco-based accounting services company built for SaaS businesses, pairing expert human accountants with proprietary software that "shows its work." The platform delivers continuous accounting and reconciliation, explainable financial reporting through its agentic reporting layer (Prism), SaaS revenue and accounts-receivable insights, and real-time visibility into cash, burn, and runway alongside department-level spend tracking. Quanta is a managed-services and software product for finance teams rather than a developer-facing API provider; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Homebrew and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Scalable CFO
providers.description: The Scalable CFO is an Abu Dhabi (ADGM) based financial-operations platform for small and medium-sized enterprises. Its MADI software delivers real-time cash-flow forecasting, "what-if" scenario simulation, bill-payment planning and invoice-collection tracking, syncing with accounting systems such as Xero and QuickBooks. Alongside the software it runs a marketplace connecting businesses to 6,300+ pre-vetted fractional CFOs and accountants for accounts cleanup, tax compliance, margin optimization and fundraising readiness. The Scalable CFO is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: TopKey
providers.description: TopKey is an AI-powered financial operating system purpose-built for professional short-term rental, vacation rental, and long-term rental property managers running 50-5,000+ units. It automates property-level and owner-level expense management, corporate and bring-your-own cards (BYOC), bill pay / AP, banking through partner banks (Thread Bank, Member FDIC), AI-assisted accounting, inventory, invoicing, work-order expense tracking, and revenue reconciliation. TopKey integrates deeply with property management systems (Guesty, Hostaway, OwnerRez, Streamline, Track, Hostfully) and accounting software (QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite). Backed by a16z and Felicis. TopKey consumes partner APIs for its integrations but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time; it ships a product help center and a machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: Trim
providers.description: Trim is a consumer fintech company founded in 2015 that built an automated personal finance assistant which finds and cancels unwanted subscriptions, negotiates bills such as cable and internet, and automates savings for its users. Trim was backed by Version One Ventures and was acquired by OneMain Financial; its former asktrim.com home now redirects to OneMain MyMoney (onemainmymoney.com), where the product lives on as a personalized money insights and expense tracking app. Trim/MyMoney is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: LedgiFi
providers.description: LedgiFi (formerly Krypto Ledgers) is a Latin American cryptocurrency tax and portfolio-tracking platform founded in 2020 and headquartered in Antofagasta, Chile. The product syncs a user's transaction history from exchanges and wallets — Binance, Coinbase, Kraken and MetaMask among them — normalizes it across more than 25,000 assets, and computes realized capital gains using the valuation methods and monetary-correction adjustments each jurisdiction requires, so investors can file a compliant return. Its Chilean profile applies the SII's specific rules (IPC indexation and dollar-variation adjustments, Impuesto de Primera Categoría and Impuesto Global Complementario), and the platform has since expanded to Mexico, Spain, Colombia and Argentina. Alongside tax reporting it offers a portfolio view spanning crypto, stocks and ETFs, with per-asset performance and allocation. LedgiFi is a 500 Global (500 LatAm B18) portfolio company. It runs a monitored production API at api.ledgifi.com that backs its own web and mobile apps, but publishes no developer portal, no API specification and no self-service API program.

providers.name: Mimo
providers.description: Mimo (short for "Money In, Money Out") is a London- and Stockholm-based B2B fintech that gives small and medium-sized businesses a single platform to manage, understand and control their cash flow. Founded in 2023, Mimo bundles supplier payments, invoice collection, multi-currency accounts, access to working capital and automated bookkeeping, and has grown to offer an AI "Associate" that automates recurring accounting workflows such as financial close, bank reconciliation, accounts payable and payroll for finance teams and accounting firms. Mimo integrates with accounting tools such as Xero. It is backed by Northzone, Seedcamp, Cocoa Ventures, Project A and others, and has secured a $125M+ embedded-funding partnership with Froda. This profile is a company record in the API Evangelist network; Mimo currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Nitra
providers.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Wholesail
providers.description: Wholesail is an all-in-one accounts receivable and B2B payments platform for food & beverage wholesalers, distributors, and service vendors. It helps vendors onboard customers, manage credit risk, automate collections, accept ACH and card payments, and drive autopay — all connected to the vendor's ERP or accounting system. Wholesail is a fintech company backed by Foundry Group. As of enrichment it publishes no public developer API; it integrates with ERP systems using their native API protocols, scheduled file exchange, and robotic process automation, and it partners with Stripe, Plaid, Modern Treasury, JP Morgan, and SVB for payment processing. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: XSquare
providers.description: XSquare (listed as XSquire in the 500 Global portfolio) is a Dubai-based B2B financial operations platform for the GCC, live across the UAE and Qatar. It unifies e-invoicing, receivables collection via embedded payment links and QR codes (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank), supplier payables on corporate card, and automatic invoice-to-payment reconciliation on a single ledger, with native ERP integrations (Zoho, Xero, Wafeq, Odoo) and a PSP network (Tess, Telr, Geidea). PCI DSS Level 1 v4 certified, UAE FTA e-invoicing ready (PEPPOL, structured XML), and non-custodial by design through licensed PSP partners regulated by CBUAE and QCB. Founded in 2023 by Tanvir Shah and Ashwin Shenoy; operates as XSquare Payment Services LLC (Dubai) and XSquare LLC (Doha). No public developer API, docs, or SDKs are published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Butn
providers.description: Butn is an Australian embedded-finance company that funds business cashflow at the point of transaction, plugging invoice finance, outsourced credit terms, and supplier "pay now, settle later" directly into the platforms its business customers already use. Its funding products — Butn X (invoice finance to draw cash early against receivables), Butn Terms (outsourced buyer credit where Butn carries the risk), and Butn Pay (paying suppliers upfront in exchange for extended repayment) — are designed to be embedded into partner marketplaces, accounting tools, and B2B platforms such as MYOB, Salesforce, and FoodByUs rather than sold as a standalone destination. Butn sits in the spend / accounts payable and accounts receivable financing layer of Australia's payments market, where money movement rides the New Payments Platform and the banks opened by the Consumer Data Right. Its integration and embedding are delivered through private, partner-provisioned APIs: Butn markets "plug and play" embedding for partners but does not operate a public self-serve developer portal, publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger definitions, or expose openly documented API reference material as of this profile.

providers.name: Helu Io
providers.description: helu.io is a financial management, controlling, and reporting platform for startups and small-to-medium businesses. It connects directly to DATEV accounting data (via a certified DATEVconnect interface) to produce automated, real-time financial reports, customizable dashboards and KPIs, budget vs. actuals comparisons, multi-entity consolidation, and planning, so finance teams can analyze, plan, and collaborate without manual spreadsheet work. The company is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and hosts data on German servers in compliance with DSGVO/GDPR. helu.io is a SaaS product; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI — its integrations are product-level (DATEV, plus data upload from HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Excel, and Personio).

providers.name: Tenex
providers.description: Tenex is a PropTech platform for real estate and hospitality operators across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region, offering an all-in-one suite that unifies property management, tenant and landlord experience, facility and asset management, real estate accounting, VR for off-plan developments, and a hospitality guest experience app. Trusted across 500+ buildings and communities, it advertises integrations with ZATCA, SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft Dynamics to automate compliance and unify operations. Tenex is backed by 500 Global and the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface is published.

providers.name: Epicor
providers.description: Epicor Software Corporation provides industry-specific enterprise resource planning software for manufacturing, distribution, retail, and service industries. Epicor Kinetic, the flagship ERP platform, exposes an Open REST API built on OData v4 that gives developers service-based access to all business objects, processes, reports, BAQs, and Epicor Functions using standard HTTP methods and API key authentication.

providers.name: Leaner Technologies
providers.description: Leaner Technologies (株式会社Leaner Technologies) is a Tokyo-based B2B SaaS company founded on February 22, 2019 by CEO Yusuke Ohira, operating under the mission "調達のスタンダードを刷新し続ける" (continuously renew the standard of procurement). It builds the "Leaner" (リーナー) cloud suite for corporate procurement and purchasing departments: Leaner購買 (purchasing), a purchase-to-pay system covering quotation, approval workflow, ordering, receiving and payment; Leaner sourcing, a quotation and sourcing workspace; Leaner Connect, an SRM supplier-relationship platform; plus procurement BPO and consulting services. The platform aggregates supplier and EC catalogs (including Amazon Business and MonotaRO) into cross-catalog search, and applies AI to classify purchasing data for indirect-spend visibility and cost optimization. The company holds ISMS ISO/IEC 27001:2013 / JIS Q 27001:2014 certification (registration JP21/080659, February 2021). Leaner publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs as of this enrichment pass — its integration surface is delivered through partner catalog connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: MHub
providers.description: MHub is a Malaysian property-technology (proptech) platform operated by TRB Ventures Sdn Bhd and backed by 500 Global. It gives real-estate developers an integrated system to manage the entire new-property sales cycle — from lead generation, launch, and online booking (Showroom, CRM, SalesCandy) through automated billing and collections (Credit Control), accounting and financial reporting, statutory compliance (HIMS/KPKT registry synchronization and LHDN-compliant e-invoicing), commission control, and handover/defect management. MHub runs a developer portal at developer.mhub.my and an authentication-gated REST API at api.mhub.my for platform integrations.

providers.name: Stacks
providers.description: Stacks is an AI-native financial close and accounting platform for controllers, CFOs, and accounting teams. It automates the monthly close across existing ERPs with agentic tooling for account reconciliations and transaction matching, journal-entry posting and review, close-management checklists and approvals, and AI-powered analysis, variance explanation, and reporting. Stacks connects directly to ERP systems (Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday), data warehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift), file storage, and spreadsheets, and offers an Excel add-in for manual journals. A developer API for custom reconciliation logic is announced as "coming soon." Stacks is a fintech company backed by EQT Ventures, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Version One Ventures. Profile enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public web surfaces (no public API specification is yet available).

providers.name: Baselane
providers.description: Baselane is an all-in-one financial platform (financial operating system) for independent landlords and real estate investors, combining FDIC-insured landlord banking, automated rent collection, bookkeeping and expense tracking, analytics and reporting, and cash-flow tools in a single product. Banking services are provided through partner Thread Bank, and account connectivity to external banks is powered by Plaid. Baselane is a consumer/SMB fintech application (web and mobile apps) rather than an API platform: it publishes no first-party public developer API, developer portal, or API reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Sector: fintech / proptech.

providers.name: Dianxiaomi
providers.description: Dianxiaomi (店小秘) is a free cross-border e-commerce ERP platform operated by Shenzhen Meiyunji Network Technology Co., Ltd., serving more than 1.8 million cross-border sellers worldwide. It unifies product listing and data collection, multi-platform order processing, warehouse and inventory management, procurement, financial and profit analytics, and customer service across 70+ marketplaces including AliExpress, Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop, with integrations to 1,700+ logistics providers and 130+ overseas warehouses. The platform is user-facing SaaS; no public developer/API open platform is currently published.

providers.name: Forterro
providers.description: Forterro is a pan-European industrial software company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, that provides enterprise resource planning (ERP) and specialised business software to the industrial mid-market. Built through a series of acquisitions, Forterro operates a portfolio of regional and vertical ERP brands - including Abas, Jeeves, Garp, Proconcept, Sylob, Silog, Myfactory, Orderwise, Clipper, 123Insight, BPSC, Helios, Proffix, Prodaso and its cloud-native Fortee product - alongside best-in-class point solutions such as warehouse management (WMS), point of sale (POS), material requirements planning (MRP) and business intelligence. The company serves more than 13,000 industrial businesses across manufacturing, warehousing, wholesale and retail from 40+ offices worldwide.

providers.name: Siteline
providers.description: Siteline is billing and accounts receivable software built specifically for commercial subcontractors (trade contractors). It centralizes pay applications (including AIA G702/G703 progress billing), lien waivers, lien rights, compliance documents, change orders, collections, and A/R reporting in one workflow, replacing the spreadsheets, PDFs, and GC payment-portal logins that AP/AR teams juggle every month. Siteline integrates with construction accounting systems (Sage, Foundation, Viewpoint/Vista, Spectrum, QuickBooks, Acumatica, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, CMiC, and others) and with GC payment portals (Textura, GCPay, Procore Pay) so billing data flows without double entry. Founded in 2019 by Claire Wilson and Gloria Lin, backed by Menlo Ventures and First Round Capital; subcontractors have billed over $10B across 200,000+ projects on the platform. Siteline publishes no public developer API — integrations are managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Coinshift
providers.description: Coinshift is a non-custodial, multi-chain onchain treasury management platform for startups, DAOs and crypto-native organisations, founded in 2021 as MultiSafe and built on top of Safe (Gnosis Safe) multisig accounts. The application unifies portfolio tracking across ERC-20 tokens and NFTs, multi-signature proposal and transaction workflows, mass and recurring payouts, contact and label management, CSV transaction export and cash-flow reporting, plus embedded dApp integrations for Aave, CoW Swap, 1inch, LI.FI, ParaSwap, Hedgey, Request Finance and Superfluid money streams, with Slack and Discord signing notifications. Coinshift also issues onchain yield assets — csUSDL, an ERC-4626 vault receipt token for USDL deposited into the Coinshift USDL Morpho Vault, csUSDC, the SHIFT governance token, and the iUSPC institutional credit product. Coinshift publishes no public developer API: the documentation at docs.coinshift.xyz is entirely end-user product and asset guidance, with no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, GraphQL schema or webhook catalog.

providers.name: OrderCircle
providers.description: OrderCircle is a B2B wholesale order management software platform, founded in 2015 in San Francisco, that gives fast-growing brands one system to automate wholesale orders, track inventory in real time, generate invoices, and run a self-service B2B eCommerce portal for their buyers. It targets wholesale operations in apparel, coffee, jewelry, food and beverage, hemp, vape, and CBD, and connects to existing tools through pre-built integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, QuickBooks, Xero, ShipStation, Stripe, Square, PayPal PayFlow, and Authorize.Net. OrderCircle does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its programmatic surface is limited to its packaged third-party integrations. This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Possible Finance
providers.description: Possible Finance is a consumer fintech company offering small-dollar installment loans and credit-building products through a mobile app. Its core products are the Possible Loan (up to $500 with flexible repayment schedules), the Possible Advance (up to $300 drawn against a future paycheck), and Bill & Rent Reporting that builds credit history by reporting on-time payments to the credit bureaus. The company charges no late fees or penalty charges and uses AI-driven underwriting based on real banking activity rather than FICO scores, serving borrowers who are underserved by traditional credit. Possible Finance operates as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and is backed by Union Square Ventures. It is a mobile-app, consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aura Finance
providers.description: Aura Finance is an employer-sponsored financial wellness platform that blends behavioral psychology with money management to help employees reach financial stability and peace of mind. The San Francisco fintech — a Techstars Economic Mobility 2023 company and an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 318940) — delivers goal-based automated investing, one-on-one financial coaching over chat, budgeting and saving tools, financial-literacy workshops, mindfulness exercises to reduce money stress, and a money-personality quiz, offered through a B2B2C model to organizations and their workforces. The company publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; its member application lives at web.aurafi.io.

providers.name: EcomExperts
providers.description: EcomExperts is a Latin American ecommerce ERP and technology platform that helps online sellers manage, synchronize, and automate their stores from a single screen. It centralizes omnichannel operations across marketplaces and sales channels (including multi-account Mercado Libre management), synchronizes prices and stock in real time, and issues electronic invoices automatically in bulk. Delivered as a SaaS application with a hosted dashboard and a 7-day free trial, EcomExperts operates across Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Uruguay, Colombia, and Peru. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. EcomExperts does not currently publish a public developer platform, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures company identity and public-surface signals only.

providers.name: Eton Solutions
providers.description: Eton Solutions, L.P. is a Morrisville, North Carolina wealth-technology company that builds AtlasFive, a purpose-built ERP platform for single-family offices, multi-family offices, private funds and the ultra-high-net-worth families they serve. AtlasFive consolidates general ledger and partnership/fund/trust accounting, investment management and performance, bill pay and transaction processing, tax workflow, CRM and document management onto one data core, and aggregates positions and transactions from more than 1,500 banks and custodians via direct electronic feeds, portal scrapes, PDF statement extraction and partner aggregators. The EtonAI product line layers a knowledge graph and generative-AI assistants over that core. Integration is delivered through customer-scoped Reporting APIs and a Power BI connector rather than a public developer program: Eton Solutions publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK or sandbox as of August 2026. The company does publish a substantial compliance posture — ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management), ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II, with GDPR and CCPA alignment — and the platform is hosted on Microsoft Azure. Founded out of the multi-family office Eton Advisors and led by CEO Robert Mallernee with Executive Chairman Satyen Patel, with additional offices in Dubai and Bengaluru.

providers.name: Backstartup
providers.description: Backstartup is a Colombian tech-enabled accounting and legal services firm for startups and small businesses (notably SAS entities). It automated company formation, bookkeeping, tax filing, payroll, and legal/DIAN compliance for founders in Latin America. Backstartup has since been integrated into Numbi (numbi.ai), a tech-enabled accounting firm that operates monthly bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and DIAN compliance on top of the accounting systems companies already use (Siigo and Alegra), pairing expert accountants with automation and AI. Backstartup's legacy domain (backstartup.com) now redirects to numbi.ai and Backstartup operates as a sub-organization within Numbi's Colombia operation. This is a services-company profile: no public developer API or OpenAPI is published. It entered the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Cino
providers.description: Cino (getcino.com) is a European consumer fintech that offers the first shared virtual card that splits and pays a group bill at the same time. Members connect their existing debit or credit cards, create a group with configurable split ratios, and each person is charged only their proportional share at the moment of payment with no pre-funding required. The shared card works online and in person for one-off or recurring expenses, integrates with Apple Pay and Google Pay, supports per-transaction and monthly spending limits, and positions itself as a replacement for bill-splitting tools like Splitwise, Tricount, PayPal, and Tikkie. Cino is available across 29 European countries and is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital. This is a consumer mobile app with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Raenest
providers.description: Raenest (formerly Geegpay) is a global money platform for freelancers, creators, remote workers, students, and businesses in Africa and beyond. It provides multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, EUR, USDT, and USDC, virtual and physical Visa cards, international payment collection from 190+ countries, smart invoicing tools, US stock investing, stablecoin support, and a rewards program. Raenest is delivered through its mobile and web apps (app.raenest.com); as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. Backed by QED Investors and Techstars.

providers.name: Travelstop
providers.description: Travelstop (rebranded WegoPro) is a modern corporate travel and expense management platform founded in Singapore and backed by Accel. Companies use it to book flights and hotels from multiple supply partners, enforce travel policy and approval workflows, and automate expense reporting with receipt scanning (OCR), duplicate detection, and fraud prevention. Expense and accounting data syncs to Xero and QuickBooks, and native iOS and Android apps support travelers on the move. The product exposes prebuilt in-app accounting integrations rather than a public, self-serve developer API; this profile enriches its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Assemble
providers.description: Assemble builds autonomous AI agents that help enterprise IT and business-systems teams automate development work inside core platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Workday, and NetSuite. The agents scope changes across integrated ERP, CRM, and HRIS systems, understand cross-system dependencies, implement and validate modifications, and keep a complete audit trail so teams can review agent work, approve modifications, and revert individual changes or restore a system to a prior state. Assemble is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company targeting IT and business-systems teams managing complex enterprise transformations. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI, so only its verified public identity and website properties are captured.

providers.name: BillTrim
providers.description: BillTrim is a consumer bill-management and negotiation service that helps households lower, monitor, and pay their recurring bills. Its team negotiates with providers on the customer's behalf (up to twice a year), watches for price increases before autopay processes, and can pay bills automatically from a connected bank account. BillTrim advertises support for 20,000+ service providers across internet, cable, phone, insurance, and other recurring household expenses. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Current
providers.description: Current (Finco Services, Inc.) is a New York City-based U.S. financial technology company operating a mobile-first consumer banking platform serving over six million members. Through partner banks Choice Financial Group and Cross River Bank it offers fee-free spending accounts with early direct deposit (up to two days early), fee-free overdraft, and paycheck advances; Savings Pods earning competitive APY with automated Round-Ups; the Build Card for responsible credit building without a traditional credit check; fee-free cryptocurrency trading; and teen banking accounts with parental controls and automatic allowances. Current is a technology company, not a bank. It does NOT publish a first-party public developer API or developer portal — no developer.current.com (does not resolve), current.com/developers and current.com/api return 404, and api.current.com is an undocumented mobile-app backend. Programmatic access to member account data is available only through third-party open-finance aggregators (Plaid), on a consumer-permissioned basis. This profile captures the company's public web, legal, and security surface and its aggregator-only data-access posture.

providers.name: Meadow
providers.description: Meadow is a financial technology company delivering modern student financial services to colleges and universities. Its platform spans the full student financial lifecycle — Meadow Price (a mobile, SAI-compliant net price calculator), Meadow Pay (student billing and payments with automated workflows), Meadow Pre (pre-collections for recovering unpaid tuition), and Meadow Checkout (campus-wide collection of non-tuition fees). Meadow helps institutions improve enrollment, retention, and payment outcomes from application through graduation. Backed by Matrix Partners and Y Combinator. No public API or developer platform is published as of this profile.

providers.name: HighRadius
providers.description: HighRadius is an AI-powered autonomous finance platform for the Office of the CFO, automating the Order-to-Cash (O2C), Record-to-Report (R2R), Accounts Payable (AP), and Treasury processes with a network of orchestrated AI agents. The platform covers invoicing, collections, cash application, deductions, credit, dispute management, financial close, reconciliation, consolidation, and cash forecasting. HighRadius serves 1,500+ enterprise customers and ships pre-built integrations with 50+ ERPs and systems including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, and NetSuite. Integration is delivered through those pre-built ERP connectors and partner engagements rather than a public self-serve developer API; the company publishes a Trust Center documenting SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and GDPR posture.

providers.name: Paraglide
providers.description: Paraglide is a British-Swedish AI company building autonomous agents that automate accounts receivable for high-volume B2B finance teams. Its agents handle two-way billing communication across the order-to-cash lifecycle: answering customer billing questions, chasing overdue invoices, resolving disputes and deductions, running collections, operating a supplier portal, and applying cash — integrating with ERPs, CRMs, and billing software to cut Days Sales Outstanding and improve cash flow. Founded in 2025 by Rasmus Areskoug and Andreas Astrom with offices in London and Malmo, Paraglide raised a $5M seed round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and DN Capital in January 2026.
