As of this profile the company is a product/agent platform with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Beam
providers.description: Beam is a construction financial management platform for residential and commercial contractors, headquartered in San Francisco. Its cloud software unifies estimating and proposals, progress invoicing with online payment collection, job costing and real-time profitability, expense management via the Beam Card, bill-pay automation, lien-waiver and compliance tracking, project management (daily logs, scheduling, change orders), and a cash-management account that earns cash back. Beam integrates with QuickBooks Online, CompanyCam, RenoFi and XactRemodel, and relies on vetted partners including Stripe, Footprint and CapitalOS for payments and KYC/KYB. Beam does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation surface, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Karat.io
providers.description: Karat (trykarat.com) is a fintech platform providing integrated business banking and financial tools built for entrepreneurs, content creators, agencies, and small businesses managing irregular income. Its product suite spans FDIC-insured business checking accounts with high APY, the Karat Card and Karat Max charge/credit cards with rewards and no annual fees, mass and international contractor payments, AI-powered bookkeeping with automatic transaction categorization, invoicing, and multi-entity team management. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Karat publishes a consumer web and mobile app but no public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Kestrl: Muslim Money App
providers.description: Kestrl is a UK-based, FCA-regulated ethical fintech offering a values-aligned money app for Muslim and ethically-minded consumers. In partnership with Maybank Islamic, it provides interest-free (Sharia-compliant) banking, a Mastercard debit card with values filtering, goal-based sub-accounts, interest purification and Zakat calculation, transaction monitoring that alerts users to payments toward ethically questionable companies, and security features such as card freezing and biometric authentication. Kestrl is a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: MidFirst Bank
providers.description: MidFirst Bank is a federally chartered savings association (thrift) headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and owned by Midland Financial Co. Founded in 1982 with roots in Midland Mortgage from the early 1950s, it is the largest privately owned bank in the United States, with roughly $42 billion in assets and retail banking, private banking, commercial real estate lending, and nationwide mortgage servicing operations across Oklahoma, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, Texas, and Utah. MidFirst does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated: through its "Open Access" program, MidFirst adds direct API connections between its Business Online Banking platforms and consumer-permissioned data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Stripe, Intuit, Mastercard/Finicity, Envestnet Yodlee, and Morningstar), replacing screen scraping. There is no publicly documented first-party API surface, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is published on its site as of this review.

providers.name: Commons
providers.description: Commons is an Oakland, California consumer climate-fintech company founded in 2018 by Sanchali Seth Pal and operated under the name Joro until its March 2023 rebrand. Its free iOS and Android app connects a user's bank accounts and credit cards through Plaid and runs every transaction through a proprietary carbon-estimation engine, the Carbonizer, which translates dollars spent into an estimate of kilograms of CO2e, alongside budgeting, savings goals, expert-reviewed sustainable brand ratings, a rewards program, monthly community challenges and an optional paid offset membership. The company has raised roughly USD 13.9 million across three rounds from investors including Sequoia Capital and Amasia. Commons is a direct-to-consumer mobile product rather than an API vendor: thecommons.earth is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract, its brand directory and member exchange run on Next.js and Softr respectively, and its only public GitHub organization, CommonsTech, holds a single 2023 repository publishing carbon-offset provider evaluations rather than code.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Caribou
providers.description: Caribou is a Denver-based fintech that helps drivers lower their monthly car payments by refinancing existing auto loans through a network of banks, credit unions, and community lenders. Customers check personalized rates with a soft credit pull (no score impact), compare offers, add co-borrowers, and complete refinancing online, and can bundle optional vehicle protection plans. Caribou reports 150,000+ customers and average savings of about $162/month. The company exposes a consumer web application and a contact-gated partner integration program (click-out and API options for affiliates); it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API at this time.

providers.name: Clark
providers.description: Clark ("Dein Versicherungsmanager") is a Germany-based digital insurance manager that lets consumers view, compare, optimize, and manage all of their insurance policies in one mobile app and web platform. Founded in Frankfurt in 2015, Clark pairs a licensed insurance brokerage with automated tariff comparison across more than 180 insurance providers and free expert consultation, covering health, liability, property, life, mobility, and retirement products. The company operates across Germany, Switzerland, France, and the UK, serves over 700,000 customers, and is backed by venture investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Clark exposes no public developer API or developer portal; it is a consumer-facing insurtech rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Croissant
providers.description: Croissant is the workspace infrastructure layer for distributed teams, letting companies find, book, and manage on-demand access to 700+ coworking spaces across 100+ cities without long-term leases. Founded in 2015, the platform pairs instant workspace booking with spend governance, centralized policy controls, vendor consolidation, and usage-intelligence reporting, giving finance and people teams real-time control over where and how their people work. Croissant serves early-stage, scaling, and enterprise organizations, and exposes Slack, HRIS, stipend, and ERP integrations plus a custom API and integrations on its enterprise tier.

providers.name: Juno
providers.description: Juno is a Brazilian B2B payments fintech, acquired by EBANX in October 2021, that provides a complete billing and payments platform for Brazilian companies. Founded in 2014 in Maringá, Paraná, Juno powers more than 35,000 small and medium businesses with online sales and collections via Pix, boleto bancário, boleto_pix, and credit cards, plus marketplace payment split, recurring subscriptions, and a digital business account (Conta Juno) with Banking-as-a-Service capabilities. Juno is a participant of the Brazilian Interbank Payments Chamber (CIP). The company exposes a public REST API v2 through the Juno Developer Academy at integracao.juno.com.br, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials, plus HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks and native mobile Direct Checkout SDKs for Android and iOS for PCI-safe card data encryption.

providers.name: Ventura
providers.description: Ventura builds the AI workforce for distributors and manufacturers, starting with quoting and order entry. It reads inbound requests in any format - emails, PDFs, images, and phone calls - matches products against the customer's catalog, drafts a quote or order for a sales rep to review and approve, and pushes the approved result into the customer's ERP, with sales intelligence and a phone agent that transcribes rep calls and creates the resulting quote or order. Ventura plugs into the ERP and CRM a distributor already runs, follows the team's documented procedures, and learns from every correction. Ventura (formerly Autola) is operated by Gradient Ascent Labs, Inc., a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company based in San Francisco founded by Swen Koller and Jack Collins. As of 2026-08-14 the company publishes a marketing website and a privacy policy only: no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, OpenAPI, MCP server, or agent card was found on any Ventura host, and the customer application at app.ventura.ai redirects every path to a login.

providers.name: Mosaic Tech
providers.description: Mosaic Tech (Mosaic) was a San Francisco-based Strategic Finance Platform, founded in 2019, that connected ERP, CRM, HRIS, billing and data-warehouse systems into a single financial data model for FP&A teams — real-time analytics, agile financial planning, cash-flow forecasting, headcount planning and multi-entity consolidation. HiBob announced its acquisition of Mosaic on 2025-02-13 and closed it on 2025-04-01, folding the product into HiBob's finance/FP&A suite. As of 2026-08-26 the mosaic.tech domain 301-redirects every path to hibob.com, app.mosaic.tech redirects to finance-app.hibob.com, and api.mosaic.tech answers 503 on every path. Mosaic never published a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification under its own brand — 493 archived mosaic.tech URLs in the Internet Archive contain no /api, /docs, /developers, swagger or openapi path. HiBob's own developer surface is profiled separately.

providers.name: Treasury
providers.description: Treasury (treasury.app) is a consumer investing and personal-finance education platform that bills itself as "the first investing platform built for learning as a community" and a "non-judgmental investing community." It pairs creator-led learning communities (workshops, coaching, and discussion forums), commission-free brokerage investing accounts with fractional and recurring investments, and self-guided courses on investing, personal finance, and retirement. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and other investors, Treasury has introduced tens of thousands of new investors to the market. It has no traditional public REST/OpenAPI developer platform, but it does expose an agent-native surface: a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at treasury.app/mcp guarded by an OAuth 2.1 authorization server (authorization code + PKCE, dynamic client registration, scope mcp:connect).

providers.name: Worldover
providers.description: Worldover is the AI operating system for chemicals and cosmetics companies, replacing fragmented ERP, PLM, QMS, LIMS, and regulatory tools with one AI-orchestrated system custom-built around each team's workflows. Powered by Willow, its chemical and regulatory intelligence engine, it runs AI agents for demand planning, regulatory monitoring, quality, formulation R&D, supply chain, SDS authoring, and PLM updates. Headquartered in London and backed by Index Ventures, Chalfen, and EF, Worldover serves beauty brands, manufacturers, ingredient providers, distributors, and pharma and supplements companies. No public developer API is published.

providers.name: Advantive
providers.description: Advantive is an AI-enabled software company for specialty manufacturing and distribution operations, unifying ERP, MES, quality (SPC/SQC), PLM, WMS, and B2B commerce workflows into industry-specific systems. Built from a portfolio of brands including Advantzware, DDI System, Distribution One, InfinityQS (Enact and ProFicient), Kiwiplan, WinSPC, and VIA, Advantive serves more than 2,500 customers across eight countries in verticals such as food and beverage, packaging (corrugated, folding carton, plastics), automotive, aerospace and defense, electronics, and distribution of fasteners, bearings, HVAC, and janitorial supplies. The company is a private-equity-backed operations software provider; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public digital surface. No public developer API or OpenAPI has been found — integration is delivered through the products' own connectors and the Advantive support portal.

providers.name: Anyfin
providers.description: Anyfin is a Swedish consumer-fintech company that helps people lower the cost of their existing debt. Through its mobile app, customers photograph or import a current loan, credit card, or installment plan and Anyfin offers to refinance and consolidate it at a lower interest rate into a single monthly payment. Products span personal loans, credit-card and installment refinancing, car loans, debt consolidation, credit-score checking (via UC) and optional payment-protection insurance (via AXA). Founded in 2018 and backed by Accel, EQT Ventures and Northzone, Anyfin operates primarily in the Swedish market. It exposes no public developer API or developer portal; its api.anyf.in backend serves the consumer app only.

providers.name: Datacor
providers.description: Datacor is an enterprise software company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, that builds industry-specific business management and engineering software for process manufacturers, chemical distributors, and animal-nutrition producers. Its business-automation suite spans ERP, CRM, MES, WMS, formulation management, BLISS LIMS, regulatory and nutrition labeling, and TrackAbout asset tracking, while its engineering line delivers chemical process simulation and flow-modeling tools including CHEMCAD, Fathom, Arrow, Impulse, and xStream. Datacor serves the petrochemical, refinery, energy, feed, and specialty-chemical sectors, and has begun layering AI-driven capabilities across its products. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Datacor does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specifications; this profile captures its verified public identity while the API surface (if any) remains behind its customer support portal.

providers.name: Finku
providers.description: Finku is an AI-based personal finance management (PFM) mobile app from Indonesia, recognized as the number-one Indonesia PFM app and a Google Play "Best of 2025" selection with more than one million users. It helps people track expenses, set budgets, and build better money habits through manual entry, receipt and bank e-statement scanning, and FinGPT, a chat-based AI financial assistant. The app connects multiple banks and e-wallets, generates real-time interactive dashboards and reports, and runs a freemium model with a Premium tier. Finku is registered with Indonesian regulators OJK, Kominfo, AFTECH, and AFPI, and secures user data with 256-bit AES encryption. Finku is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile originated as a VC-portfolio lead for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: FlyFin
providers.description: FlyFin is an AI-powered tax preparation and filing platform for freelancers, self-employed individuals, 1099 contractors, sole proprietorships, LLCs, S-Corps, C-Corps, partnerships, and W-2 employees. It pairs an A.I. deduction scanner that connects to 2,000+ financial institutions through Plaid with a team of certified CPAs who prepare and file federal and state returns. The product suite includes a quarterly tax calculator, a CPA-certified AI tax assistant for unlimited questions, audit insurance with IRS representation, and Excel tax-summary exports. FlyFin operates as a consumer mobile and web application (iOS and Android) and does not publish a public developer API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Glimpse
providers.description: Glimpse (legally Dime Campus, Inc.) is an AI-native retail finance platform that automates deductions management, revenue recovery, and cash application for consumer brands and CPG companies. Its AI agents are trained on billions of dollars in retail transactions to track, validate, and dispute invalid deductions, recover trapped cashflow, and match payments faster across retailer accounts. Glimpse reports a 91% dispute win rate, $200M+ in transactions processed, and 100+ hours saved monthly per finance team, and works alongside major retailers including Walmart, Target, Kroger, Walgreens, and Amazon. The San Francisco company serves 200+ consumer brands, raised a $35M Series A, and is backed by 8vc. It is currently an enterprise, contact- sales SaaS with no public self-service API or developer portal.

providers.name: Oolka
providers.description: Oolka is a Bangalore-based consumer fintech that helps people in India check, monitor, and improve their credit scores. Its mobile app provides free bureau-integrated credit-score checks (Experian), a Credit Builder for users with no prior credit history, EMI and bill payments with cashback via Bharat Bill Pay (the RBI-NPCI initiative), AI-guided insights on credit utilization and payment timing, and assistance disputing incorrect credit-report entries. Oolka operates as a co-branded financial-product partner working with banks and financial institutions. It is a consumer-facing mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: SmartAsset
providers.description: SmartAsset is a financial technology company that runs the largest online marketplace connecting consumers with fiduciary financial advisors. Its SmartAdvisor matching service pairs more than 50,000 retail investors each month with up to three vetted advisors based on geography, investable assets, and preferences, while the SmartAsset Advisor Marketing Platform (AMP) delivers advisors a subscription stream of qualified referrals plus lead automation that syncs into their CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Wealthbox, Redtail, Zoho, Pipedrive, SmartOffice). SmartAsset also publishes a large library of consumer personal-finance calculators and editorial content across taxes, retirement, mortgages, investing, and banking. Backed by a16z and Y Combinator, SmartAsset is a lead-generation and media business and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Taxdoo
providers.description: Taxdoo is a Hamburg-based fintech providing real-time e-commerce accounting software for online retailers and tax advisors. The platform automatically captures sales, fees, payments, invoices, and contracts across 50+ marketplaces, shop systems, and payment providers (Amazon, eBay, Kaufland, Shopify, JTL, PayPal, Stripe, Klarna, Mollie), reconciles them into GoBD-compliant, audit-ready financial data, performs AI-based invoice verification, and exports daily to DATEV. Integrations are delivered as managed no-code connectors; Taxdoo does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Mooncard
providers.description: Mooncard is a French corporate expense-management platform that pairs a smart payment card, a mobile app, and accounting-automation software so finance teams can handle business spending end to end without manual data entry. It automates expense reports, VAT recovery, and mileage and per-diem calculations, then syncs transactions into accounting systems such as Sage, Cegid, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Exact Online, and Agicap. Mooncard also runs a developer program that offers API access plus a sandbox environment, though the API reference and OpenAPI are gated behind a developer-portal login and are not publicly discoverable.

providers.name: Arzana
providers.description: Arzana is an AI-powered Office Execution System for US manufacturers and distributors, founded in 2025 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Arzana trains custom models on a factory's historical data and deploys agents that automate back-office work — quoting, estimating, order entry, purchasing, prospecting, outreach, CRM, AP 3-way match, AR tracking, and customer service — alongside a customizable ERP/CRM/MES with every agent pre-installed. Forward-deployed engineers configure each agent per operation; Arzana reports going live in 120 days with 99%+ accuracy. Arzana currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it does publish a /llms.txt for agent discovery.

providers.name: Prolaera
providers.description: Prolaera is a learning and compliance platform built for modern CPAs and accounting firms, combining automated CPE (Continuing Professional Education) tracking, a learning management system (LMS), and a built-in course library so firms can administer training, monitor license and compliance requirements, and manage professional development in one place. Prolaera merged with LCvista and now operates as "Prolaera by LCvista"; the product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application at app.prolaera.com with SSO/SAML 2.0 identity support and SCORM/AICC/xAPI content compatibility. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Prolaera does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Relevize
providers.description: Relevize is an AI-driven partner payments and channel marketing platform that helps B2B companies run Market Development Funds (MDF), SPIFs, and partner incentive programs. It combines virtual and physical expense cards (Magic Cards) with spending controls, AI-powered claims and receipt processing that cuts submission time, automated purchase orders and vendor invoicing, and a compliance engine that validates proof of execution. A companion DemandGen product runs partner-led demand generation campaigns. Customers include Apptio, Atlassian, Chili Piper, New Relic, and WatchGuard. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: EAS Innovations Inc
providers.description: EAS Innovations Inc operates ELEV8, an end-to-end, cloud-based dealer management system (DMS) built for independent auto dealers and automotive finance companies. The platform unifies real-time accounting, inventory management, CRM and desking, loan servicing, payments and collections into a single fully-integrated system. It offers per-seat pricing, user-based access rights, user-level audit logs, whitelisted IP addresses, multi-rooftop access and department-level restrictions, and is delivered as a SaaS web application at app.elev8dms.com. EAS Innovations is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: BrightGo
providers.description: BrightGo is an all-in-one janitorial and commercial-cleaning ERP platform for building service contractors. It unifies field operations, workforce management, and back-office finance in one system: scheduling, GPS-verified time and attendance, inspections and quality assurance, real-time job costing, payroll, and accounting, plus operations business-intelligence dashboards and an in-app employee communication portal. Backed by Index Ventures and Costanoa Ventures, BrightGo serves janitorial companies across the U.S. and Canada. No public developer API or documentation surface has been identified; the product is delivered via web (app.brightgo.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps.

providers.name: CoPlane
providers.description: CoPlane is a San Francisco-based enterprise software company building an AI-native intelligent operations layer for the back office of essential enterprises. The platform combines AI agents with deterministic business rules on a durable workflow engine to automate high-friction, exception-heavy processes across finance, procurement, and operations — including invoice intake, PO matching, vendor onboarding, cash application, billing, collections, bank and account reconciliation, close processes, and variance analysis. CoPlane runs inside the customer's own cloud environment and interoperates with existing enterprise systems (SAP, Workday, Coupa) across Source-to-Pay, Quote-to-Cash, and Record-to-Report workflows without a rip-and-replace migration. Founded in 2024, the company raised a $14M seed round in November 2025 led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Stripe, Optum Ventures, and Terrain. This profile was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; CoPlane does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Dooly
providers.description: Dooly was a connected workspace for revenue teams that improved Salesforce CRM hygiene by syncing meeting notes, pipeline updates, and next steps back into Salesforce automatically. It layered a fast note-taking surface, deal vitals, real-time playbooks, and one-click CRM updates on top of Salesforce so account executives could keep their pipeline clean without manual data entry. Backed by Battery Ventures, Dooly was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. The Dooly platform was shut down on June 30, 2025; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and this profile captures the remaining public surface (website, privacy policy, terms) for the record.

providers.name: Finda
providers.description: Finda (핀다) is a South Korean fintech company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Seoul that operates a licensed online loan-comparison and financial-product marketplace. Through its mobile app and website, Finda lets consumers compare loan products from 76+ financial institutions and 400+ products in about a minute, refinance existing loans ("갈아타기"), aggregate accounts and cards for asset management, run financial calculators (interest, DSR, year-end tax, mortgage eligibility), and monitor and manage their credit. Registered as a loan-brokerage/loan-collection corporation under Korea's Financial Services Act, Finda earns commissions from partner financial institutions rather than charging consumers. It reports 3.47M+ cumulative members and 256T+ won in managed loan assets, and is backed by 500 Global. Finda is a consumer B2C platform and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Hesi
providers.description: Hesi (合思, operated by Beijing Hosi Information Technology Co., Ltd.) is an AI-driven spend and expense management SaaS platform founded in 2014 and backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its cloud platform covers intelligent expense control and reimbursement ("no expense reports needed"), corporate business-travel booking, AI-powered audit and approval, electronic accounting archives, accounts payable/receivable, and business-intelligence analytics. Hesi serves 7,000+ paid enterprises — including large corporations and Fortune 500 firms across China — and runs a PaaS platform with integrations to roughly 1,400 banks. The company operates R&D centers in Beijing, Hangzhou, and Nanchang with 22 direct service offices nationwide.

providers.name: ivymark
providers.description: ivymark was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found that the repo domain ivymark.com 301-redirects in full to www.ivy.co — Ivy, a business-management platform for interior designers (product sourcing, proposals, invoices, client mood boards, project and time tracking, online payments, and reporting), now operated as part of Houzz Pro. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found on either ivymark.com or ivy.co, so no API artifacts could be produced this round; only the identity, verified marketing links, and a live domain-security probe are recorded.

providers.name: NICKL
providers.description: NICKL (Nicklpass) is a subscription management platform that bills itself as "the operating system for subscriptions." It helps organizations govern the digital tools, SaaS subscriptions, and data services their teams use by connecting identity, usage, and procurement data in one place. Capabilities include role-based governance and provisioning, usage intelligence to surface adoption and redundant spend, and coordinated procurement that aggregates demand to negotiate from real usage data. The platform integrates with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Plaid, and applies AI models for insights and pricing optimization. NICKL participated in the Comcast NBCUniversal LIFT Labs Accelerator powered by Techstars. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and hosted control panel but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Prime Meridian
providers.description: Prime Meridian (Prime Meridian Labs) is an AI-powered consumer tax preparation and e-filing service that files federal and state income tax returns for free. Users upload their tax documents, answer a few clarifying questions, and the platform's AI generates a plain-language return covering W-2 employment, self-employment (Schedule C), K-1 partnership income, and multi-state situations, then e-files it with the IRS and state authorities in roughly fifteen minutes. The company is backed by General Catalyst and counts former IRS Commissioner Daniel Werfel among its strategic advisors. It is a consumer web application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Tessera Labs
providers.description: Tessera Labs is an AI-native enterprise software company building a governed, multi-agent AI platform that automates complex ERP and business-system transformations, compressing SAP ECC-to-S/4HANA migrations and broader modernization work from years to weeks. The platform orchestrates data, process, and code changes across ERP, CRM, HCM, and finance systems (SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Oracle) with enterprise governance, full audit trails, and traceability, letting business teams describe requirements in natural language. Founded by AI researchers and enterprise-software veterans and backed by a $60M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz. Tessera Labs currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; it is a sales-led enterprise platform.

providers.name: Wollit
providers.description: Wollit is a UK-based credit-health subscription service (£9.99/month) that helps consumers build and strengthen their credit profile. Authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority for credit-broking activities, Wollit reports rent and subscription payments to Experian, Equifax and TransUnion, and bundles a suite of consumer tools: Rent Reporting, Payment Reporting, an AI credit assistant (Olli), Affordability Boost, Credit Smart lessons, and Credit Wins. It is a consumer-facing fintech app and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Buildertrend
providers.description: Buildertrend is an Omaha, Nebraska-based cloud construction-management platform serving residential home builders, remodelers, and specialty trade contractors. The product consolidates sales (CRM, leads, proposals, contracts, email marketing), project management (schedule, daily logs, selections, change orders, warranties, sub portal, client updates), and financial management (estimates, bids, takeoff, job-costing budgets, bills, purchase orders, invoices, online payments) into a single web and mobile application used by 20,000+ builders. Pricing is custom-quoted by sales rather than published self-serve tiers, with unlimited users and projects on every plan, and the platform integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and other accounting and trade tools through a partner integrations marketplace. The company exposes a REST API at api.buildertrend.com that is gated by partner agreement — endpoints return 401 Unauthorized to the public and there is no open developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API key signup. As a result Buildertrend is profiled here as a non-public (partner-only) API provider; the public surface documented is limited to marketing, support, integrations marketplace, mobile apps, and corporate resources.

providers.name: OneShield
providers.description: OneShield Software provides core insurance platform solutions for property and casualty (P&C) insurers, managing general agents (MGAs), program administrators, and insurance startups. Its two platforms — OneShield Enterprise, a comprehensive cloud/SaaS core suite, and OneShield Market Solutions (OMS), a preconfigured SaaS offering — cover policy administration, billing, claims, rating, product configuration, relationship management, business intelligence, and analytics across more than 90 lines of business. OneShield exposes RESTful and SOAP integration services (XML/JSON) through its Services Designer and OMS API integration suite, but publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI; API access is provisioned to customers and implementation partners. Headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts with offices in India, OneShield is backed by investors including Bain Capital and Earlybird Venture Capital.

providers.name: LearnVest
providers.description: LearnVest was a New York personal-finance company founded in 2009 by Alexa von Tobel and backed by Accel, selling subscription financial planning that paired consumers with CFP professionals alongside budgeting, spending-tracking and goal tools. Northwestern Mutual acquired LearnVest in 2015 for a reported $250 million and terminated the subscription planning service on June 5, 2018, closing all client accounts. The brand was relaunched as a consumer financial-education content site, and learnvest.com today is an archived article library on budgeting, saving, paying off debt and career growth, operated under the Northwestern Mutual brand. LearnVest never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or sandbox, and no developer surface exists today.

providers.name: Numbi
providers.description: Numbi is a tech-enabled accounting and payroll firm for Colombian companies — especially SAS entities, SMBs, and startups. It pairs expert accountants with automation and AI to run monthly bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and DIAN electronic-invoicing compliance. Numbi is a service rather than software or an ERP: it operates on top of a company's existing accounting systems (Siigo and Alegra) instead of replacing them, ingesting documents (PDFs, XMLs, images) and keeping tax calendars and filings current. Founded in Bogotá and backed by Homebrew and Newtopia VC. No public developer API surface is published as of this pass.

providers.name: Olist
providers.description: Olist is a Brazilian commerce technology company headquartered in Curitiba, Paraná, offering an integrated ecosystem of solutions that automate business management for online sellers. Its products include an ERP for inventory, invoicing and order automation, a multi-marketplace Integration Hub (Mercado Livre, TikTok Shop and others), a POS for physical stores, a digital account with Pix payments, shipping and fulfillment (Envios), and storefront creation. Olist exposes robust partner APIs through its Technology Partner program ("Parceiro Tecnológico"), where approved developers receive test credentials and Swagger documentation to build and homologate integrations reaching 60,000+ merchants. The public API surface is gated behind partner registration; no open developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published.

providers.name: Whitespace
providers.description: Whitespace is an AI operating system for wholesale distributors, based in London and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch. The platform connects to a distributor's existing business systems (ERPs such as SAP, NetSuite, Epicor, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and Sage, plus Salesforce, HubSpot, QuickBooks, Gmail and Outlook) to build a model of operations, then deploys self-improving AI agents that automate demand forecasting, inventory replenishment, order entry, quote generation, customer query responses, and accounts payable and receivable. It targets sectors including industrial supplies, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, building materials, foodservice, consumer goods and textiles. Founded by Alex Tung and Leon Yao. As an early-stage company it currently ships a product but publishes no public API, developer documentation or SDK.

providers.name: Credit Karma
providers.description: Credit Karma is an AI-powered personal finance platform founded in 2007 and owned by Intuit since 2020, serving more than 140 million members in the US, UK and Canada. It began as a free credit-score and credit-monitoring destination and has grown into a broad consumer finance marketplace spanning credit cards, personal and auto loans, mortgages, auto and home insurance, banking (checking, savings and credit-builder accounts), tax filing, and identity monitoring. Credit Karma monetizes through personalized recommendations and lead generation rather than a public developer or partner API; it maintains no external consumer-facing API program. It does run an active engineering culture with 29 public open-source repositories on GitHub (Thrift and GraphQL tooling), a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program via HackerOne, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security certifications.

providers.name: Focal Point Procurement Solutions
providers.description: Focal Point is an AI-powered procurement orchestration platform for enterprise procurement teams. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the SaaS platform sits on top of a company's existing S2P and ERP systems to centralize procurement data, intake, and workflows across six core modules: Request Intake Management, Procurement Activity Management, Sourcing Event Management, Supplier Relationship Management, Third-Party Risk Management, and Contract Lifecycle Management. It connects existing systems and data via API integrations, automates tactical no-code workflows, and provides total spend visibility, intelligent intake, and smart routing so procurement teams can focus on strategic work. Focal Point does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal; integrations are delivered through the platform. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kudos
providers.description: Kudos is a consumer credit-card rewards and smart-shopping assistant operated by Kudos Technologies, Inc., founded in 2021 by Tikue Anazodo and Ahmad Ismail. Its browser extension and iOS/Android apps sit at online checkout and recommend which of a shopper's connected cards to use to maximize points, cash back, and card benefits. Kudos Boost pays cashback at 15,000+ stores, redeemable as Amazon gift cards or PayPal cash, and the product bundles free credit-score access, a wallet and credit-management hub, a best-card cheatsheet, weekly insights scores, a Dream Wallet planner, and an Explore card-comparison and Test Drive tool. Kudos is backed by QED Investors. As of July 2026 Kudos publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its only machine-readable public surface is mobile app-association metadata at app.joinkudos.com.

providers.name: PDI Technologies (fka PDI Software)
providers.description: PDI Technologies (formerly PDI Software) is a global provider of software and data solutions for the convenience retail and wholesale petroleum industries, serving 200,000+ customers across 60+ countries. Its portfolio spans PDIQ (an AI foundation for convenience and fuel operations), PDI Enterprise wholesale petroleum software, ERP and back-office systems, POS and store systems, logistics, loyalty marketing, fuel and mobility payments, an offer network, insights and analytics, cybersecurity (PDI Security and Network Solutions, formerly Echosat), and the consumer app GasBuddy. PDI is backed by Insight Partners and has grown through acquisitions including P97 Networks. The company exposes no public self-serve developer/API portal; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Xfactor.io
providers.description: Xfactor.io is an AI-powered revenue operations platform founded by Mike Carpenter and backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its Growth AI engine, together with the Xfactor Central, OpenInsights, and Simulation products, builds a live digital twin of a company's go-to-market operations — connecting CRM, pipeline, usage, and financial data so revenue teams can test decisions through simulation before rolling them out. The platform is delivered as a closed B2B SaaS application (app.xfactor.io) and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or client SDKs; security posture is documented on a Secureframe trust center with a SOC 2 Type II attestation.

providers.name: Craftable
providers.description: Craftable is hospitality's back-office software platform for restaurants, bars, hotels, and resorts, originally known for its Bevager and Foodager products, that connects purchasing, inventory, recipes, and accounts payable with accounting and sales data. Its suite spans Intelligent Ordering (eProcurement), AP Automation with Invoice AI, Inventory and Recipe Management, and Daily Actionable Insights, plus AI features such as Operator AI and the Crafty in-app assistant. Craftable is SOC 2 compliant and SSO-capable, with more than 1,000 POS, EDI, and vendor/API integrations spanning systems such as Toast, Square, Lightspeed, Clover, SpotOn, TouchBistro, Aloha by NCR Voyix, Restaurant365, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, and Xero. Craftable does not publish a public self-service developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; integrations are delivered through its implementation team during onboarding, and API access to a connected platform is provisioned by requesting a scoped API key from that platform's support team.

providers.name: Northstar
providers.description: Northstar is an employer-sponsored financial wellness benefit that helps employees understand, manage, and get the most out of their total compensation and personal finances. Delivered as a workplace benefit (offered by employers to their workforce), Northstar pairs financial guidance with tools for budgeting, saving, equity/compensation planning, and overall money management. The company is a fintech provider backed by GGV Capital. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, Northstar publishes a marketing site, blog, and legal pages, but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface — its product is consumed as an employee benefit, not as a developer API.

providers.name: Proper
providers.description: Proper (proper.ai) is an AI-powered, full-service property-management accounting and bookkeeping provider serving property managers, asset managers, and real estate developers. Rather than shipping software, Proper delivers a trained accounting team supported by automation to handle accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank reconciliations, month-end close, and financial reporting, integrating with existing property-management systems such as AppFolio, Buildium, and RentManager. Founded in the property-management space in 2017, the company is backed by QED Investors, Redpoint Ventures, MetaProp, Expa, and Bling Capital. As of this enrichment pass Proper exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company record.

providers.name: Simplywise
providers.description: SimplyWise is an AI-powered admin-automation platform for contractors, tradespeople, and small business owners. Its consumer mobile and web apps bundle a receipt scanner and expense organizer, an automatic mileage tracker for tax deductions, an AI-powered job/cost estimator, and an AI receptionist that answers inbound calls and messages. The company reports serving more than 1.2 million business owners. SimplyWise is a fintech-adjacent SMB productivity product backed by QED Investors; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, or developer portal — the apps are consumer-facing only.

providers.name: Suplari
providers.description: Suplari is an enterprise procurement intelligence platform that goes beyond spend analytics, using AI to clean, classify, and unify fragmented spend data across ERP, P2P, and spreadsheet sources. It delivers spend analytics, value orchestration, savings tracking, contract intelligence, and ESG intelligence, alongside procurement-specific AI agents (Suplari Worker, Assistant, and AI Studio) that integrate with SAP, Oracle, Workday, Coupa, Databricks, Snowflake, and Microsoft. Suplari was acquired by Microsoft in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Taxscouts
providers.description: TaxScouts is a UK online tax-return and Self Assessment service that pairs individuals, sole traders, landlords and investors with accredited accountants to prepare, review and file their taxes with HMRC for a flat fee. Founded in London, TaxScouts was acquired by Taxfix and its taxscouts.com domain now redirects to taxfix.com/en-uk. The service is a consumer-facing web and mobile product with pricing tiers for one-off filing, optimisation with HMRC audit protection, and year-round accountant support. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation; this record captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cardinal
providers.description: Cardinal is an AI platform for precision outbound sales — it markets itself as "revenue agents for high-growth companies" — built for go-to-market teams that want outbound to run as one engine instead of a stack of disconnected tools. Its agents build and refresh account lists from signals, monitor what prospects post and engage with, generate personalized snippets, and orchestrate end-to-end email and LinkedIn plays, while capturing inbound from website visitors, product signups and ad impressions. The company is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company founded by Devishi Jha and Jianna Liu, based in San Francisco, and names Mintlify, Deepgram, Greptile, Giga and Luminai among its customers. Cardinal moved its primary web presence from trycardinal.ai to trycardinal.com during 2026: https://trycardinal.ai/ now HTTP 301s to https://www.trycardinal.com/ and the former deep pages on the .ai domain (/company, /product) return 404, though the company still runs its customer application, its email and its analytics identity on trycardinal.ai. The product is sold as half-software and half-service ("we wire into your existing stack and build agents around plays that already work for you"), delivered through a customer app at app.trycardinal.ai behind a Stytch login, with a Calendly GTM chat as the only publicly reachable entry point. It reads from and writes back to customer CRMs and says it adds a new integration every two weeks, but names none of them publicly and publishes no outbound API of its own: across four hosts on two domains this pass found no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, MCP server, agent card, webhook catalog, SDK, CLI, developer portal or documentation site. docs.trycardinal.ai does not resolve in DNS, api.trycardinal.ai is a dangling custom domain whose Render origin answers x-render-routing: no-server, and every /api/* path on the customer app returns HTTP 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}.

providers.name: CoinTracker
providers.description: CoinTracker is a cryptocurrency portfolio tracker and crypto tax software that connects a user's exchange accounts and blockchain wallets to automatically track holdings, calculate cost basis and capital gains, and generate tax reports and IRS forms. It supports a large catalog of exchanges, wallets, and cryptocurrencies, and offers tax-loss harvesting, performance tracking, and integrations with consumer tax-filing products. For developers and partners, CoinTracker publishes a first-party JavaScript SDK (@cointracker/tax-kit) for supplying cost-basis data; its core HTTP API is offered through enterprise and partner integrations rather than a self-serve public developer program. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from publicly discoverable surfaces (npm, GitHub, status page, DNS/TLS).

providers.name: Cedar
providers.description: Cedar is a healthcare financial technology company whose patient financial experience platform unifies billing, payments, insurance coverage, and support for health systems, hospitals, and clinician-services groups. Its products include Cedar Pay (pre-visit, post-visit, and financing patient payments), Cedar Cover (benefits and financial assistance, including Medicaid enrollment), Cedar Support (AI-powered patient support and call-center automation via Kora AI), and Cedar Intelligence (a proprietary AI system for personalized patient engagement). Cedar reports having served over 50 million patients and processed billions of dollars in patient payments. The company is backed by a16z, Founders Fund, QED Investors, and SV Angel. Cedar publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or GitHub organization; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security-posture surface.

providers.name: Stampli
providers.description: Stampli is an AI-driven accounts payable and procure-to-pay automation platform (invoice capture, coding, approvals, vendor management, payments, and corporate cards) that stays aligned to a company's ERP as the system of record. Stampli does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer API or developer portal. What Stampli markets as its "API" is a set of pre-built, in-house cloud-to-cloud ERP integrations (plus on-premises "Bridge" connectors and file-based sync) that Stampli operates on the customer's behalf to sync master data - invoices, vendors, purchase orders, GL accounts, locations/entities, and approvals - between Stampli and 70+ ERPs such as NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Oracle, and Acumatica. Access is gated behind a sales/onboarding relationship; there is no documented public REST/GraphQL/WebSocket surface, no self-service authentication, no OpenAPI reference, and no published developer documentation as of this catalog entry. Integrations are configured by Stampli during onboarding rather than by third-party developers against an open API.

providers.name: Donnerstag Ai
providers.description: Donnerstag.ai (Donnerstag.ai Technologies GmbH) is a Frankfurt-based enterprise fintech building an AI Reconciliation Layer for enterprise finance. Its platform automates financial reconciliation at the line-item level across accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank, and intercompany flows, adapting to each customer's systems, data sources, workflows, and roles. The stated goal is 100% line-item coverage at T+0 so the financial close becomes a confirmation rather than a month-end scramble, with an immutable audit trail for GoBD, IFRS, SOX, and BEPS. The company serves logistics, payment service providers, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, human resources, and construction, is EU-hosted in Frankfurt, and is founded by Barbaros Ozbugutu and Volkan Ozkan and backed by Speedinvest. As a solution-and-services provider it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs.

providers.name: Groyyo
providers.description: Groyyo is a Gurugram, India based B2B manufacturing and supply-chain company for the fashion, apparel and lifestyle industry, founded in July 2021 by Subin Mitra and Pratik Tiwari. It connects global brands with a vetted network of small and mid-sized Asian factories and gives those factories production software — sales-order management, bill-of-materials creation, production tracking, quality control and business reporting — delivered as the Groyyo and Groyyo + mobile apps and an internal factory ERP rather than as a public developer platform. The company also runs sourcing, fabric and consulting lines, plus RFQ and supplier-KYC intake on its own website. As of August 2026 Groyyo publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: NerdWallet
providers.description: NerdWallet is a personal finance company that helps consumers make smarter money decisions across credit cards, banking, investing, loans, mortgages, insurance, and taxes. Through its website and mobile apps it offers comparison tools, product marketplaces, educational content, and free credit-score monitoring. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, NerdWallet is publicly traded (NASDAQ: NRDS) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of ivp. As of this enrichment pass NerdWallet publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or well-known API discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Bayapay Sdn Bhd
providers.description: BayaPay Sdn Bhd is a Malaysian fintech (incorporated 2021, registration 202101021154 / 1421454-H, based in Subang Jaya, Selangor) building programmable, permission-based business and vehicle expense management on an open-loop prepaid Mastercard. Its flagship BayaFuel FuelFleet programme gives fleet operators, SMBs, corporate teams and gig workers real-time spend controls, customizable limits, fraud deterrence and digitized expense tracking across fuel, travel and operational spend. The reloadable prepaid card is issued under license from Instapay Technologies Sdn Bhd (a Bank Negara Malaysia e-money issuer and Mastercard Asia/Pacific licensee), and BayaPay is one of the first Full Functional Open-Loop payment solutions in the APAC region. A 500 Global portfolio company. The public site is Wix-powered and exposes an agent-accessible llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint; no bespoke BayaPay developer/payments API is publicly documented at this time.

providers.name: Souqalmal
providers.description: Souqalmal was a UAE-based personal-finance comparison marketplace that let consumers across the GCC compare and apply for credit cards, personal loans, bank accounts, and insurance products online. The brand has since transitioned to Yabi (yabimoney.com), an AI-powered financial coaching application offering personalized guidance, budgeting tools, spending tracking, credit checks, and financial-education content on iOS and Android. Backed by 500 Global. The souqalmal.com domain now permanently redirects to yabimoney.com. No public developer, API, or partner-integration surface is currently published.

providers.name: SpryPoint
providers.description: SpryPoint is a cloud-based customer service and operations software provider for utilities, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, Canada. Its platform modernizes the meter-to-cash lifecycle for water & sewer, electric, and gas utilities across North America through an integrated suite of modules: SpryCIS (customer information system), SpryEngage (omnichannel customer portal), SpryWallet (payment processing), SpryMobile MFS (field service orders), SpryMobile WOAM (work order and asset management), SpryBackflow (backflow compliance), and SpryIDM (interval data management). The company serves 100+ utility clients, employs 285+ people, is SOC 2 audited, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Insight Partners. SpryPoint publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; integrations are delivered through partnership engagements rather than a self-service API.

providers.name: Tiyaro
providers.description: Tiyaro is an enterprise AI company whose product, DeepQuery, replicates complete business processes as AI agents that can be described in plain English. Rather than rules engines or brittle integration workflows, DeepQuery uses LLMs combined with enterprise-specific product and customer data to identify a solution strategy and execute it across multiple steps using built-in tools. Its flagship application targets customer support and IT service desks - an "IT SuperAgent" trained on hundreds of third-party product procedures that recommends and executes resolution steps for incoming tickets - alongside revenue-operations and sales/marketing automation use cases. The company was founded by a team that previously built an edge software stack for hosting AI applications, and is backed by General Catalyst. Tiyaro goes to market as an enterprise product engaged through a book-a-demo motion rather than a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Gravy
providers.description: Gravy is a local-first, AI-powered personal finance workspace that runs on the Mac. It connects every bank, credit card, and investment account, automatically categorizes every transaction, and lets people ask plain-language questions about their money while keeping the data on their own device for privacy. Gravy focuses on optimizing spending, surfacing savings, tracking investments and recurring subscriptions, and automating tedious money tasks for both individuals and small businesses. It is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company. Gravy is a consumer application and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: LegalZoom
providers.description: LegalZoom.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: LZ) is a Glendale, California online legal technology and services company that helps individuals and small businesses create legal documents and form, run, and grow their businesses without necessarily hiring an attorney. Founded in 1999, LegalZoom offers business formation services (LLC, S-Corp, C-Corp, nonprofit, DBA), registered agent service, EIN/tax ID filing, annual report and compliance filings, business licenses, virtual mail, business banking partnerships, trademark registration, and ongoing bookkeeping and tax services through LZ Books and LZ Tax. On the personal side it provides wills, living trusts, power of attorney, prenuptial agreements, and a partner-driven divorce flow via Divorce.com. Customers access an attorney-network legal advice subscription (LZ Legal Services / business advisory plans) connecting them to independent attorneys for consultations and document review. LegalZoom went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (ticker LZ) and serves customers primarily in the United States. The company's revenue model is transactional document and formation fees plus recurring subscription services (registered agent, compliance, attorney advice, bookkeeping). LegalZoom does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations (e.g. divorce.com, banking partners, accounting partners) appear to be private commercial arrangements rather than self-service developer APIs. The legalzoom.com web app calls a set of internal hosts under apigw.legalzoom.com (checkout-graphql-public-api, customer, experimentation, revv, attorney-state-service, site-search) but these are first-party and not documented for third-party use.

providers.name: Solomon
providers.description: Solomon (Solomon AI, solomontax.ai) is an agentic AI platform for tax preparation aimed at accounting firms, automating the preparation of review-ready individual 1040 returns for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. The system interprets K-1/K-3 footnotes, applies multi-state SALT rules to K-1s, reconciles rental and real estate investments, analyzes brokerage statements for foreign income, and produces workpapers and audit trails, positioning itself to replace legacy tools such as SurePrep and K1x. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Moneyfellows
providers.description: Money Fellows is an Egyptian fintech, founded in 2018 and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt, that digitizes the traditional rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA / "gam'eya") model as a mobile app. Members join Money Circles to save together and access interest-free funds on flexible 6, 10, or 12-month plans of up to 1.2M EGP, and can spend and save through a prepaid Money Fellows Mastercard. The service is Sharia-compliant (Official Fatwa No. 46205 from the Egyptian Dar Al Iftaa) and has served millions of users while raising roughly $60M across its funding rounds, including a 2025 Series B first close backed by investors such as Partech. Money Fellows is a consumer mobile application and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Personal Capital
providers.description: Personal Capital is a digital wealth management and personal finance company, now operating as an Empower company, that pairs free online money-management tools with paid registered-investment-adviser services. Its Personal Capital / Empower Personal Dashboard app lets individuals link bank, brokerage, retirement, and loan accounts to track net worth, analyze investment fees, plan for retirement, and manage cash flow, while Personal Capital Advisors Corporation (an SEC-registered investment adviser) offers human financial advisors and managed portfolios for clients who link at least $100,000 in investable assets. Personal Capital was acquired by Empower Retirement (Great-West Lifeco / Power Corporation) in 2020. The company is consumer-facing and, as of this enrichment pass, does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Powerup Money
providers.description: PowerUp Money is an India-based mutual fund advisory app that helps retail investors select, monitor, and rebalance their mutual fund portfolios. It is operated by a SEBI-registered Investment Advisor (RIA No. INA000019798) and BSE member (IA-BSE Membership No. 2465), and describes itself as "India's trusted Mutual Fund Advisory App" serving 900,000+ investors. Consumer-facing features include portfolio performance analysis, fund recommendations (start/pause/exit SIP guidance), monthly portfolio reports, and Elite membership tools such as Power Rank fund selection, Rank Trends monitoring, and Power Rebalancing for tax-efficient quarterly adjustments. It is distributed as iOS and Android mobile apps; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company.

providers.name: SAGARIS
providers.description: SAGARIS is an agentic revenue operating system for B2B sales teams — CRM, dialer, inbox, SMS, social, an AI receptionist and an AI coach in one system, where AI agents act on the pipeline under approval gates and an audit trail rather than only reporting on it. Pricing is public at 499 USD per founding seat per month, with a custom Enterprise plan. SAGARIS describes a Model Context Protocol endpoint that lets an AI client read the CRM, sequences and workspace with a workspace API key, read-only and scoped to the workspace.

providers.name: Sav Technologies Limited
providers.description: Sav Technologies Limited operates Sav (sav.money), a UAE-based intelligent financial platform that lets users track, save, invest, and grow their wealth across accounts. Sav offers a suite of consumer products including Gold (physical gold investment from AED 10), MyMoney (financial management and savings), Card (a prepaid card with cashback), Wealth (investing), Sav Pro (premium membership), and an upcoming Credit product. Sav describes itself as extending the APIs and technology components of licensed financial services providers to its users. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Sav publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Finom
providers.description: Finom is a European fintech headquartered in Amsterdam that provides business banking, invoicing, and financial management for entrepreneurs, freelancers, and SMEs. Operating as a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), Finom offers multi-currency business accounts, 24/7 SEPA Instant and SWIFT payments, direct debits, Visa Business physical and virtual cards with up to 3% cashback, compliant e-invoicing (ZUGFeRD, XRechnung), and integrations with accounting platforms such as DATEV, Lexware, sevDesk, Xero, and QuickBooks. It serves Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands with region-specific tooling. Finom does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public discovery, security, and operational surface (llms.txt, security.txt / Intigriti VDP, domain security, status page).

providers.name: Jupiter Money
providers.description: Jupiter Money is a Bengaluru-based Indian digital banking app (neobank) operated by Amica Financial Technologies Private Limited. Founded in 2019 by Jitendra Gupta, Jupiter delivers a consumer "money app" experience that bundles savings and salary accounts, UPI payments, co-branded credit cards, personal loans, mutual funds, digital gold, fixed and recurring deposits, insurance, and a Jewels rewards program into a single mobile application. Jupiter is itself not a bank — it operates as a fintech marketplace and Loan Service Provider on top of regulated partners. Federal Bank is the primary banking partner for savings, salary, and deposit products, with CSB Bank powering the Edge+ and Edge RuPay credit cards and Federal Bank the Edge Federal VISA card. Lending is provided through partners including Amica Finance Private Limited and Kisetsu Saison Finance, with mutual funds through AIAPL and digital gold through MMTC-PAMP. The product is consumer facing and distributed via the Android and iOS apps; Jupiter does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. All integrations with banks, NBFCs, NPCI/UPI rails, card networks, and depositories are private business-to-business arrangements rather than an open API program.

providers.name: Khatabook
providers.description: Khatabook is a Bengaluru, India-based fintech company building a mobile-first digital ledger ("bahi khata") and business management platform for India's 6.3 crore-strong MSME sector. Founded in 2018 by Ravish Naresh, Vaibhav Kalpe, Dhanesh Kumar, and Jaideep Poonia, its flagship Khatabook Android app lets shopkeepers and small merchants record credit transactions ("udhaar"), send free WhatsApp/SMS payment reminders, collect payments via UPI and QR codes, and generate ledger statements — replacing the paper notebook ("khata") historically used across Indian retail. The app has been downloaded over 50 million times and is offered in 13+ Indian languages. Khatabook's portfolio also includes Cashbook (cash-in/cash-out tracking), Pagarkhata/Pagarbook (staff attendance and salary management), Biz Analyst (Tally mobility for accountants, acquired in 2021 for ~$10M), and a suite of GST, EMI, income tax, payroll, and loan calculators. The company has raised roughly $190M across seed through Series C from Sequoia Capital, Tencent, DST Global, GGV Capital, Y Combinator, B Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, and angels including MS Dhoni, valuing it around $600M. Khatabook monetizes via SMB lending tie-ups, premium business tools, and adjacent fintech distribution. The Khatabook GitHub organization (verified, owns khatabook.com) exists but has no public repositories, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or partner program — its surface is a consumer/SMB mobile app rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Topline Pro
providers.description: Topline Pro is an AI-powered business management platform for local and home service professionals in the United States — contractors, landscapers, painters, roofers, cleaners, and other owner-operated service companies. It provides AI-generated websites, local marketing and online discovery, lead capture with automated follow-up, AI-assisted customer communication, appointment and job scheduling, and invoicing with automated payment collection. Topline Pro is backed by Forerunner Ventures and Northzone. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDK, gRPC, AsyncAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface; it does publish an llms.txt at its marketing domain that describes the platform for AI agents.

providers.name: Thndr
providers.description: Thndr is an Egyptian investment and brokerage mobile app that lets retail users open a regulated brokerage account and invest in Egyptian Exchange (EGX) stocks, US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, and IPOs from their phone. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Cairo, Thndr is licensed by Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and registered with the Egyptian Exchange as a brokerage, positioning itself as a low-cost, mobile-first gateway to the capital markets across Egypt and the wider MENA region. The company raised a $20M Series A in 2022 led by Tiger Global with participation from Prosus Ventures and others, and has been recognized among Forbes Middle East's top fintech companies. Thndr's product surface is a consumer investing app (iOS, Android, and a web account-access portal) with an educational Learn hub and a customer support center; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: Drahim Holdings
providers.description: Drahim (دراهم) is a Saudi personal-finance and automated-investment fintech, founded in Riyadh in 2021 by Sultan Alkhayal and Yasser Alshurihi. Its mobile app uses open banking to aggregate a user's bank accounts into one view, enriches and auto-categorizes transactions (2.5B+ processed), and offers auto-savings, Zakat calculation, and Sharia-compliant robo-advisory portfolios spanning 40+ funds across Saudi and global equities, real estate, and commodities. Drahim is licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) for open-banking/payment services and by the Capital Market Authority (CMA) for investment management; it was backed by Y Combinator and 500 Global, and Al Rajhi Bank acquired a 65% majority stake in 2024. Drahim is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and product identity plus live domain-security posture. Consumer surfaces include the iOS and Android apps and a business platform.

providers.name: FloatMe
providers.description: FloatMe is a US fintech app offering interest-free cash advances ("Floats") to help members bridge income gaps between paychecks — new eligible members can request up to $50 and existing members up to $100, with no credit check and no reporting to credit bureaus. Beyond advances, FloatMe provides spending tracking and insights, low-balance alerts to help avoid overdraft fees, income and cash-flow forecasting, and an exclusive marketplace of deals on everyday essentials. The service runs on a $4.99/month membership, with optional instant-transfer fees. FloatMe operates a consumer mobile app and website; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Grubmarket
providers.description: GrubMarket is a food technology company founded in 2014 that digitally transforms the American food supply chain across the U.S. and Canada. It operates a B2B wholesale eCommerce marketplace connecting buyers to thousands of food products, an AI-powered ERP and warehouse-management software suite (WholesaleWare) for food distributors and growers, and a direct-to-consumer farm-fresh food delivery service. Backed by Battery Ventures, GGV Capital, and Y Combinator, GrubMarket was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass GrubMarket publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: B&L Information Systems
providers.description: B&L Information Systems, LLC is a metalcasting-focused enterprise resource planning (ERP) software company founded more than 50 years ago and headquartered in Bridgman, Michigan. Its flagship product, Odyssey ERP, is a cloud-based ERP purpose-built for foundries, die casters, and investment casters, spanning manufacturing, sales, inventory, quality, finance, and data analytics. B&L pairs the software with implementation, consulting, data-conversion, training, and support services tailored to the metalcasting industry. The company is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, B&L does not publish a public developer portal, REST API documentation, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Knowify
providers.description: Knowify is a New York-based construction management SaaS for trade contractors (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, painting, remodeling, concrete, excavation), covering the full job lifecycle from bidding through payment on a single platform. The product spans project execution (estimating, proposals and contracts, change orders, RFIs and submittals, scheduling, daily logs, document and photo management), service work (dispatch, invoicing, payments, field operations, asset and inventory management), and financial management (AIA billing, job costing, prevailing wage, purchase orders, expenses, WIP and reporting). Knowify is positioned as the official construction software partner of QuickBooks Online and offers deep two-way sync with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Intuit Enterprise Suite, QuickBooks Payroll, QuickBooks Payments, and QuickBooks Time, alongside native integrations with CompanyCam, Billd, Lumber, eBacon, and AIA Contract Documents. Third-party automation is available via Zapier. Pricing starts at $99/month (Core), $249/month (Advanced), and custom Enterprise, with paid add-ons for Service Pro, Live Equipment Tracking (FleetSharp), AI Dashcams, and Tool Tracking. Knowify does not publish a public REST API, webhooks specification, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; programmatic access for third parties is limited to Zapier and the QuickBooks ecosystem.

providers.name: OnPlan
providers.description: OnPlan (onplan.co) publishes guidance and content on project controls, budgeting, and forecasting for organizations managing projects and capital programs. The site covers cost planning and budget management, risk management frameworks, change control procedures, earned value management, and benefit realization tracking across infrastructure, construction, and technology projects. It is presented as an informational and educational resource rather than a self-service SaaS platform: at the time of enrichment the public surface consists of a homepage, a blog of dated articles, a contact page, a privacy policy, and a sitemap, with no developer portal, public API, documentation, pricing, sign-up/login, or terms-of-service pages exposed. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from the live site; no machine-readable API artifacts were found to harvest.

providers.name: Numos
providers.description: Numos is an AI agent platform that automates accounting and financial planning & analysis (FP&A) workflows for finance teams. It layers above existing ERPs with "zero disruption to your current architecture" and learns a company's accounting policies and entity structures to run strategic FP&A and variance analysis, continuous month-end close, accounts payable orchestration, and accounts receivable / revenue recognition. Numos is headquartered in San Mateo, California and is backed by General Catalyst. Its product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.numosai.com); the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio and enriched from Numos's public web surface.

providers.name: Craftview
providers.description: Craftview Software GmbH is a Frankfurt-headquartered European software group that builds ERP and project-management software for the skilled trades. Formed as a buy-and-build platform, Craftview operates a portfolio of long-established regional ERP brands — C'FLUIDE, ES2000, EXTRABAT, GILDE, KS21, MOSER, OSD, PLENION, RITA BOSSE and WINWORKER — serving green industries, construction-related trades, technical services and specialized crafts across Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and France. The group reports 25,000+ active customers, 330+ employees and 11 locations across 41 key European regions. Craftview publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API definitions; its software is sold and delivered per brand as on-premise and cloud ERP for trade businesses.

providers.name: Kos
providers.description: Kos (Kosai, Inc.) builds what it calls the world's first virtual finance employee: an AI agent given its own workstation, org identity, software licenses, RBAC and audit logs, which completes finance and back-office workflows for capital- and inventory-heavy operators across datacenters, defense, energy, long-lead equipment, space and contracting.
