Kos reviews pay applications and vendor invoices line-by-line against GMP contracts, catching missing backup, overbills and calculation errors; generates, routes and closes out purchase orders inside a customer's ERP; and is taught new workflows over screenshare like a new hire. It is reached over email, Slack, Teams, phone and Zoom rather than through a UI, app or public API. Founded by Tanuj and Mani, who met as graduate researchers at Stanford under Sachin Katti; backed by 8VC, XYZ Ventures, MVP Ventures and Launch, with advisors including former Equinix CFO Keith Taylor. Headquartered in San Francisco, California.

providers.name: MaxRewards
providers.description: MaxRewards is a consumer credit-card rewards app for iOS and Android that helps people manage their credit cards and maximize the rewards they earn on everyday spending. It links a user's cards, tracks spending, automatically activates card-linked offers, surfaces personalized card recommendations, compares credit cards by rewards rate and welcome offer, and monitors credit scores — all in one place — so cardholders earn more cash back and points with less manual effort. MaxRewards is an Atlanta-based fintech backed by Techstars. It is a consumer product company: it publishes a public marketing site and an internal app API, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Goin
providers.description: Goin is a European consumer fintech platform, backed by Anthemis and based in Barcelona, Spain, that helps more than 700,000 users across Europe grow their money and spend less. The app bundles automated savings (fixed daily, weekly or monthly rules and goal-based portfolios), investing, buying and selling of cryptocurrencies, cashback and rewards at hundreds of online and physical stores, gift cards and coupons, and a browser extension that surfaces discounts while shopping. Bank accounts are connected securely under Europe's PSD2 open banking regulation, and a referral program rewards users for inviting friends. Goin is a business-to-consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer program, API, or documentation surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks Goin as a portfolio lead and captures its public web, help, and legal presence.

providers.name: Modak
providers.description: Modak (Modak Makers) is a US consumer fintech that offers a family money-management app built around a free Visa debit card for kids and teens. Parents can assign chores and automate allowance, set savings goals with reward boosts, and use co-parenting tools, gift links, ATM access, bill splitting, and spending controls such as instant alerts, card freeze, and biometric security. Kids earn MBX reward points through daily steps and challenges that convert to pocket money, so they learn to spend, save, and manage money in real life. Modak is delivered as a mobile consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by GGV Capital.

providers.name: Procuri
providers.description: Procuri (procuri.ai) presents itself as an AI-powered procurement automation platform that uses specialized AI agents to discover and vet suppliers, optimize contract negotiation and pricing, monitor policy and regulatory compliance, and assess supplier and market risk for enterprise procurement teams. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass the public site publishes no developer/API surface (no docs, developer, API-reference, or OpenAPI pages resolve).

providers.name: Trezy
providers.description: Trezy is a Franco-Dutch fintech SaaS (Trezy SAS, founded 2021 in Paris by Quentin Lacointa) offering AI-driven cash flow management for small and medium businesses across Europe, the US, and Canada. It connects to 2,000+ banks via PSD2/Open Banking to deliver real-time cash position, automatic AI transaction categorization, 95%-accurate 12-month cash flow forecasting, real-time P&L, 27+ financial KPIs, supplier cost analysis, and OCR-based document management from a single platform starting at a free tier. Trezy also offers dedicated plans for external CFOs (DAF) and accounting firms, and integrates with QuickBooks Online and Pennylane. Backed by Seedcamp and Playfair Capital (with Kima Ventures and Discovery Ventures) in a €3M seed round. Trezy publishes an llms.txt corpus and an /.well-known/ai-plugin.json manifest but does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Net Worth
providers.description: netWorth (networth.mx) is a Mexico City fintech founded in 2016 and a 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 10 company that helps individuals plan and manage retirement in Mexico. It specializes in Planes Personales de Retiro (PPR) and long-term savings and investment plans, combining human financial advisors (asesores) with digital tools such as retirement calculators and simulators, and commercializes plans backed by insurers and financial institutions such as Allianz and Skandia (Optimaxx Plus). The consumer product surfaces are a Webflow marketing site plus a client app at retiro.networth.mx and an authenticated portal at api.networth.mx; there is no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program at this time.

providers.name: Atlas
providers.description: Atlas is an AI implementation partner built for independent accounting firms, deploying supervised, firm-specific AI "junior accountants" that automate repetitive, data-intensive workflows such as client onboarding, follow-ups, bookkeeping, compliance, and financial reporting while keeping human accountants in control of every decision and client relationship. Founded by Arpit Maheshwari (CEO) and Jagmal Singh (CTO) and co-led by Accel and Stellaris with Felicis participation, Atlas raised a $6M seed round in 2026 to scale its network of partner firms across North America. Atlas is currently a services-led AI company and publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Crete Professionals Alliance
providers.description: Crete Professionals Alliance (rebranded in 2025 as "Current", current.co) is a growth platform for independent accounting firms, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The alliance provides member firms with technology, talent, capital, and strategy to compete at enterprise scale, spanning 48 partner firms across 39 states and 3 countries with more than 2,000 employees. Service lines include accounting, advisory, audit and attest, client accounting services, and tax. This is a professional services / accounting company, not a developer-facing API provider: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. The record is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph coverage of Bessemer holdings.

providers.name: Excelergy
providers.description: Excelergy is a global provider of high-performance retail energy billing and revenue management software, now part of Harris Computer. Its flagship product, RevenueManager, is a cloud-based, meter-to-cash billing platform used by competitive energy retailers across more than 200 jurisdictions in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. RevenueManager handles residential, commercial, industrial, and wholesale billing across multiple commodities (electricity, natural gas, water, heat, and sewage), supporting complex tariff and pricing models, customer lifecycle management, smart-meter and time-of-use pricing, and built-in Salesforce CRM integration. The platform exposes APIs for connectivity with third-party systems and access to data held in the RevenueManager database. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; Excelergy publishes a corporate marketing site and a customer support portal but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Fold
providers.description: Fold (NASDAQ: FLD) is a bitcoin financial services company founded in 2014 and based in Atlanta, Georgia, billed as the first publicly traded bitcoin financial services company. Fold makes it easy for individuals and businesses to earn, save, and use bitcoin through consumer products including the Fold App, the Fold Bitcoin Rewards Credit Card, the Fold Debit Card, and the Fold Bitcoin Gift Card marketplace, paying real bitcoin rewards (not points or a proprietary token) on everyday purchases and bill payments. Bitcoin custody and Lightning Network payouts are powered by partners such as BitGo and OpenNode. Fold is a consumer-facing fintech application and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tilt
providers.description: Tilt is a consumer fintech mobile app for building and rebuilding credit. It offers cash advances of up to $400, a line of credit with potential limit increases, and three credit cards (Essentials, Motion, and Engage), evaluating applicants from real-time bank-linked financial data rather than credit history alone. The app adds credit-score monitoring with personalized tips, customizable budgeting and spend tracking, AI-assisted automatic savings, and on-time-payment rewards, for an $8/month subscription after a 14-day trial. Tilt is a consumer application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Kaizntree Inc.
providers.description: Kaizntree is a New York-based operations platform for growth-stage consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands, giving multi-channel manufacturers and sellers a single system to run purchasing, inventory, sales, fulfillment, production, and lot-level traceability. Its two products are Kaizntree OS, a cloud ERP that centralizes stock across raw materials, intermediate goods, packaging, finished and bundled products with COGS, margin, multi-location, batch/expiry and audit-ready records, and JP, an ERP-agnostic AI operations assistant that automates high-volume workflows such as purchase-order processing, reporting, data synchronization, and OTIF tracking. Kaizntree integrates with sales channels (including Shopify), accounting, WMS, and fulfillment platforms. Backed by 500 Global (seed, 2022), it operates on usage-based pricing. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Kaizntree publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Seafair
providers.description: Seafair is an AI-native ERP platform for maritime operations, unifying crew management, HSQE and regulatory compliance, technical maintenance (planned maintenance systems and defect tracking), and accounting into a single system for shipping companies and ship managers. Its AI compliance engine performs document search and framework reviews (such as DryBMS and TMSA) and embeds AI assistance directly into operational workflows. Seafair markets itself as API-first with fast ERP integrations, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition. Seafair is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SoLo Funds
providers.description: SoLo Funds is a Techstars-backed, Los Angeles fintech that operates a community-driven peer-to-peer lending marketplace delivered as a consumer mobile app for iOS and Android. Members request small, short-term loans that other members choose to fund, with borrowers offering an optional tip and donation rather than mandated interest, positioning the platform as a member-to-member alternative to payday and overdraft borrowing. SoLo Funds is a consumer financial-services product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only publicly reachable operational surface is a hosted status page.

providers.name: Truvio
providers.description: Truvio is a unified software portfolio company providing intelligent, AI-driven automation solutions for Microsoft Dynamics 365 across finance, operations, Business Central, and commerce. Its practitioner-built solutions span Accounts Payable automation (ExFlow), Banking & Treasury automation (SKSoft), eCommerce and Product Information Management (DynamicWeb), and Project & Production Management (Axtension), embedding expertise directly into Dynamics 365 to help organizations close the ERP value gap. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: EY
providers.description: One of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit, tax, consulting, and advisory services. Operates in over 150 countries helping businesses navigate regulatory and strategic challenges, and runs proprietary technology platforms such as EY Helix (analytics), EY Atlas (research), and EY Canvas (audit) for internal and engagement use.

providers.name: Brightwheel
providers.description: Brightwheel (mybrightwheel.com) is an all-in-one childcare and early education management platform used by childcare centers, preschools, and early-learning programs to run daily operations - attendance and check-in, digital daily sheets, tuition billing and payments, enrollment and admissions, staff/timecards, classroom (room) management, learning assessments, and real-time parent messaging and photo/video sharing. As of this catalog entry, Brightwheel does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key signup, OpenAPI specification, or webhook documentation. The only Brightwheel API activity that is publicly acknowledged is bespoke, contract-scoped work built for individual government partners - for example a private API implemented to submit attendance and subsidy data to Iowa's childcare subsidy data system - and inbound integrations where Brightwheel pushes data into third-party products (e.g. staff timecards to Gusto for payroll). None of these expose a documented API surface that outside developers can build against. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Jar
providers.description: Jar is a Bengaluru-based fintech company operating India's first micro-savings app, enabling tens of millions of Indians to save in 24K digital gold from as little as ₹10. The app supports daily, weekly, monthly, and instant savings mechanisms, plus a round-up feature that automatically invests spare change from everyday transactions into 99.5%+ pure digital gold held in insured vaults. Founded in 2021 by Nishchay AG (CEO) and Misbah Ashraf (CPO) under Changejar Technologies Private Limited, Jar has grown to 50+ million registered users across 12,000+ Indian zip codes. The company recently vertically integrated its gold operations, moving away from a third-party distribution model to purchase, store, and manage gold directly. Jar partners with Brink's for global custody, ICICI Lombard for insurance, Vistra as independent trustee, and BDO as statutory auditor. Adjacent products include Nek, a direct-to-consumer gold and silver jewellery brand sold via shopnek.com. Jar reached profitability in 2025 after backing from Tiger Global, Arkam Ventures, Rainfall Ventures, Yes VC, and others at a $300M+ valuation, and is preparing for an IPO. There is no public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program — Jar is a B2C consumer mobile app distributed exclusively through Apple App Store and Google Play.

providers.name: Stessa
providers.description: Stessa is a financial reporting, accounting, and management platform for rental property owners and small-to-mid-size landlords, headquartered in San Francisco and operated as a brand of Roofstock alongside Mynd and RentPrep. The platform helps owners track unlimited properties and portfolios with automated bank and credit card feeds, transaction categorization, mileage tracking, receipt scanning, Schedule E-ready tax reporting, online rent collection, tenant screening through RentPrep, e-signature leasing with 50+ legal templates, maintenance request tracking, and property-specific Stessa Cash Management accounts with high-yield APY and FDIC insurance up to $3M per entity. Stessa is delivered as a web app and iOS/Android mobile apps with three tiers — Essentials (free), Manage, and Pro — and serves more than 350,000 landlords. Bank, credit card, and payment data flows in through aggregator partners (Plaid-style open banking) rather than a public Stessa API, and the only developer-facing GitHub presence is an org with a handful of forked Ruby and Vue.js utilities. There is no public Stessa REST API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no published webhooks; the Stessa community has open feature requests for a public API to pull reports and transactions, but none has shipped.

providers.name: Silo
providers.description: Silo is a cloud-based ERP platform built specifically for the fresh-produce supply chain, serving growers, packers, shippers, and distributors. The platform unifies produce operations across five modules - a diversified produce ERP, labor and asset management, payments and financial operations, EDI and traceability, and analytics and intelligence - to improve operational efficiency and financial visibility for small to midsize produce businesses. Silo is backed by a16z and Initialized Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Rational
providers.description: Rational (rational.to) is a Y Combinator (S26) company building AI employees, or "AI coworkers," for accounting and finance teams. Its AI agents onboard themselves to a firm, build a company "brain," and perform recurring accounting work — accounts payable, AR collections, bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, document collection, expense review, and month-end close — while keeping postings, payment release, and policy-sensitive decisions behind explicit human approval gates with an inspectable review history. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco by Jibril Moinuddin and Christ Xu, Rational targets accounting firms and finance teams facing a structural capacity and labor shortage. As an early-stage company it currently exposes a marketing and agent-discovery surface (llms.txt, ai-discovery.json, RFC 9116 security.txt) rather than a public developer API; this profile captures that surface and will be enriched as a developer platform ships.

providers.name: ReadSoft
providers.description: ReadSoft was a provider of intelligent automation and business process management solutions for accounts payable and other document-intensive processes. Acquired by Lexmark in 2014, the technology was rolled into Kofax and is now part of Tungsten Automation. ReadSoft no longer publishes a public developer-facing REST API; its capture and AP automation products are delivered as installed enterprise software with partner-only integration resources.

providers.name: Walter
providers.description: Walter is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI employee for the manufacturing back office. Founded in 2026 by Nikolas Keller (CEO) and Lukas Postulka (CTO), Walter logs into the enterprise systems a company already runs on — SAP, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Teams, Outlook and Gmail — the way a new hire would, and takes over manual paperwork: reading sales orders and purchase orders from emails and PDFs, capturing and validating the data, cross-checking it against the ERP, ordering from suppliers and catching pricing errors before they ship. It uses a purpose-built document-understanding model (rather than legacy template OCR) that supports 270+ languages and reaches 90%+ accuracy after minimal training, cutting an order that used to take 15 minutes down to about one. Walter requires no integration project and no rip-and-replace, operating the same screens the team already uses. It is an early-stage company with no public API, developer program, SDKs or documentation; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Involve.AI
providers.description: Involve.AI was an AI-driven customer intelligence platform for customer success and revenue teams. It unified data from CRM, support, product-usage, and billing systems to calculate customer health scores and power an Early Warning System that predicted churn and surfaced renewal and upsell opportunities, with a 9Factor model scoring qualitative and quantitative signals. Founded as a Techstars-backed startup, Involve.AI was renamed into Jeeva.ai rather than shut down — the GitHub organization login is still Involve-AI while its display name is now Jeeva AI, and involve.ai redirects to jeeva.ai. The product surface is retired: app.involve.ai no longer resolves, the involve.ai web origin answers Cloudflare 522 on every path but the root redirect, and api.involve.ai answers 530 with no origin behind it. Only the customer knowledge base at city.involve.ai survives. Involve.AI never published a developer API — it took admin-granted read access into a customer's source systems (Salesforce, Zendesk, Snowflake, Azure SQL, Pendo) through a no-code Data Mapping tool and returned health scores through configured write-backs into the system of action — so this profile documents company identity and a retirement record rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Octavewealth
providers.description: Octave Wealth (octavewealth.com) is a Y Combinator-backed company that, based on its name and branding, operates in the wealth and personal-finance space. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence sits behind Cloudflare and exposes no public developer API, documentation, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface; the only machine-discoverable artifact found was a published RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact. This profile records that verifiable state rather than a developer program.

providers.name: Rebaja Tus Cuentas
providers.description: Rebaja Tus Cuentas is a Latin American consumer fintech, backed by 500 Global, that helps individuals lower their debt and monthly loan payments. Through its website (rebajatuscuentas.com, redirecting to rtc.pe in Peru) it lets people compare refinancing and debt-consolidation offers from banks and lenders to reduce the cost of their existing loans, credit cards, and other obligations. It operates as a business-to-consumer marketing and lead-generation platform built on WordPress and fronted by Cloudflare, with a public blog and help center but no publicly documented developer program, API, or integration surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Atrium
providers.description: Atrium is a sales-effectiveness and sales-performance business intelligence platform for revenue teams. It continuously monitors sales KPIs to surface anomalies in rep and team performance, detects which behaviors and activities are driving (or dragging) output, and delivers AI-powered coaching recommendations to managers and reps. The product connects directly to Salesforce, HubSpot, data warehouses, and communication tools rather than exposing a public developer API. Founded in San Francisco by Jason Heidema (CEO) and Peter Kazanjy and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Bullpen Capital, and Electric Capital, Atrium was acquired by Fullcast in 2025 and is now offered as Fullcast Performance; atriumhq.com redirects to fullcast.com and only the customer application login at app.atriumhq.com remains on the Atrium domain.

providers.name: Causal
providers.description: Causal (causal.app) is a financial planning and business modeling platform for building spreadsheet-style models, forecasts, dashboards, and scenario analysis, aimed at finance teams and startups doing FP&A and extended planning and analysis (xP&A). Causal was acquired by Lucanet and its capabilities are now delivered as part of the Lucanet CFO Solution Platform; the marketing site redirects to Lucanet while existing customers sign in at my.causal.app. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or docs surface is currently published. Backed by Accel and Kindred Ventures.

providers.name: Z-Trip
providers.description: Z-Trip (在途商旅) is a Shanghai-based enterprise travel and expense management SaaS platform (a corporate travel management company, or TMC) serving medium and large Chinese enterprises. It unifies booking of flights, hotels, trains, car rentals, visas, insurance, and MICE events with automated expense reporting, budget and policy controls, monthly invoicing, and up to 45 days of advance funding. The platform integrates with corporate OA, ERP, cost-control, and HR systems and offers single sign-on, aggregating supplier inventory from 200+ airlines and millions of hotels for 1,700+ enterprise clients. Surfaced from the dcm-ventures portfolio; no public first-party API/developer platform is published, though third-party integration connectors and SSO exist.

providers.name: Corpay
providers.description: Corpay (formerly FLEETCOR) is a corporate payments company that provides commercial cards, accounts payable automation, cross-border payment solutions, fuel and fleet cards, and workforce travel management services. The company serves over 800,000 customers globally through its Corpay Complete spend management platform and ERP integrations. A public, openly accessible developer API portal could not be confirmed from the corporate website at the time of this review.

providers.name: Lendtable
providers.description: Lendtable was a US consumer fintech that extended a line of credit so individuals could afford to max out employer-sponsored benefits they would otherwise leave on the table — primarily the employer 401(k) match and Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP). In its own words: "Lendtable gives a line of credit to help individuals get their employer 401(k) match and ESPP." The product advanced cash against a user's paycheck contributions and took a share of the resulting gains, and was distributed direct-to-consumer and through employers via a Lendtable for Business offering, alongside an iOS app and a Zendesk help center. Lendtable was backed by Partech among others. The company now appears defunct: lendtable.com, the blog, and all product paths return HTTP 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED (probed 2026-07-19), the iOS App Store listing is delisted, and the last successful Internet Archive capture of the live site is 2024-12-06. DNS, Google Workspace mail (MX/SPF/DMARC) and the GitHub organization remain registered. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were ever published by this company.

providers.name: Levelset
providers.description: Levelset is a New Orleans-based construction payment software company that helps contractors, subcontractors, material suppliers, and equipment rental firms manage mechanics lien rights, preliminary notices, lien waivers, and payment compliance across all 50 U.S. states. The platform automates preliminary notice delivery, lien filing and release, conditional and unconditional lien waiver exchange, job and stakeholder research, and contractor payment-history monitoring, with deep state-by-state lien-law templates and deadline tracking. Founded as zlien in 2011 and rebranded to Levelset in 2018, the company was acquired by Procore Technologies for approximately $500 million in November 2021 and now operates as part of Procore's invoicing and payments suite. Customer-facing integrations exist with Procore, Sage, Viewpoint, Foundation, Acumatica, QuickBooks and other construction ERP and accounting platforms, but Levelset does not currently publish a self-serve public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal — integrations are delivered through partner-built connectors, the Procore Marketplace, and direct enterprise engagements with the Levelset integrations team. The Levelset GitHub organization is empty and developers.levelset.com / developer.levelset.com are not publicly reachable as of this profile date.

providers.name: CashDirector
providers.description: CashDirector is a fintech platform delivering AI-powered financial management for small businesses through a white-label, B2B2C partner model. It embeds banking and accounting automation directly into financial institutions' online banking platforms so banks can offer their SME clients a "beyond banking" daily digital business assistant. The platform automates invoicing, expense tracking, cash flow forecasting and receivables management, using AI and OCR to process financial documents automatically. It supports multibanking with minimal IT involvement and reports over 250,000 users across partnerships with six major European banks, positioning itself as Europe's first online accounting system with full banking integration. CashDirector is a Techstars portfolio company; it publishes no public developer portal or open API surface — integration is delivered privately to bank partners.

providers.name: Corpay (formerly FLEETCOR)
providers.description: Corpay is a global S&P 500 corporate payments company (NYSE: CPAY) that resulted from the March 2024 rebrand of FLEETCOR Technologies. The company serves more than 800,000 business clients across 200+ countries in 140+ currencies and processed approximately $400 billion in payments in 2024 with reported revenue of about $4.0B. Corpay operates across five product lines built largely through acquisition — Commercial Cards (including Corpay Mastercard), AP Automation (extended by the 2024 acquisition of Paymerang), Cross-Border Payments (built on the 2017 acquisition of Cambridge Global Payments and the 2025 acquisition of Alpha Group International), Fuel & Fleet Cards (the original FLEETCOR business plus the 2014 acquisition of Comdata), and Workforce Lodging & Travel. Despite this scale, Corpay does not operate a public developer portal — there is no developer.corpay.com, no public OpenAPI catalog, no public GitHub presence, and no self-service API key issuance. All integration surfaces (ERP connectors for NetSuite, Sage, Microsoft Dynamics, QuickBooks, Acumatica, CMiC, Deltek, Trimble; the former Cambridge cross-border payments API; AP-automation API hooks) are sales-led and gated behind enterprise contracts.

providers.name: Kema
providers.description: Kema (Kema FZ-LLC) is a UAE-based B2B fintech providing cash-flow and accounts-receivable tools for SMEs across the MENA region. Its platform combines invoice financing that advances up to 95% of invoice value, accounts-receivable automation with automated reminders, invoice tracking and reconciliation, and branded payment links delivered over email, WhatsApp and SMS that accept cards and wire transfers. Additional capabilities include practice-management tooling for accounting firms, recurring-payment automation, credit assessment and a real-time AR dashboard and analytics. Kema is backed by Speedinvest and reports 4,000+ companies transacting on its network.

providers.name: Tammwel
providers.description: Tammwel (Tamawal) is a Saudi Arabian digital financing intermediary that connects consumers with licensed financial institutions to compare and obtain Sharia-compliant financing. Its consumer platform and iOS/Android apps let users apply once and receive multiple offers across four products - personal loans, credit cards, auto financing, and mortgage financing (each up to 150,000 SAR) - emphasizing transparent pricing with no hidden fees. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tammwel publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and infrastructure security posture.

providers.name: Baan
providers.description: Baan (Baan Company N.V., originally The Baan Corporation) was a Dutch enterprise resource planning software vendor founded in 1978 in Barneveld, Netherlands by Jan Baan and later joined by his brother Paul Baan. Baan built one of the first genuinely component-based ERP suites, known for its Dynamic Enterprise Modeler (DEM), its Baan Tools 4GL development environment, and deep manufacturing and project-industry functionality. At its late-1990s peak Baan served roughly 3,000 customers and posted close to $700 million in revenue, making it one of the leading global ERP providers alongside SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft. Following accounting controversy and a collapse in its share price, Baan was acquired by the British engineering group Invensys in 2000, sold on to SSA Global Technologies in 2003, and absorbed into Infor Global Solutions when Infor acquired SSA in 2006. Baan no longer exists as an operating company or an independent brand: the product line lives on as Infor LN, and the baan.com and baan.nl domains now permanently redirect to the Infor LN product page. Consequently this profile carries no first-party API surface of its own — any modern programmatic access to the Baan lineage is delivered through Infor LN REST APIs and the Infor ION API gateway on Infor's developer platform. Baan Company is listed by Battery Ventures as an exited investment.

providers.name: Bluebook
providers.description: Bluebook is a Stockholm, Sweden based software company building AI agents for accounting firms, accountants, and CFOs. The platform automates accounting workflows — reconciliations, accruals, accounts payable and receivable, month-end close, reporting, and accounting research — with the stated goal of a "zero-day close", and integrates with the general ledgers firms already run on, notably QuickBooks and NetSuite. The product surface is organized around Background Agents, Checklists (tasks, delegation, human-in-the-loop approvals, month-end close), and an Assistant covering FP&A, flux analysis, and accounting research. Founded in 2024 by Philip Andersson (CEO), Jonathan Andersson (COO), and Filip Stål (CTO), Bluebook went through Y Combinator (Winter 2025) and raised a $3M pre-seed led by EQT Ventures with participation from Y Combinator and angel investors from Affirm, OpenAI, and ElevenLabs. Bluebook is a product company, not an API provider: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Vegafund
providers.description: Vegafund Inc was the company behind Roi (getroi.app), an AI-powered personal finance and investing app that delivered individually tailored insights, education, and guidance in real time. A 500 Global portfolio company, Roi was acquired by OpenAI in 2025 and wound down operations with a final day of service on October 15, 2025. The company published no public API or developer program, and getroi.app is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Zeen
providers.description: Zeen is an AI-powered autonomous personal finance platform — a money copilot that connects to your financial accounts and uses background AI agents to manage money on your behalf. Its features include an interactive AI financial copilot that answers questions in real time, Guard (loss prevention that avoids overdraft fees and cancels unused subscriptions), Grow (yield optimization that moves idle balances to higher-interest accounts), and Guide (spending insights). As of mid-2026 Zeen is in pre-launch with a public waitlist. Zeen is backed by Cowboy Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Inyad
providers.description: Inyad is an all-in-one business management and payments platform for small and medium businesses across Morocco, the Middle East, and Africa. Its mobile-first apps let merchants sell, get paid, and run their operations from one place — including a smart point-of-sale (POS Mahaal), automatic invoicing, an online store builder, employee attendance and payroll (Staff), a digital credit book (Konnash), in-store card terminals and terminal-free digital collection (Collect), professional business accounts, and money-transfer services. The company reports 250,000+ professionals on the platform and is backed by investors including Partech, Al Mada Ventures, CDG Invest, and FJ Labs. Inyad exposes an internal application backend (api.inyad.com) but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Nqoodlet
providers.description: Nqoodlet is a Saudi Arabia-based (Riyadh) corporate spend and expense management platform for businesses from SMEs to enterprises. It lets teams issue unlimited virtual and physical company cards, track every transaction in real time, manage and control cards from a single dashboard, and pay globally in local currency without conversion fees. Over 600 companies use Nqoodlet to streamline expense management, eliminate paperwork, and gain clearer visibility into company spending. It is backed by 500 Global. Nqoodlet does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures the company's public web identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Getground
providers.description: GetGround is a London-based property investment platform that lets UK and international buy-to-let investors set up and run their rental businesses through a limited company. The all-in-one platform handles limited company formation, business bank accounts, accounting and tax filing (including Making Tax Digital), bookkeeping, buy-to-let mortgages, landlord insurance, tenant finding, and sourcing of investment properties. GetGround is backed by QED Investors and offers subscription tiers and launch packs for landlords managing single or multiple rental properties.

providers.name: Apla, Inc.
providers.description: Apla, Inc. (aplahub.com) was an AI-based accounting and bookkeeping platform based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2023. Aplá targeted early-stage startups and accountants working in QuickBooks Online, offering automated expense categorization, transaction and expense management, bookkeeping, and financial reporting, and shipped a "Vendor Search" Chrome extension that retrieved vendor details inside QuickBooks Online. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive: the aplahub.com origin is unreachable (HTTP 522/525 behind Cloudflare) and third-party trackers list it as deadpooled. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface could be found; the only developer-facing artifact located was the QuickBooks Online Chrome extension.

providers.name: BankOns
providers.description: BankOns was a San Mateo, California mobile savings startup founded in the summer of 2010 by Joshua Greenough, a former VP of Operations at PowerReviews. Launched in May 2011, the app connected a user's bank transaction history to their location, analyzing spending habits to surface the nearby merchant deals and rewards best suited to them, drawing on Foursquare and other local deals data. The name was a contraction of "bank" and "coupons". BankOns was seed funded by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) plus a friends-and-family round. In May 2012 Capital One acquired select BankOns software through a limited asset purchase agreement, and several team members including Greenough joined Capital One Labs. The product was wound down and the company no longer operates a consumer service or a developer platform. The bankons.com domain resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander with no content, and no API, documentation, SDK, or developer surface exists.

providers.name: BillGuard
providers.description: BillGuard was a consumer personal-finance and transaction-security company whose mobile app scanned bank and credit-card transactions for hidden fees, billing errors, grey charges, and fraud, and let users flag or dispute suspicious charges. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company was acquired by Prosper Marketplace in 2015 and folded into the Prosper Daily app; billguard.com now 301-redirects to prosper.com and no independent BillGuard developer, API, or documentation surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no live API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI)
providers.description: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI) is a top-25 nationally ranked accounting and advisory firm headquartered in Alabama, operating 70+ locations across 13 states plus Mexico. The firm delivers audit and attest, tax, and advisory services (cybersecurity, fraud and forensics, valuations, and transaction advisory) to more than 18 industries, alongside value add-on subsidiaries including CRI Advanced Analytics, CRI CFO Hub, and CRI M&A Advisors, and is a member of PrimeGlobal. It was surfaced via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched here; note that criadv.com is a professional-services accounting firm, not a Bessemer-backed fintech startup, so the portfolio-lead tagging is a domain false-positive. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: Ciridae
providers.description: Ciridae is building an AI-native operating system for services businesses — the industrial, construction, and field-service companies that make up the real economy. Its platform replaces fragmented ERPs and spreadsheets with a unified system that automates core business operations across project management, financials, CRM, accounts payable and receivable, and reporting, while keeping humans in the loop to oversee AI decisions. Modules span AI-generated field workforce scheduling, vendor onboarding and compliance, automated payment workflows, and customer order expediting, typically deployed in a two-to-four-week implementation with embedded engineers. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, Ciridae is backed by Accel. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Cleanwise
providers.description: Cleanwise (Cleanwise, Inc.) is a Jan/San procurement management company serving multi-location national and regional businesses. The company applies janitorial supply category knowledge and custom procurement management systems to help customers manage, measure, and control their janitorial and sanitation spend. Cleanwise describes itself as technology-enabled and customer-driven, combining in-house procurement systems, industry expertise, and supplier partnerships to deliver product efficiencies and standardized best practices across distributed facility footprints. Its published customer examples include the US Postal Service, JCPenney, and Best Buy, with claimed first-year savings of 10-20% of total Jan/San spend. Insight Partners has listed Cleanwise in its portfolio since 2022. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API artifact has been found for Cleanwise; the company operates as a procurement services provider rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Coinbooks
providers.description: Coinbooks is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Consona
providers.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.

providers.name: Corio, Inc.
providers.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Customer Portals
providers.description: Customer Portals is the topic dedicated to the architecture, APIs, schemas, and reference designs behind self-service customer portals. A customer portal is a secure web or mobile experience where authenticated customers can manage their profile, view orders and invoices, pay bills, submit and track support tickets, download documents, manage notification preferences, and access account-specific resources. Modern customer portals are typically composed of multiple back-end APIs - authentication and identity, profile and preference management, billing and invoicing, support and ticketing, notifications, and document delivery - surfaced through a single front-end shell. This repository tracks the vendors, patterns, and standards that make customer portals reliable, accessible, and API-driven.

providers.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service
providers.description: The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) is the agency within the Department of Defense responsible for paying members of the U.S. military, DoD civilian employees, contractors, and annuitants, as well as providing finance and accounting services to DoD components and other federal agencies. DFAS exposes member-facing self-service portals such as myPay but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Fi Money
providers.description: Fi Money is a Bengaluru, India based money-management application and consumer fintech operated by Epifi Technologies, founded in 2019 by ex-Google Pay (Tez) executives Sujith Narayanan and Sumit Gwalani together with Neeraj Bhope and Prasanna Ranganathan. Fi is not a chartered bank; it delivers a millennial-focused mobile experience layered on top of partner RBI-licensed Federal Bank, providing zero-balance digital savings accounts, a Visa debit card, deposits, mutual funds, Indian and US stocks, EPF tracking, credit cards, personal loans, jump-style automated savings rules ("FIT Rules"), and an AI-powered money assistant. Fi has raised roughly US$169M across multiple rounds from investors including Sequoia Capital India (Peak XV), Ribbit Capital, Temasek, Alpha Wave, and B Capital, and serves Indian retail consumers via iOS and Android apps. There is no classic public REST developer API or partner banking-as-a-service surface; Fi's only developer-facing interface is the Fi MCP (Model Context Protocol) server — a JSON-RPC streaming endpoint at https://mcp.fi.money:8080/mcp/stream that lets users connect their own Fi account to LLM clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini, ChatGPT) and call read-only tools such as fetch_net_worth, fetch_credit_report, fetch_epf_details, fetch_bank_transactions, fetch_mf_transactions, and fetch_stock_transactions to expose their net worth, holdings, EPF balance, credit report, and transactions to AI assistants. A hackathon-friendly mock server (epiFi/fi-mcp-dev, Go) and developer documentation (epiFi/mcp-docs) are published publicly on GitHub.

providers.name: Finmark
providers.description: Finmark was a financial planning, modeling, and forecasting SaaS platform for startups and small businesses, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, letting founders build budgets, cash-flow runway, hiring plans, and scenario models without spreadsheets. It was acquired by BILL (bill.com) and wound down as a standalone product: as of this enrichment pass finmark.com and www.finmark.com return a 301 permanent redirect to https://www.bill.com/. There is no longer an independent Finmark developer portal, API, documentation, pricing, or status page to enrich; the domain-security probe below reflects the residual finmark.com DNS/TLS surface only.

providers.name: Finnomena
providers.description: Finnomena is a Thailand-based wealth-technology and investment platform, headquartered in Bangkok, that lets retail investors research, buy, hold, and rebalance mutual funds and other investment products through a single mobile and web application. The platform combines a robo-advisory experience and model portfolios with an active investment community and a large body of Thai-language market education and analysis content. Finnomena Funds operates as a licensed investment intermediary, and the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Finnomena publishes a consumer-facing WordPress marketing site and a mobile app but no public developer program, API, or OpenAPI surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Fluidly
providers.description: Fluidly was a London-based intelligent cashflow forecasting fintech founded in 2016 by Caroline Plumb, providing SME cash-flow prediction, scenario planning, and working-capital tools used by roughly 1,300 UK accountancy firms. OakNorth Bank acquired Fluidly in December 2021 and folded the product into its Credit Intelligence Suite; the independent Fluidly brand has since been retired and fluidly.com now redirects to OakNorth's partnerships page. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record — no independent Fluidly developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains.

providers.name: Folhamatic
providers.description: Folhamatic (IOB Folhamatic Group) is a Brazilian developer of integrated accounting, payroll, and fiscal/tax software for accounting firms and businesses, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Americana, Sao Paulo. Its product line includes Folhamatic Payroll for personnel management and electronic files, Electronic Point Control for time-clock management, the Folhamatic Accounting system for management reporting, and Folhamatic Written Tax for tax departments. At acquisition it served more than 11,000 companies with 500-plus employees. Folhamatic was acquired by the UK's Sage Group in June 2012 and now operates as part of Sage in Brazil. The company publishes no first-party public developer API, and the historic folhamatic.com.br domain no longer serves a live site.

providers.name: Jetway
providers.description: Jetway was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead pointing at nextravel.com. Enrichment found that nextravel.com now 301-redirects to TravelPerk (www.travelperk.com), which itself redirects to www.perk.com, an all-in-one business travel and expense-management platform. NexTravel was a US corporate-travel startup acquired by TravelPerk; it no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery documents at nextravel.com (every probed path soft-404s to the Perk marketing site). This profile is retained as an acquired/redirected lead with no independent developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: LumaTax
providers.description: LumaTax is a US and Canadian sales tax automation platform that helps businesses automate sales tax filings, manage nexus exposure, and streamline remittance across multiple state and federal jurisdictions. The product imports transaction data from sources such as Amazon, Stripe, Shopify, and Excel, validates that data and assigns correct tax jurisdictions, generates categorized return summaries, files returns automatically, and stores past filings for audit preparation. Originally an independent Seattle fintech backed by Cowboy Ventures, LumaTax was acquired and is now offered as a product line under Taxually alongside CrossTax, EcoTax, and OneTax. As of enrichment it exposes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Mamut
providers.description: Mamut was a Norwegian business software company (Mamut ASA / Mamut AS) that provided accounting, ERP, CRM, e-commerce and online-presence software to small and medium-sized businesses across the Nordics and parts of Europe. It was acquired by Visma in 2011 and the Mamut product line has since been absorbed into the Visma family of business software. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the mamut.com web server is unreachable (both HTTP and HTTPS time out) and there is no reachable public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface under the Mamut brand; enrichment therefore captured only what could be probed from DNS/TLS. Sector: enterprise.

providers.name: Mint
providers.description: Mint was a personal finance, budgeting, and money-management product originally built by Aaron Patzer and backed by First Round Capital and Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC) before its 2009 acquisition by Intuit. Intuit shut the standalone Mint service down and reimagined its features (transaction review, spending tracking, net-worth monitoring, account linking across 17,000+ financial institutions) inside Credit Karma. Mint exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile is retained as a network company record. Sector: fintech.

providers.name: OutlookSoft
providers.description: OutlookSoft was a corporate performance management (CPM) software company providing budgeting, planning, consolidation, forecasting, and financial reporting software. Originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, enrichment confirmed OutlookSoft was acquired by SAP in 2007 and folded into SAP Business Planning and Consolidation (SAP BPC). The outlooksoft.com domain is now controlled by SAP (SAP nameservers) and serves no live site, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no independent API to enrich.

providers.name: Portal Software
providers.description: Portal Software was an Accel-backed billing and revenue-management software company whose portal.com domain now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to Oracle WebCenter Portal, indicating the business and its assets have been absorbed into Oracle. It was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, but the enrichment pass finds no independent developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or published security program under portal.com — the domain serves only an Oracle marketing redirect, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich beyond the domain-level TLS/DNS security probe.

providers.name: Prelay
providers.description: Prelay was a deal collaboration ("team selling") platform that helped B2B revenue teams coordinate the internal stakeholders behind complex enterprise deals — sales engineers, legal, deal desk, finance, and leadership — inside a shared workspace that plugged into the CRM. Founded 2019 in San Francisco (Y Combinator W20), it was a SaaS application aimed at sales and revenue operations, not a developer/API product. The company has since ceased operations: Y Combinator lists Prelay as Inactive, Crunchbase records it as permanently closed, the github.com/prelay organization was archived on 2025-10-16 with zero public repositories, and as of 2026-08-14 prelay.com and www.prelay.com no longer complete a TLS handshake (the Webflow certificate has been deprovisioned) while app.prelay.com answers 404 for every path. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server or agent card ever existed, and no api./docs./developers. subdomain resolves. Prelay was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PwC
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms providing audit and assurance, tax, and management consulting services globally. PwC operates as a network of member firms across approximately 150 countries with hundreds of thousands of professionals. Service lines include audit, deals and transactions, tax compliance and advisory, risk assurance, cybersecurity and privacy, ESG and sustainability assurance, workforce transformation, and digital/technology consulting (cloud, data, AI, ERP). PwC publishes thought-leadership content and operates client portals for engagement delivery and document exchange, but it does not publish a public developer API or open partner integration portal at the corporate level - client connectivity is bilateral and project-scoped rather than offered as a self-serve API product.

providers.name: Rocketrip
providers.description: Rocketrip was a New York City corporate travel cost-savings platform that gave business travelers a personalized budget (a "Price to Beat") and rewarded employees who booked flights, hotels, and rail below it, sharing the savings between the traveler and the company. It was backed by Canaan Partners, GV, Bessemer, and Y Combinator. As of this enrichment pass the rocketrip.com and www.rocketrip.com domains 301-redirect to Tabhi (tabhi.ai / tabhi.com), the developer, docs, and api subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI could be found — the standalone Rocketrip product and its API surface appear to have been retired or folded into Tabhi.

providers.name: Soff
providers.description: Soff is an AI-powered quoting platform for U.S. distributors that turns inbound RFQs into won deals. It automatically captures requests for quotes from email, generates instant quotes and PDFs, tracks quote performance (won vs. lost), logs activity into ERP/CRM systems, and analyzes customer behavior and lost-deal reasons. Backed by Y Combinator (S24) and General Catalyst, based in San Francisco, and SOC 2 Type II certified. As of this enrichment pass Soff publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Spenny
providers.description: Spenny is an Indian personal-finance and micro-investing app that works like a digital piggy bank, rounding up everyday spending on cards, UPI, and netbanking and automatically investing the spare change. Users can put round-ups and lump sums (from as little as Rs. 10) into digital gold and curated mutual fund baskets, with no lock-ins and anytime withdrawals. Spenny is a consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Spiff
providers.description: Spiff was a sales commission and incentive compensation management (ICM) platform that automated commission calculations, gave sales reps real-time earnings visibility, and streamlined finance-side reconciliation for revenue teams. Founded in Utah and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Norwest Venture Partners, Spiff was acquired by Salesforce in 2024 and folded into Sales Cloud as "Salesforce Spiff" / Incentive Compensation Management. As of this profile the standalone spiff.com and app.spiff.com properties redirect to salesforce.com, and no independent Spiff public API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI surface remains discoverable — its capabilities are now delivered through the Salesforce platform.

providers.name: Tactic
providers.description: Tactic was a cryptocurrency and digital-asset accounting platform founded in 2021 in New York and backed by Lux Capital. Its product aggregated on-chain activity and exchange/custody data (Coinbase and others) into a unified treasury view and crypto sub-ledger, automatically categorizing transactions, calculating USD gain/loss and taxable events, and reconciling the crypto sub-ledger to traditional accounting software such as QuickBooks. Tactic launched from stealth in 2022 (originally on choosetactic.com, later the exact-match tactic.com) and raised roughly $13.6M before being acquired by TaxBit in January 2023 to augment TaxBit's digital-asset accounting suite. The standalone product, developer portal, and API surface have been retired; the tactic.com domain is now listed for sale and no independent developer surface remains.

providers.name: taptrip.co
providers.description: TapTrip (taptrip.co) was a UK-based self-serve business travel and expense booking platform for SMEs, founded in 2018 in Manchester and part of the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars. It let smaller businesses book and manage flights, hotels, rail, and ground transportation without a travel management company. TapTrip was acquired by TripStax in July 2022 and folded into the TripStax platform as an SME online-booking module for travel management companies; the standalone brand was absorbed. As of this enrichment pass the taptrip.co domain no longer hosts an active product — it resolves to a ParkingCrew domain-parking service and the TLS endpoint does not respond. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the standalone company.

providers.name: Tidemark
providers.description: Tidemark is enterprise financial and operational planning software for continuous, extended, and driver-based planning. It provides scenario ("what-if") modeling, workflow and approvals, and real-time data integration across 140+ ERP and EPM systems for budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning. Founded as a venture-backed cloud analytics and enterprise performance management (EPM) company and counted among the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio, Tidemark was later acquired and is now offered as a product within the insightsoftware family. It has no publicly documented API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through pre-built ERP/EPM connectors rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: TrustAI
providers.description: TrustAI (trytrust.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Summer 2026 company founded in 2026 by Hannah Chung and Medha Venkatapathy that provides continuous compliance, governance, and risk assessment for AI agents operating on sensitive enterprise systems, with an initial focus on ERP agents such as SAP Joule. It maps what every agent can reach, then runs evaluations across six domains - data privacy, hallucinations and grounding, permission compliance, robustness at scale, accountability, and security - including adversarial pentests and prompt-injection red-teaming, and maps every risk to controls like SOX, ITGC, ISO 27001, GxP, and the EU AI Act for audit-ready reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, docs, or SDKs. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: United Capital
providers.description: United Capital (United Capital Financial Advisers / United Capital Financial Partners) was a US wealth counseling and financial life management firm founded in 2005, known for its FinLife CX white-label advisor technology platform. Bessemer Venture Partners partnered with the company in 2009. At acquisition it managed roughly $25 billion for 22,000 clients through 220+ advisors in over 90 offices. Goldman Sachs acquired United Capital in May 2019 for $750 million in cash, rebranding it Goldman Sachs Personal Financial Management, which Creative Planning acquired in 2023. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API or developer surface; its historic domain unitedcp.com now returns HTTP 404.

providers.name: whatiseven
providers.description: whatiseven (Even, formerly Even Responsible Finance) was an earned-wage-access and personal-finance fintech that let workers access a portion of their pay before payday, budget with "okay to spend" guidance, and automatically save. Backed by Slow Ventures, Even was acquired by One (Walmart's fintech venture, now OnePay) and folded into the OnePay @Work earned-wage-access product ("Instapay"). The whatiseven.com domain now redirects through even.com to onepay.com/atwork. Even operates no independent public developer platform, API, or documentation, and the acquirer OnePay publishes no public API surface either. This profile is retained as a network record of the company and its acquisition.

providers.name: WISECRICKET HOLDING KY
providers.description: WiseCricket (WISECRICKET HOLDING KY) offers AI-powered fiscal and accounting audit software for businesses ("Software de Auditoria Fiscal y Contable con IA para Empresas"). The Spanish-language platform applies artificial intelligence to tax and accounting compliance, helping companies automate financial and tax audits and surface issues. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found a marketing landing page but no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Zeitgold
providers.description: Zeitgold was a Berlin-based fintech that automated bookkeeping, invoice and receipt processing, payments, and financial administration for small and medium-sized businesses, blending software with human back-office review. It was backed by Battery Ventures and other investors and was acquired by Deel in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public developer surface: zeitgold.com does not respond on HTTP or HTTPS, and zeitgold.de resolves to a parked/reserved domain page. No public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable artifact could be discovered, so this profile remains an identity-only record.

providers.name: Rocket Companies
providers.description: Rocket Companies is a Detroit-based financial services firm that provides digital solutions for homeownership and personal finance. Its portfolio includes Rocket Mortgage for home loans, Rocket Homes for real estate search, and Rocket Money for personal finance management. Rocket Companies does not publish a public corporate developer API portal at the holding-company level.

providers.name: Tinvio
providers.description: Tinvio is a Singapore-based B2B commerce and payments SaaS that helped merchants and their suppliers manage ordering, invoicing, and business payments across Southeast Asia. The company was backed by Partech. As of 2026 Tinvio has been integrated into Jaz (jaz.ai), an AI-powered accounting platform for modern businesses, and now operates as a feature within Jaz rather than as a standalone product; tinvio.com redirects to the Jaz landing page. Tinvio does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDK, CLI, or OpenAPI definition, so this profile captures the company identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network rather than an API surface.

providers.name: APP Group  Ness Czechia
providers.description: APP Group (renamed Ness Czechia after its acquisition by Ness Digital Engineering) is an enterprise IT services and systems-integration company headquartered in Prague, Czech Republic, with offices in Brno and Ostrava. Operating today as Ness Czech s.r.o., it is one of the most significant SAP providers (SAP Gold Partner) in the Czech Republic and the wider CEE region, delivering system integration, ERP and SAP S/4HANA implementation, business intelligence, data analytics, eGovernment / eHealth registers, core banking, pricing and billing, CRM and portals, IoT, and digital-platform engineering to large enterprises and the public sector. It is not a public API provider: it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a self-serve API program. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: Monto
providers.description: Monto is a B2B payments platform that automates supplier-side billing and collection across customer accounts-payable (AP) portals. It connects suppliers to 500+ AP platforms, using AI to deliver and format invoices per portal, verify data, match invoices to purchase orders, track invoice and payment status in real time, and retrieve remittance details end to end. Integrations include a NetSuite bundle (Send to Monto), generic ERP integration, and email or web upload. Monto reports $10B+ collected across 67 countries. The company is SOC 2 Type II audited. Monto is backed by Scale Venture Partners. This profile has no public developer API or documentation surface as of enrichment.

providers.name: Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board
providers.description: The Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board (FASAB) is an independent organization responsible for establishing accounting standards for the federal government. FASAB strives to improve the quality and consistency of financial reporting within federal agencies, ultimately ensuring transparency and accountability in government financial operations.

providers.name: BlueTarp Financial
providers.description: BlueTarp Financial is a B2B trade-credit and accounts-receivable financing company, founded in Portland, Maine, that lets suppliers, distributors, and building-materials dealers extend revolving or net-terms credit to their business customers while BlueTarp pays the supplier upfront and assumes the credit risk and collections. Its SmartView portal manages the purchase-to-payment lifecycle: credit decisioning, invoicing, billing, and receivables. BlueTarp was acquired and is now operated as Capital One Trade Credit; its independent site (bluetarp.com) redirects to capitalone.com/trade-credit/bluetarp. BlueTarp publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Nook
providers.description: Nook is an accounts payable (AP) automation platform for businesses, combining invoice management with automated payment workflows to reduce manual data entry, cut errors, and give finance teams clearer visibility over outgoings. Founded in the UK and backed by Speedinvest as an early investor, Nook was acquired by payments infrastructure provider Modulr; its product now operates as "Modulr AP" and its former standalone site at nook.io presents the combined Modulr AP offering. Nook does not publish an independent public developer platform, API reference, or SDKs — the payment rails are provided through Modulr's platform — so this profile is maintained as a company record rather than an API-bearing provider.

providers.name: AssetVault
providers.description: AssetVault is a London-based consumer fintech platform that helps individuals and families catalogue, protect, and grow their valuable assets in one secure digital vault. It spans physical items (homes, vehicles, jewelry), digital assets (passwords, investment portfolios), and financial holdings, layering on digital estate planning (eWill), insurance claims support, analytics, and concierge services. The platform emphasizes bank-grade security with encrypted transmission, two-factor authentication, and biometric access, and is available as an App Store, Google Play, and web app. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface is published yet.

providers.name: PolicyPal
providers.description: PolicyPal is a Singapore-based InsurTech and digital insurance broker founded in 2016 by Val Yap that lets consumers buy, understand, and organize their insurance policies from a mobile app using OCR and rule-based policy digitization. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), PayPal Incubation, and Startupbootcamp FinTech, it was the first startup to graduate from the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox and was acquired by Hong Kong's AMTD Digital in 2020. As of 2025 PolicyPal Pte. Ltd. and its entities (including PolicyPal Tech Pte. Ltd., Baoxianbaobao Pte. Ltd. and the ValueChampion brand) are no longer regulated by MAS, and the consumer website is undergoing a revamp. PolicyPal does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Blue Studios
providers.description: Blue Studios Labs is a family-focused technology company operating under the tagline "Where Families Flourish." It builds consumer digital products that help couples and families explore, learn, and grow together. Its portfolio includes Wallio, a shared financial-management app for couples and families; Blue Studios EDU, an entertainment-based educational streaming service; and Blue Studios Entertainment, a media-production studio creating family-oriented narratives and content. The company reports more than 400 million digital views, 350,000 game plays, and 4,000+ classes delivered. Blue Studios is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: liangzizhige
providers.description: liangzizhige.com is the corporate domain of QuantaSing Group Limited (NASDAQ QSG), a China-based online learning company listed by Qiming Venture Partners in its technology portfolio as a provider of personal finance online courses. As of this enrichment pass the liangzizhige.com domain is registered through Alibaba Cloud but publishes no A record and serves no website; the only live company surface found is the investor-relations site, which redirects to ir.quantasing.com. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, public GitHub organization, or published client libraries were found for this company.

providers.name: Mujer Financiera
providers.description: Mujer Financiera is a Latin American financial-education platform founded in 2018 in Buenos Aires, Argentina by Sabrina Castelli, focused on closing the gender gap in financial inclusion. It delivers courses, packs, and multi-month programs (MF Platinum) on budgeting, saving, and investing, alongside a mobile app for tracking personal finances, a supportive community, a newsletter, and corporate financial-education services for companies. The platform reports hundreds of thousands of women served across 12+ countries and is backed by 500 Global. It is a business-to-consumer fintech/edtech offering and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Peddlr
providers.description: Peddlr is a Philippine fintech startup offering free mobile point-of-sale (POS) and bookkeeping software for Filipino micro, small, and medium businesses (MSMEs). Its app spans sales recording, offline inventory management, expense tracking, cash and credit ledgers, bills payment, QRPH, e-loading and gaming pins, a payment ledger, and accounting reports, with over two million downloads across 1,400+ cities and municipalities. Peddlr is registered with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas as an Operator of Payment Systems. The company publishes no public developer program or API at this time; this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bankiom
providers.description: Bankiom is a Dubai-based consumer fintech founded in 2018 by Danny Abla. It began as a UAE/GCC lifestyle neobank offering free virtual prepaid Mastercard cards, multi-bank account aggregation, spending insights, and instant peer transfers through a mobile app across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman. Bankiom has since repositioned as an autonomous AI money agent that securely connects to a user's bank, audits roughly 90 days of transactions, and surfaces the fees, interest, unused rewards, forgotten subscriptions, and expiring loyalty points a customer should not be paying, charging only a capped share of verified savings. It is a consumer-facing application and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Bento
providers.description: Bento (Bento Technologies, Inc., dba Bento for Business) was a Chicago- and San Francisco-based small-business fintech that provided card-based payment and expense management for small and mid-size businesses: virtual and physical employee and utility cards, per-card spend controls and category restrictions, real-time spend tracking, and accounting integrations. Bento published a public REST API at api.bentoforbusiness.com (documented at apidocs.bentoforbusiness.com) for issuing employee and utility virtual cards, retrieving card numbers, activating and customizing billing addresses, and reading card transactions, plus outbound webhooks for card transaction completed and declined events; API access was granted per account via an Access Key and Secret Key issued by api-support@bentoforbusiness.com. Bento raised a $2.5M seed round led by Anthemis Group in 2015, with Blumberg Capital, LionBird, Pivot Investment Partners, Edison Partners and Espresso Capital also investing. U.S. Bank agreed to acquire Bento Technologies on August 11, 2021 and closed the acquisition on August 31, 2021, folding the product into U.S. Bank's small-business spend management offering. The Bento card program was then wound down: card reloads stopped April 30, 2024 and all card program services were discontinued June 25, 2024, with customers directed to alternative providers. The developer surface is retired — apidocs.bentoforbusiness.com and api.bentoforbusiness.com no longer resolve in DNS, and bentoforbusiness.com now redirects to U.S. Bank. This profile is retained as a historical record of a former API provider; there is no live API to consume.

providers.name: CakeHealth
providers.description: CakeHealth (Cake Health) was a San Francisco health-insurance management startup founded in 2011 by Rebecca Woodcock, pitched as "Mint for health insurance." Users linked their insurer logins so the service could aggregate health plans, claims, bills, deductibles, and out-of-pocket spending into a single consumer dashboard. It launched as a TechCrunch Disrupt finalist and was backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kima Ventures. Inbox Health acquired the company for its medical-bill tracking technology in April 2016, after which the product was shut down.
