The company is defunct and no longer operates an API or developer surface; the cakehealth.com domain has since been repurposed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party site.

providers.name: Janney Montgomery Scott
providers.description: Janney Montgomery Scott LLC is a full-service wealth management, financial services, and investment banking firm headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and continuously operating since 1832. A wholly owned subsidiary of The Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company, Janney serves individual investors, corporations, and municipalities through more than 100 branch offices across the United States, with over 900 financial advisors managing in excess of $167 billion in client assets under advisement. The firm provides client account access through the MyJanney online portal and iOS/Android mobile apps, but does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or external developer portal.

providers.name: payflows
providers.description: Payflows is an AI-native financial operations platform that unifies procurement, treasury, and accounting into one agentic workspace for finance teams. Its product suites span Apollo (procurement from purchase request to receipt), Vera (vendor and contract management), Athena (accounting and AP automation from AP to tax reporting), and Metis (treasury from payment to bank reconciliation), with spend analytics, cashflow forecasting, global payments, and risk management. Payflows integrates with major ERP, banking, payment, and expense systems. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Habitto
providers.description: Habitto is a Tokyo-based fintech company building a mobile financial wellness app for the Japanese market under the banner お金の新習慣 ("new money habits"). The app pairs a high-yield savings account and a cashback debit card with access to human financial advisors who help users save, grow, and protect their money. Habitto is backed by the fintech-focused venture investors Anthemis and QED Investors. This API Evangelist profile has been enriched with company identity, website link properties, and a domain-security probe; Habitto is a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: InstaPaisa
providers.description: InstaPaisa was an India-based personal-finance and lending fintech surfaced as a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct or absorbed — its domain instapaisa.com resolves (Amazon CloudFront) but redirects to InCred Finance (incred.com), an Indian digital lending / NBFC platform, indicating an acquisition or wind-down. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found for InstaPaisa, so no API artifacts could be harvested or derived; only live domain-security signals for instapaisa.com were probed.

providers.name: NEO Success
providers.description: NEO Success (operating as NEO Money) was a Bangkok, Thailand personal-finance and money-management fintech founded in 2019 by Punnamas Vichitkulwongsa and backed by 500 Global. It built a consumer platform aimed at helping users reach financial freedom and manage their money. As of this enrichment pass the company is out of business (per PitchBook) and its domain neomoney.com resolves to a parked domain-for-sale page (Afternic/GoDaddy) — there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Okcredit
providers.description: OkCredit is a mobile digital ledger (bahi khata) application for small business owners and merchants across India, letting shopkeepers record credit and payment transactions digitally, send automated collection reminders over SMS and WhatsApp, and share account statements with customers. The consumer-facing Android and iOS apps replace the traditional paper udhaar ledger; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Open
providers.description: Open (Open Financial Technologies) operates at open.money as an India-based fintech offering a connected digital business banking platform for SMEs and startups. It pairs a business current account with invoicing, payments, automated accounting, expense management and payroll, letting founders run their banking and finance operations from a single dashboard. Open is a Speedinvest portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company website is protected by Cloudflare and no public OpenAPI could be harvested during enrichment.

providers.name: Qashio Holding Company Limited
providers.description: Qashio is a United Arab Emirates-based financial technology company providing corporate spend management for businesses. Its platform offers unlimited smart corporate cards with advanced spending controls, rewards and cashback on transactions, and automated expense management, and it integrates with major ERP and accounting systems including Microsoft Dynamics 365, Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Xero, and Zoho. As of this enrichment pass Qashio publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and remains a company-level record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Spenmo
providers.description: Spenmo was a Singapore-based spend management platform for businesses, offering corporate Visa debit cards (physical and virtual), bill and invoice management with smart scanning, employee reimbursements and claims, and accounting integrations with Xero, NetSuite, QuickBooks and Jurnal. Operated by Digital Services SG Five Pte Ltd, it worked with MAS-licensed payment partners rather than providing regulated payment services directly. The company ceased operations on 14 August 2025 and permanently disabled customer access. No public API or developer program was ever published.

providers.name: WayPay
providers.description: WayPay was a cloud-based B2B payments and accounts-payable-automation fintech headquartered in Burlington, Ontario, Canada. Its platform let businesses pay any supplier by any method (EFT, cheque, credit card, wire) from a single dashboard, reconciling against accounting and ERP software to automate the accounts-payable workflow. Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) announced its acquisition of WayPay in July 2019, after which the independent brand was retired. As of this enrichment pass the domain waypay.ca resolves via DNS (behind Akamai, enterprise mail) but serves no public site (HTTP 503), and there is no reachable public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Illuminet
providers.description: Illuminet, located in Seattle, Washington, provides advanced intelligent network, database, and billing services to the telecommunications industry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass no live public web or API surface could be located (illuminet.com is a parked/for-sale domain, illuminet.io does not resolve, and the Insight Partners portfolio page carries no descriptive content), so this profile remains a company record with no developer or API artifacts.

providers.name: Clarity Money
providers.description: Clarity Money was a personal-finance and money-management mobile app founded in 2016 by Adam Dell (Oath Holdings / Dell family) that used data-driven analysis to help consumers track spending, cancel unwanted subscriptions, negotiate bills, move savings, and manage budgets. It was acquired by Goldman Sachs in 2018 and folded into the Marcus by Goldman Sachs consumer platform; the standalone Clarity Money app was subsequently discontinued. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. No public developer program, API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published, and the claritymoney.com domain no longer resolves to a live site (held by Goldman Sachs registrar CSC).

providers.name: Digit
providers.description: Digit was a consumer fintech company that built an automated personal-savings app: it analyzed a user's checking-account activity and quietly moved small, safe amounts into an FDIC-insured savings account, later expanding into automated investing and retirement (Digit Invest, Digit Retirement). Founded in 2013 in San Francisco by Ethan Bloch and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, Digit was acquired by Oportun in late 2021 and folded into Oportun's savings product. The standalone Digit brand is now retired: digit.co and hellodigit.com redirect to oportun.com/savings, and there is no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no active developer surface.

providers.name: Ivella
providers.description: Ivella was a consumer fintech company that built shared money-management and multi-account banking tools aimed at couples and households, backed by the fintech venture firm Anthemis. As of 2026 Ivella's products have been sunset and the team has joined EarnIn to continue building. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Anthemis portfolio-company lead; the enrichment pipeline found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface, and the company is no longer operating as an independent product.

providers.name: Long Game
providers.description: Long Game was a San Francisco fintech startup founded in 2015 by Lindsay Holden that used prize-linked savings and casual mobile gaming to help Gen-Z and millennial consumers build healthy financial habits and grow their savings. Backed by Obvious Ventures and others (raising over $20M in venture capital), Long Game was acquired by Truist Financial in May 2022 and folded into Truist Foundry, which relaunched the Long Game app in May 2023. It is a consumer mobile product with no public developer API surface, and the standalone longgame.co domain no longer resolves.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: 1sm
providers.description: 1sm was a New York City revenue-operations (RevOps) analytics startup founded in 2020 by James Weitzman, Chris Lonardo and Jordan Josloff. It raised a $375K pre-seed round announced in July 2020 while in the Techstars NYC 2020 accelerator class, and pitched itself as the first no-code RevOps analytics platform — integrating a company's existing sales and marketing tools into one unified view of buyer personas and ideal customer profiles, with forward-looking analytics predicting which messaging would drive clicks, meetings and closed deals. The product never advanced past a public beta waitlist and no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer program was ever shipped. As of September 2026 the company's former domain, 1sm.io, is registered to a third party — Nocode ltd of Paphos, Cyprus, the entity behind the Latenode automation platform — which republishes the archived July 2020 marketing page with injected affiliate copy and a "Contact the Domain Owner" footer, so that host is deliberately NOT wired as this company's Website pointer.
